62	# Every MASS_PRIORITY source except the trailing "assumed" default is a real
63	# measured/derived stellar mass.
64	_MEASURED_MASS_SOURCES = frozenset(MASS_PRIORITY[:-1])
65	
66	
67	# Below this scaled impact the smooth mNFW hot-halo column is extrapolated
68	# through the galaxy interior (not the CGM it was calibrated for) and the DM
69	# blows up; the "capped" intervening DM evaluates the column at this floor so a
70	# physically bounded value can be reported alongside the raw one.
71	INTERIOR_B_OVER_RVIR = 0.1
72	
73	# In this sample z_frb == 1.0 exactly is a placeholder for an unmeasured host
74	# redshift (Freya/Mahi/Johndoeii). Without a real z the Macquart <DM_cosmic> and
75	# the foreground/background split are meaningless, so those budgets are flagged
76	# and the cosmic/host terms are withheld rather than presented as if real.
77	PLACEHOLDER_Z = 1.0
78	
79	
80	def _is_placeholder_z(z: float) -> bool:
81	    return math.isfinite(_f(z)) and abs(float(z) - PLACEHOLDER_Z) < 1.0e-6
82	
83	
84	# Yamasaki & Totani 2020 ApJ 888,105 give a Galactic hot-halo DM ~43 pc/cm^3
85	# along typical sightlines; 40 is a round, deliberately conservative prior.
86	DM_MW_HALO = 40.0
87	
88	# Macquart+2020 Nature 581,391 / Deng & Zhang 2014: f_IGM ~ 0.84 of cosmic
89	# baryons are in the diffuse ionized IGM, with electron fraction chi_e ~ 7/8
90	# (H + singly-ionized He).
91	F_IGM = 0.84
92	CHI_E = 0.875
93	
94	
95	def _f(value: Any) -> float:
96	    """Coerce to float, returning NaN for missing/non-finite/sentinel values."""
97	    if value is None:
98	        return math.nan
99	    try:
100	        if np.ma.is_masked(value):
101	            return math.nan
102	    except TypeError:
103	        return math.nan
104	    try:
105	        out = float(value)
106	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
107	        return math.nan
108	    if not math.isfinite(out) or out <= -9990.0:
109	        return math.nan
110	    return out
111	
112	
113	def _truthy(value: Any) -> bool:
114	    if isinstance(value, str):
115	        return value.strip().lower() in {"true", "t", "1", "yes", "y"}
116	    try:
117	        if pd.isna(value):
118	            return False
119	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
120	        pass
121	    return bool(value)
122	
123	
124	def dm_cosmic_macquart(z: float, f_igm: float = F_IGM, chi_e: float = CHI_E) -> float:
125	    """Return the Macquart-relation mean cosmic/IGM DM at redshift z (pc/cm^3)."""
126	    z_value = float(z)
127	    if not math.isfinite(z_value) or z_value <= 0.0:
128	        return 0.0
129	
130	    from scipy.integrate import quad
131	
132	    # Deng & Zhang 2014 ApJ 783,L35 / Macquart+2020 Nature 581,391:
133	    # <DM_cosmic> = n_e,0 * (c/H0) * int_0^z (1+z')/E(z') dz', with the present
134	    # diffuse-IGM electron density n_e,0 = f_IGM chi_e Omega_b rho_crit,0 / m_p.
135	    n_e0 = (f_igm * chi_e * config.COSMO.Ob0 * config.COSMO.critical_density0 / const.m_p).to(u.cm**-3)
136	    hubble_dist = (const.c / config.COSMO.H0).to(u.pc)
137	    integral, _ = quad(
138	        lambda zp: (1.0 + zp) / math.sqrt(config.COSMO.Om0 * (1.0 + zp) ** 3 + config.COSMO.Ode0),
139	        0.0,
140	        z_value,
141	    )
142	    dm = (n_e0 * hubble_dist * integral).to(u.pc / u.cm**3).value
143	    return float(dm)
144	
145	
146	def parse_dm_obs(path_or_name: str | None) -> float | None:
147	    """Extract the observed DM from a burst filename/id.
148	
149	    The codetection bursts encode DM as the integer token after the Stokes flag,
150	    e.g. ``casey_chime_I_491_2085_32000b_cntr_bpc.npy`` -> 491 (DSA paths used a
151	    lowercase 'l' where Stokes 'I' was intended).
152	    """
153	    if not path_or_name:
154	        return None
155	    import re
156	
157	    stem = os.path.basename(str(path_or_name))
158	    m = re.search(r"_[IlL]_(\d+)_\d+_\d+b", stem)
159	    if not m:
160	        return None
161	    try:
162	        return float(m.group(1))
163	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
164	        return None
165	
166	
167	def read_measured_tau_ms(fit_json_path: str | None) -> float | None:
168	    """Return tau_1ghz (ms) from a scat_analysis fit_results.json, else None.
169	
170	    This is a raw parser: it returns the best-fit tau regardless of fit quality.
171	    Use read_tau_fit for the quality-gated value with uncertainties.
172	    """
173	    if not fit_json_path or not os.path.exists(fit_json_path):
174	        return None
175	    try:
176	        with open(fit_json_path) as fh:
177	            data = json.load(fh)
178	    except (OSError, ValueError):
179	        return None
180	    params = data.get("best_params", {}) if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
181	    tau = params.get("tau_1ghz")
182	    tau_f = _f(tau)
183	    if not math.isfinite(tau_f) or tau_f <= 0.0:
184	        return None
185	    return float(tau_f)
186	
187	
188	def read_tau_fit(fit_json_path: str | None) -> dict | None:
189	    """Read tau_1ghz with uncertainty and quality flag from a fit_results.json.
190	
191	    Prefers the posterior median + 16/84 from best_params_percentiles (the
192	    uncertainty-bearing summary); falls back to the best_params point estimate.
193	    Returns {tau, err_minus, err_plus, quality_flag, chi2_reduced} or None when no
194	    usable tau is present. The quality_flag is the pipeline's recalibrated
195	    chi2-driven gate (PASS/MARGINAL/FAIL); callers decide whether to ingest.
196	    """
197	    if not fit_json_path or not os.path.exists(fit_json_path):
198	        return None
199	    try:
200	        with open(fit_json_path) as fh:
201	            data = json.load(fh)
202	    except (OSError, ValueError):
203	        return None
204	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
205	        return None
206	
207	    err_minus = err_plus = math.nan
208	    tau_f = math.nan
209	    pct = data.get("best_params_percentiles")
210	    if isinstance(pct, dict) and isinstance(pct.get("tau_1ghz"), dict):
211	        tau_pct = pct["tau_1ghz"]
212	        tau_f = _f(tau_pct.get("median"))
213	        err_minus = _f(tau_pct.get("err_minus"))
214	        err_plus = _f(tau_pct.get("err_plus"))
215	    if not math.isfinite(tau_f):
216	        params = data.get("best_params", {}) or {}
217	        tau_f = _f(params.get("tau_1ghz"))
218	    if not math.isfinite(tau_f) or tau_f <= 0.0:
219	        return None
220	
221	    gof = data.get("goodness_of_fit", {}) or {}
222	    return {
223	        "tau": float(tau_f),
224	        "err_minus": err_minus,
225	        "err_plus": err_plus,
226	        "quality_flag": gof.get("quality_flag"),
227	        "chi2_reduced": _f(gof.get("chi2_reduced")),
228	    }
229	
230	
231	_PYGEDM: Any = None
232	
233	
234	def _load_pygedm() -> Any:
235	    """Import pygedm once, shimming the SciPy>=1.14 removal of integrate.simps."""
236	    global _PYGEDM
237	    if _PYGEDM is not None:
238	        return _PYGEDM
239	    try:
240	        import scipy.integrate as _si
241	
242	        if not hasattr(_si, "simps"):
243	            # pygedm.yt2020 still calls the removed scipy.integrate.simps; the
244	            # successor simpson made x keyword-only, so wrap rather than alias.
245	            _si.simps = lambda y, x=None, *a, **k: _si.simpson(y, x=x, *a, **k)
246	        import warnings
247	
248	        with warnings.catch_warnings():
249	            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
250	            import pygedm
251	        _PYGEDM = pygedm
252	    except Exception:
253	        _PYGEDM = False
254	    return _PYGEDM
255	
256	
257	def galactic_dm_tau(l_deg: float, b_deg: float, method: str = "ne2001", dist_pc: float = 30000.0):
258	    """Return (DM_NE2001, DM_YMW16, tau_MW_ms) toward Galactic (l, b).
259	
260	    Uses the compiled pygedm NE2001/YMW16 models (offline). Returns NaNs if
261	    pygedm is unavailable so callers degrade gracefully.
262	    """
263	    pg = _load_pygedm()
264	    if not pg:
265	        return (math.nan, math.nan, math.nan)
266	    import warnings
267	
268	    with warnings.catch_warnings():
269	        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
270	        dm_ne, tau_ne = pg.dist_to_dm(l_deg, b_deg, dist_pc, method="ne2001")
271	        dm_yw, tau_yw = pg.dist_to_dm(l_deg, b_deg, dist_pc, method="ymw16")
272	    tau = tau_ne if method == "ne2001" else tau_yw
273	    try:
274	        tau_ms = float(tau.to(u.ms).value)
275	    except (AttributeError, u.UnitConversionError):
276	        tau_ms = float(tau) * 1.0e3
277	    return (float(dm_ne.value), float(dm_yw.value), tau_ms)
278	
279	
280	def _find_burst_config_path(name: str, configs_dir: str) -> str | None:
281	    """Return the data path string from a target's CHIME burst config yaml."""
282	    if not configs_dir or not os.path.isdir(configs_dir):
283	        return None
284	    target = name.lower()
285	    for fn in os.listdir(configs_dir):
286	        if not fn.lower().endswith((".yaml", ".yml")):
287	            continue
288	        if not fn.lower().startswith(target):
289	            continue
290	        try:
291	            with open(os.path.join(configs_dir, fn)) as fh:
292	                for line in fh:
293	                    if line.strip().startswith("path:"):
294	                        return line.split("path:", 1)[1].strip()
295	        except OSError:
296	            continue
297	    return None
298	
299	
300	def _lookup_dm_obs(name: str, configs_dir: str | None) -> float | None:
301	    if configs_dir is None:
302	        configs_dir = os.path.join("scattering", "configs", "bursts", "chime")
303	    return parse_dm_obs(_find_burst_config_path(name, configs_dir))
304	
305	
306	def _lookup_tau_fit(name: str, bursts_dir: str | None) -> dict | None:
307	    """Find the best CHIME scattering fit for a target across result locations.
308	
309	    Returns the read_tau_fit dict, preferring a quality-PASS fit when several are
310	    present (so a re-run that supersedes an old FAIL is picked up). Returns None
311	    if no fit_results.json with a usable tau exists.
312	    """
313	    target = name.lower()
314	    candidates: list[str] = []
315	    search_dirs = []
316	    if bursts_dir:
317	        search_dirs.append(os.path.join(bursts_dir, target))
318	        search_dirs.append(bursts_dir)
319	    search_dirs.append(os.path.join("scattering", "scat_process"))
320	    seen = set()
321	    for d in search_dirs:
322	        for pat in (f"{target}*chime*fit_results.json", f"{target}*fit_results.json"):
323	            for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, pat))):
324	                if path not in seen:
325	                    seen.add(path)
326	                    candidates.append(path)
327	
328	    best = None
329	    for path in candidates:
330	        fit = read_tau_fit(path)
331	        if fit is None:
332	            continue
333	        if fit.get("quality_flag") == "PASS":
334	            return fit
335	        if best is None:
336	            best = fit
337	    return best
338	
339	
340	def _scattering_verdict(tau_obs: float, tau_interv: float, tau_interv_hi: float, n_fg: int) -> str:
341	    if not math.isfinite(tau_obs) or tau_obs <= 0.0:
342	        return f"no scattering measurement (predicted intervening tau={tau_interv:.2g} ms)"
343	    if n_fg == 0:
344	        return "no intervening screen; scattering is host / Milky-Way"
345	    ratio = tau_interv / tau_obs
346	    ratio_hi = (tau_interv_hi / tau_obs) if math.isfinite(tau_interv_hi) else ratio
347	    if ratio >= 0.5:
348	        return f"intervening galaxy plausibly dominates (pred/obs={ratio:.2f})"
349	    if ratio_hi >= 0.5:
350	        return f"intervening galaxy may contribute (prior-upper pred/obs={ratio_hi:.2f})"
351	    if ratio >= 0.05:
352	        return f"intervening subdominant; host / Milky-Way dominates (pred/obs={ratio:.2g})"
353	    return f"intervening negligible; host / Milky-Way dominated (pred/obs={ratio:.2g})"
354	
355	
356	def _dm_verdict(dm_obs, dm_mw_ism, dm_mw_halo, dm_cosmic, dm_interv, dm_host) -> str:
357	    if not math.isfinite(dm_obs):
358	        return "no observed DM"
359	    if dm_host < -0.05 * max(dm_obs, 1.0):
360	        return "over-budget (MW+cosmic mean exceed observed; sightline below cosmic mean)"
361	    comps = {
362	        "Milky-Way": _nz(dm_mw_ism) + dm_mw_halo,
363	        "cosmic/IGM": dm_cosmic,
364	        "intervening galaxy": dm_interv,
365	        "host": max(dm_host, 0.0),
366	    }
367	    dominant = max(comps, key=lambda k: comps[k])
368	    return f"{dominant}-dominated"
369	
370	
371	def _nz(x: float) -> float:
372	    """Treat NaN as 0 for additive budget closure (model-unavailable component)."""
373	    return x if math.isfinite(x) else 0.0
374	
375	
376	def build_sightline_budget(
377	    name: str,
378	    ra_str: str,
379	    dec_str: str,
380	    z_frb: float,
381	    *,
382	    results_dir: str = "results",
383	    configs_dir: str | None = None,
384	    bursts_dir: str | None = None,
385	    enrich: bool = False,
386	    dm_mw_fn: Callable | None = None,
387	    dm_obs: float | None = None,
388	    tau_obs: float | None = None,
389	    dm_mw_halo: float = DM_MW_HALO,
390	) -> dict:
391	    """Assemble the full DM + scattering budget for one FRB sightline."""
392	    sight = SkyCoord(ra_str, dec_str, unit=(u.hourangle, u.deg))
393	    gal = sight.galactic
394	    l_deg, b_deg = float(gal.l.deg), float(gal.b.deg)
395	
396	    if dm_mw_fn is None:
397	        dm_mw_fn = galactic_dm_tau
398	    dm_mw_ism, dm_mw_ism_ymw16, tau_mw_ms = dm_mw_fn(l_deg, b_deg, "ne2001")
399	
400	    if dm_obs is None:
401	        dm_obs = _lookup_dm_obs(name, configs_dir)
402	
403	    # Scattering measurement: gate ingestion on the recalibrated quality flag.
404	    # An injected tau_obs (tests / manual override) is trusted as-is; otherwise a
405	    # fit_results.json is ingested ONLY when quality_flag == "PASS". A present but
406	    # non-PASS fit is recorded (so the verdict can say "fit present but not
407	    # locked in") but its tau is withheld from the budget.
408	    tau_obs_err_minus = tau_obs_err_plus = math.nan
409	    tau_obs_chi2 = math.nan
410	    if tau_obs is not None:
411	        tau_obs_quality = "INJECTED"
412	    else:
413	        tau_obs_quality = None
414	        fit = _lookup_tau_fit(name, bursts_dir)
415	        if fit is not None:
416	            tau_obs_quality = fit.get("quality_flag") or "UNKNOWN"
417	            tau_obs_chi2 = _f(fit.get("chi2_reduced"))
418	            if fit.get("quality_flag") == "PASS":
419	                tau_obs = fit.get("tau")
420	                tau_obs_err_minus = _f(fit.get("err_minus"))
421	                tau_obs_err_plus = _f(fit.get("err_plus"))
422	            # non-PASS: tau_obs stays None (withheld), quality recorded above
423	
424	    dm_hot = dm_cool = 0.0
425	    dm_hot_cap = dm_cool_cap = 0.0
426	    min_b_over_rvir = math.inf
427	    tau_int = tau_int_lo = tau_int_hi = 0.0
428	    n_fg = n_isect = 0
429	    dom: dict[str, Any] = {
430	        "best_z": math.nan, "best_b_over_rvir": math.nan, "best_g_scatt": math.nan,
431	        "best_cool_fc": math.nan, "best_logM": math.nan, "best_mass_source": None,
432	        "best_impact_kpc": math.nan,
433	    }
434	    best_tau = -1.0
435	
436	    csv_path = os.path.join(results_dir, f"{name.lower()}_galaxies.csv")
437	    if os.path.exists(csv_path):
438	        matches = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
439	        unified = build_unified_records(
440	            matches, z_frb=z_frb, sight_ra=sight.ra.deg, sight_dec=sight.dec.deg, enrich=enrich
441	        )
442	        for _, row in unified.iterrows():
443	            z = _f(row.get("z"))
444	            if not (math.isfinite(z) and z < float(z_frb)):  # foreground galaxies only
445	                continue
446	            n_fg += 1
447	            if _truthy(row.get("intersects_rvir")):
448	                n_isect += 1
449	            dh_raw = _nz(_f(row.get("dm_halo")))
450	            dc_raw = _nz(_f(row.get("dm_cool")))
451	            dm_hot += dh_raw
452	            dm_cool += dc_raw
453	
454	            # Capped intervening DM: re-evaluate the hot-halo column at the
455	            # CGM-regime floor max(b, 0.1 R_vir), then rescale the cool phase by
456	            # the same hot-column ratio (the cool term is sub-dominant).
457	            bor = _f(row.get("b_over_rvir"))
458	            if math.isfinite(bor):
459	                min_b_over_rvir = min(min_b_over_rvir, bor)
460	            m_halo = _f(row.get("M_halo"))
461	            rvir = _f(row.get("R_vir_kpc"))
462	            impact = _f(row.get("impact_kpc"))
463	            if math.isfinite(bor) and bor < INTERIOR_B_OVER_RVIR and all(
464	                math.isfinite(v) for v in (m_halo, rvir, impact)
465	            ) and rvir > 0.0 and dh_raw > 0.0:
466	                b_cap = max(impact, INTERIOR_B_OVER_RVIR * rvir)
467	                dh_cap = _nz(_f(scat.dm_halo_mnfw(m_halo, z, b_cap)))
468	                dc_cap = dc_raw * (dh_cap / dh_raw) if dh_raw > 0.0 else dc_raw
469	            else:
470	                dh_cap, dc_cap = dh_raw, dc_raw
471	            dm_hot_cap += dh_cap
472	            dm_cool_cap += dc_cap
473	
474	            t = _f(row.get("pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz"))
475	            if math.isfinite(t):
476	                tau_int += t
477	                tl = _f(row.get("pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz_lo"))
478	                th = _f(row.get("pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz_hi"))
479	                tau_int_lo += tl if math.isfinite(tl) else t
480	                tau_int_hi += th if math.isfinite(th) else t
481	                if t > best_tau:
482	                    best_tau = t
483	                    dom = {
484	                        "best_z": z,
485	                        "best_b_over_rvir": _f(row.get("b_over_rvir")),
486	                        "best_g_scatt": _f(row.get("g_scatt")),
487	                        "best_cool_fc": _f(row.get("cool_fc")),
488	                        "best_logM": _f(row.get("logM_best")),
489	                        "best_mass_source": (
490	                            str(row.get("mass_source")) if row.get("mass_source") is not None else None
491	                        ),
492	                        "best_impact_kpc": _f(row.get("impact_kpc")),
493	                    }
494	
495	    dm_intervening = dm_hot + dm_cool
496	    dm_intervening_capped = dm_hot_cap + dm_cool_cap
497	    if n_fg == 0:
498	        dm_regime = "none"
499	    elif math.isfinite(min_b_over_rvir) and min_b_over_rvir < INTERIOR_B_OVER_RVIR:
500	        dm_regime = "GALAXY_INTERIOR"
501	    else:
502	        dm_regime = "CGM"
503	
504	    # Without a real host redshift the cosmic/host decomposition is undefined.
505	    z_is_placeholder = _is_placeholder_z(z_frb)
506	    dm_cosmic = math.nan if z_is_placeholder else dm_cosmic_macquart(float(z_frb))
507	    dm_obs_f = _f(dm_obs)
508	    if math.isfinite(dm_obs_f) and not z_is_placeholder:
509	        base = dm_obs_f - _nz(dm_mw_ism) - dm_mw_halo - dm_cosmic
510	        dm_host = base - dm_intervening
511	        dm_host_capped = base - dm_intervening_capped
512	        dm_host_rest = dm_host * (1.0 + float(z_frb))
513	        dm_host_rest_capped = dm_host_capped * (1.0 + float(z_frb))
514	    else:
515	        dm_host = dm_host_capped = dm_host_rest = dm_host_rest_capped = math.nan
516	
517	    # Reliability of the intervening DM/tau: which mass the dominant screen used.
518	    intervening_mass_source = dom.get("best_mass_source")
519	    if intervening_mass_source is None:
520	        intervening_mass_confidence = "none"
521	    elif intervening_mass_source in _MEASURED_MASS_SOURCES:

611	def build_all_budgets(
612	    targets=None,
613	    results_dir: str = "results",
614	    configs_dir: str | None = None,
615	    bursts_dir: str | None = None,
616	    enrich: bool = False,
617	    dm_mw_fn: Callable | None = None,
618	    dm_obs_map: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
619	    tau_obs_map: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
620	) -> pd.DataFrame:
621	    """Build the DM + scattering budget for every configured sightline."""
622	    if targets is None:
623	        targets = config.TARGETS
624	    rows = []
625	    for name, ra_str, dec_str, z_frb in targets:
626	        dm_obs = dm_obs_map.get(name) if dm_obs_map is not None else None
627	        tau_obs = tau_obs_map.get(name) if tau_obs_map is not None else None
628	        rows.append(
629	            build_sightline_budget(
630	                name, ra_str, dec_str, z_frb,
631	                results_dir=results_dir, configs_dir=configs_dir, bursts_dir=bursts_dir,
632	                enrich=enrich, dm_mw_fn=dm_mw_fn, dm_obs=dm_obs, tau_obs=tau_obs,
633	            )
634	        )
635	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

638	def format_budget_table(df: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
639	    """Render the DM + scattering budget as a GitHub-flavored markdown table."""
640	    headers = [
641	        "Sightline", "z", "DM_obs", "DM_MW", "DM_cosmic", "DM_interv_raw",
642	        "DM_interv_cap", "regime", "interv_mass", "DM_host_cap", "tau_obs(ms)",
643	        "tau_interv(ms)", "scattering attribution",
644	    ]
645	    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(headers)) + "|"]
646	
647	    def fmt(x, spec):
648	        v = _f(x)
649	        return format(v, spec) if math.isfinite(v) else "-"
650	
651	    for _, r in df.iterrows():
652	        cells = [
653	            str(r["name"]),
654	            fmt(r.get("z_frb"), ".3f"),
655	            fmt(r.get("dm_obs"), ".0f"),
656	            fmt(_nz(_f(r.get("dm_mw_ism"))) + _f(r.get("dm_mw_halo")), ".0f"),
657	            fmt(r.get("dm_cosmic"), ".0f"),
658	            fmt(r.get("dm_intervening"), ".1f"),
659	            fmt(r.get("dm_intervening_capped"), ".1f"),
660	            str(r.get("dm_intervening_regime", "")),
661	            str(r.get("intervening_mass_confidence", "")),
662	            fmt(r.get("dm_host_capped"), ".0f"),
663	            fmt(r.get("tau_obs_ms"), ".3g"),
664	            fmt(r.get("tau_intervening_ms"), ".2g"),
665	            str(r.get("verdict_scattering", "")),
666	        ]
667	        lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
668	    return "\n".join(lines)

683	def make_budget_figure(df: pd.DataFrame):
684	    """Two-panel figure: stacked DM budget + predicted-vs-measured scattering."""
685	    d = df.copy()

704	    host = np.maximum(col("dm_host_capped"), 0.0)

706

713	        (host, HOST_COLOR, "host (residual)"),
714	    ):
715	        ax_dm.barh(y, vals, left=left, color=color, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.6, label=label, zorder=3)
716	        left = left + vals
717	
718	    dm_obs = col("dm_obs")

722	
723	    # Flag core-extrapolated sightlines and show the raw (uncapped) intervening DM.
724	    for yi, reg, raw, cap in zip(y, regime, interv_raw, interv):
725	        if reg == "GALAXY_INTERIOR" and raw > cap:
726	            ax_dm.annotate(

728	                xy=(0, yi), xytext=(4, -2), textcoords="offset points",
729	                va="top", ha="left", fontsize=7, color=HOST_COLOR, zorder=6,
730	            )
731

738	                xy=(max(xo, 1.0), yi), xytext=(6, 0), textcoords="offset points",
739	                va="center", ha="left", fontsize=7, color=COSMIC_COLOR, zorder=6,
740	            )
741	    ax_dm.set_yticks(y)
742	    ax_dm.set_yticklabels(names, fontsize=10)
743	    ax_dm.set_xlabel("DM (pc cm$^{-3}$)", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color=TEXT_DARK)
744	    ax_dm.set_title("DM budget per sightline  (black bar = observed DM)",
745	                    fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=DARK_BLUE, pad=10)
746	    ax_dm.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8, frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID_COLOR)
747	    ax_dm.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle=":", color=GRID_COLOR, alpha=0.8, zorder=0)
748	
749	    tau_obs = col("tau_obs_ms")

752	    tau_hi = col("tau_intervening_hi")
753	    for yi, to, ti, tl, th in zip(y, tau_obs, tau_int, tau_lo, tau_hi):
754	        if ti > 0:
755	            ax_tau.plot([max(tl, 1e-7), max(th, 1e-7)], [yi, yi], color=INTERV_COLOR, lw=2, zorder=2)
756	            ax_tau.scatter([ti], [yi], color=INTERV_COLOR, s=45, zorder=3,
757	                           label="predicted intervening" if yi == y[0] else None)
758	        if to > 0:

760	            thi = _f(d["tau_obs_err_plus"].iloc[list(y).index(yi)]) if "tau_obs_err_plus" in d.columns else math.nan
761	            if math.isfinite(tlo) and math.isfinite(thi) and (tlo > 0 or thi > 0):
762	                ax_tau.errorbar([to], [yi], xerr=[[max(tlo, 0)], [max(thi, 0)]], fmt="none",
763	                                ecolor=TEXT_DARK, elinewidth=1.2, capsize=3, zorder=4)
764	            ax_tau.scatter([to], [yi], marker="D", color=TEXT_DARK, s=55, zorder=5,

768	    quality = [str(v) for v in d.get("tau_obs_quality", pd.Series([""] * len(d)))]
769	    withheld_labeled = False

771	        if q in ("FAIL", "MARGINAL", "UNKNOWN"):
772	            x_at = max(ti, 1e-6)
773	            ax_tau.scatter([x_at], [yi], marker="x", color=HOST_COLOR, s=50, zorder=4,
774	                           label="fit withheld (failed gate)" if not withheld_labeled else None)
775	            withheld_labeled = True
776	
777	    ax_tau.set_yticks(y)
778	    ax_tau.set_yticklabels([])
779	    positive = np.concatenate([tau_obs[tau_obs > 0], tau_int[tau_int > 0]]) if len(d) else np.array([])
780	    if positive.size:
781	        ax_tau.set_xscale("log")
782	    ax_tau.set_xlabel(r"$\tau_{\rm scat}$ at 1 GHz (ms)", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color=TEXT_DARK)
783	    ax_tau.set_title("Scattering: predicted intervening vs measured",
784	                     fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color=DARK_BLUE, pad=10)
785	    handles, labels = ax_tau.get_legend_handles_labels()
786	    if handles:
787	        ax_tau.legend(loc="best", fontsize=8, frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID_COLOR)
788	    ax_tau.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle=":", color=GRID_COLOR, alpha=0.8)
789	
790	    fig.suptitle("FRB sightline DM & scattering budgets (priors + measurements)",
791	                 fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", color=DARK_BLUE)
792	    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.97))
793	    return fig

804	    )

1	"""Pure CGM scattering and dispersion predictions from galaxy scalars."""
2	
3	import math

5	import numpy as np
6	import astropy.units as u

8	from .config import COSMO

10	
11	def _is_bad(x: float | None) -> bool:
12	    """Return True for missing, NaN, or non-finite scalar inputs."""
13	    if x is None:
14	        return True
15	    try:
16	        value = float(x)
17	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
18	        return True
19	    return math.isnan(value) or bool(np.isnan(value)) or not math.isfinite(value)
20	
21	
22	def _clamp(value: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
23	    """Clamp a finite scalar to a closed interval."""
24	    return min(hi, max(lo, value))
25	
26	
27	def dm_halo_mnfw(
28	    m_halo_msun: float,
29	    z_gal: float,
30	    impact_kpc: float,
31	    f_hot: float = 0.75,
32	    y0: float = 2.0,
33	) -> float | None:
34	    """Return the observed mNFW hot-halo DM at projected impact parameter."""
35	    if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m_halo_msun, z_gal, impact_kpc, f_hot, y0)):
36	        return None
37	
38	    m200 = float(m_halo_msun)
39	    z_value = float(z_gal)
40	    b_kpc = float(impact_kpc)
41	    f_hot_value = float(f_hot)
42	    y0_value = float(y0)
43	    if m200 <= 0.0 or z_value < 0.0 or b_kpc < 0.0 or f_hot_value < 0.0 or y0_value < 0.0:
44	        return None
45	
46	    from scipy.integrate import quad
47	
48	    # Prochaska & Zheng 2019 MNRAS 485,648 set R200 from mass enclosing 200
49	    # times the redshift-dependent critical density, matching the mNFW halo
50	    # truncation used for CGM dispersion predictions in Macquart+2020.
51	    rho_crit = COSMO.critical_density(z_value).to(u.Msun / u.kpc**3).value
52	    if rho_crit <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(rho_crit):
53	        return None
54	    r200_kpc = (3.0 * m200 / (4.0 * math.pi * 200.0 * rho_crit)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)
55	    if r200_kpc <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(r200_kpc):
56	        return None
57	    if b_kpc >= r200_kpc:
58	        return 0.0
59	
60	    # Prochaska & Zheng 2019 MNRAS 485,648 use an NFW-like concentration for
61	    # halo gas; this bounded mass-concentration approximation keeps low/high
62	    # mass extrapolations numerically stable without changing the CGM trend.
63	    concentration = 7.7 * (m200 / 1.0e14) ** (-0.11)
64	    concentration = _clamp(concentration, 3.0, 15.0)
65	    rs_kpc = r200_kpc / concentration
66	    if rs_kpc <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(rs_kpc):
67	        return None
68	
69	    def shape_density(r_kpc: float) -> float:
70	        if r_kpc < 0.0:
71	            return 0.0
72	        y = r_kpc / rs_kpc
73	        # Prochaska & Zheng 2019 MNRAS 485,648 and Macquart+2020 Nature
74	        # 581,391 soften the NFW inner cusp by replacing y with y0+y, so the
75	        # column stays finite through the halo center while retaining an outer
76	        # NFW-like decline.
77	        return 1.0 / ((y0_value + y) * (1.0 + y) ** 2)
78	
79	    def radial_mass_integrand(r_kpc: float) -> float:
80	        # The 4*pi*r^2 term is the spherical volume element needed to normalize
81	        # the mNFW profile to the hot baryon mass rather than an arbitrary rho0.
82	        return 4.0 * math.pi * r_kpc**2 * shape_density(r_kpc)
83	
84	    norm_integral, _ = quad(radial_mass_integrand, 0.0, r200_kpc, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-6, limit=200)
85	    if norm_integral <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(norm_integral):
86	        return None
87	
88	    # Macquart+2020 Nature 581,391 appendix anchors halo gas to the cosmic
89	    # baryon allotment; f_hot selects the ionized hot phase within that budget.
90	    baryon_fraction = float(COSMO.Ob0 / COSMO.Om0)
91	    gas_mass_msun = f_hot_value * baryon_fraction * m200
92	    if gas_mass_msun < 0.0 or not math.isfinite(gas_mass_msun):
93	        return None
94	    rho0_msun_kpc3 = gas_mass_msun / norm_integral
95	
96	    # Prochaska & Zheng 2019 MNRAS 485,648 adopt mu_e~1.18 for fully ionized
97	    # primordial-composition CGM gas, converting gas mass density to electron
98	    # density through n_e=rho/(mu_e*m_p).
99	    mu_e = 1.18
100	    m_p_g = 1.67262192369e-24
101	    msun_per_kpc3_to_g_per_cm3 = (1.0 * u.Msun / u.kpc**3).to(u.g / u.cm**3).value
102	    rho0_g_cm3 = rho0_msun_kpc3 * msun_per_kpc3_to_g_per_cm3
103	
104	    def ne_cm3(r_kpc: float) -> float:
105	        return rho0_g_cm3 * shape_density(r_kpc) / (mu_e * m_p_g)
106	
107	    l_half_kpc = math.sqrt(max(r200_kpc**2 - b_kpc**2, 0.0))
108	
109	    def los_integrand(l_kpc: float) -> float:
110	        r_kpc = math.hypot(b_kpc, l_kpc)
111	        return ne_cm3(r_kpc)
112	
113	    column_ne_kpc_cm3, _ = quad(los_integrand, -l_half_kpc, l_half_kpc, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-6, limit=200)
114	    if not math.isfinite(column_ne_kpc_cm3):
115	        return None
116	
117	    # One kpc of path contributes 1000 pc to the conventional pc cm^-3 DM
118	    # units, and Macquart+2020 Nature 581,391 divides host/halo rest-frame DM
119	    # by (1+z) because dispersion is observed after cosmological dilation.
120	    dm_obs = column_ne_kpc_cm3 * 1000.0 / (1.0 + z_value)
121	    if not math.isfinite(dm_obs):
122	        return None
123	    return float(max(dm_obs, 0.0))

126	def dm_cool(dm_halo: float, cool_covering_fraction: float, mgii_wr: float | None = None) -> float | None:
127	    """Return a cool-photoionized CGM DM component scaled by coverage."""
128	    if _is_bad(dm_halo) or _is_bad(cool_covering_fraction):
129	        return None
130	
131	    dm_halo_value = float(dm_halo)
132	    fc = float(cool_covering_fraction)
133	    if dm_halo_value < 0.0 or fc < 0.0:
134	        return None
135	    fc = min(fc, 1.0)
136	
137	    # Werk+2014 ApJ 792,8 and Prochaska+2017 motivate a sub-dominant but
138	    # nonzero T~10^4 K photoionized column; k=0.3 is an explicit prior that the
139	    # cool phase is comparable-to-lower than the hot halo electron column.
140	    k_eff = 0.3
141	    if not _is_bad(mgii_wr):
142	        # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 and Anand+2024 use MgII equivalent width as
143	        # a monotonic proxy for cool CGM column, so tanh gives a bounded EW
144	        # boost without letting saturated absorbers dominate the prior.
145	        k_eff *= 1.0 + 0.5 * math.tanh(float(mgii_wr) / 1.0)
146	
147	    dm_value = dm_halo_value * fc * k_eff
148	    if not math.isfinite(dm_value):
149	        return None
150	    return float(max(dm_value, 0.0))
151	
152	
153	def f_tilde_prior(
154	    sfr_msun_yr: float,
155	    metallicity_12logOH: float | None = None,
156	    agn: bool = False,
157	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
158	    """Return a monotonic prior bracket for the turbulent scattering factor."""
159	    sfr = 0.0 if _is_bad(sfr_msun_yr) else max(float(sfr_msun_yr), 0.0)
160	
161	    # Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 and Cordes+2022 use F_tilde as a lumped
162	    # fluctuation factor; 0.1 is a quiescent-CGM order-of-magnitude floor in
163	    # the absence of a calibrated CGM F(SFR) relation.
164	    value = 0.1
165	    # Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 links stronger scattering to clumpier turbulent
166	    # ionized gas; log10(1+SFR) gives a transparent monotonic feedback boost
167	    # that is flat at zero SFR.
168	    value *= 1.0 + math.log10(1.0 + sfr)
169	
170	    if not _is_bad(metallicity_12logOH):
171	        # Asplund+2009 ARA&A 47,481 gives solar 12+log(O/H)~8.7; higher
172	        # metallicity is used here as a mild dust/clumping proxy with bounded
173	        # leverage because no direct CGM F-metallicity calibration exists.
174	        metallicity_factor = 1.0 + 0.3 * (float(metallicity_12logOH) - 8.7)
175	        value *= _clamp(metallicity_factor, 0.5, 2.0)
176	
177	    if agn:
178	        # Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 and Cordes+2022 associate stronger feedback
179	        # with enhanced turbulent density fluctuations, motivating a simple
180	        # factor-of-two AGN prior boost.
181	        value *= 2.0
182	
183	    value = max(value, 1e-12)
184	    # Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 emphasizes dex-level uncertainty in extragalactic
185	    # scattering environments, so a factor-three bracket encodes roughly
186	    # 0.5 dex of prior width around the deterministic central value.
187	    lo = value / 3.0
188	    hi = value * 3.0
189	    return float(value), float(lo), float(hi)
190	
191	
192	def g_scatt(z_lens: float, z_frb: float) -> float:
193	    """Return intervening-screen geometric scattering leverage in Mpc."""
194	    if _is_bad(z_lens) or _is_bad(z_frb):
195	        return 0.0
196	
197	    z_l = float(z_lens)
198	    z_s = float(z_frb)
199	    if z_l <= 0.0 or z_l >= z_s:
200	        return 0.0
201	
202	    # Macquart & Koay 2013 ApJ 776,125 and Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 give the
203	    # thin-screen leverage D_L D_LS / D_S, so a screen at the source has zero
204	    # leverage as D_LS approaches zero.
205	    d_l = COSMO.angular_diameter_distance(z_l).to(u.Mpc).value
206	    d_s = COSMO.angular_diameter_distance(z_s).to(u.Mpc).value
207	    d_ls = COSMO.angular_diameter_distance_z1z2(z_l, z_s).to(u.Mpc).value
208	    if d_l <= 0.0 or d_s <= 0.0 or d_ls <= 0.0:
209	        return 0.0
210	
211	    # Macquart & Koay 2013 ApJ 776,125 include the angular-diameter geometry;
212	    # the (1+z_l)^-2 term folds in cosmological screen dilation for a relative
213	    # Mpc-valued weight whose absolute normalization is left to tau_scat_ms.
214	    leverage = d_l * d_ls / d_s / (1.0 + z_l) ** 2
215	    if leverage <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(leverage):
216	        return 0.0
217	    return float(leverage)
218	
219	
220	def tau_scat_ms(
221	    f_tilde: float,
222	    g_scatt_val: float,
223	    dm_l: float,
224	    z_lens: float,
225	    nu_ghz: float = 1.0,
226	) -> float | None:
227	    """Return pulse-broadening timescale from a lens-galaxy screen in ms."""
228	    if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (f_tilde, g_scatt_val, dm_l, z_lens, nu_ghz)):
229	        return None
230	
231	    f_value = float(f_tilde)
232	    g_value = float(g_scatt_val)
233	    dm_value = float(dm_l)
234	    z_value = float(z_lens)
235	    nu_value = float(nu_ghz)
236	    if f_value < 0.0 or g_value < 0.0 or dm_value < 0.0 or z_value < 0.0 or nu_value <= 0.0:
237	        return None
238	
239	    # Cordes & Lazio 2002 astro-ph/0207156, Cordes+2016 ApJ 832,113, and
240	    # Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102 give tau proportional to SM*nu^-4 with
241	    # SM~F_tilde*DM^2 for a screen; A=1e-6 ms deliberately lumps the NE2001
242	    # SM-to-tau conversion and screen constants as an order-of-magnitude prior.
243	    a_ms = 1.0e-6
244	    # Macquart & Koay 2013 ApJ 776,125 convention for intervening screens uses
245	    # tau_obs=tau_rest*(1+z)^-3 after combining redshifted observing frequency
246	    # with cosmological time dilation, so the geometric weight is divided by
247	    # (1+z_lens)^3 here.
248	    tau = a_ms * f_value * g_value * dm_value**2 * nu_value ** (-4.0) / (1.0 + z_value) ** 3
249	    if not math.isfinite(tau):
250	        return None
251	    return float(max(tau, 0.0))
252	
253	
254	# Cool CGM enhances the turbulent fluctuation parameter F_tilde relative to the
255	# smooth hot halo: the cool phase shatters to ~pc cloudlets (McCourt+2018 MNRAS
256	# 473,5407), and such clumpy media can dominate radio scattering despite a
257	# sub-dominant electron column (Vedantham & Phinney 2019 MNRAS 483,971;
258	# Ocker+2021 ApJ 911,102). F_cool/F_hot is poorly constrained, so this is an
259	# explicit order-of-magnitude prior with a ~1 dex bracket.
260	COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10.0
261	COOL_CLUMP_BOOST_LO = 3.0
262	COOL_CLUMP_BOOST_HI = 30.0
263	
264	
265	def tau_scat_two_phase(
266	    f_tilde: float,
267	    g_scatt_val: float,
268	    dm_hot: float,
269	    dm_cool: float,
270	    z_lens: float,
271	    nu_ghz: float = 1.0,
272	    cool_clump_boost: float = COOL_CLUMP_BOOST,
273	) -> float | None:
274	    """Two-phase intervening-screen scattering: smooth hot halo + clumpy cool CGM.
275	
276	    Scattering measures of independent screens add, and tau is proportional to
277	    SM, so the two phases combine linearly:
278	
279	        tau = tau(F_tilde, dm_hot) + tau(F_tilde * cool_clump_boost, dm_cool)
280	
281	    The cool phase carries a smaller electron column (``dm_cool``) but a much
282	    larger fluctuation parameter because it is clumpy on ~pc scales (McCourt+2018;
283	    Vedantham & Phinney 2019; Ocker+2021); ``cool_clump_boost`` = F_cool/F_hot is
284	    an explicit order-of-magnitude prior. A missing/NaN cool column degrades to
285	    the hot-only screen; if neither phase is usable, returns None.
286	    """
287	    hot = tau_scat_ms(f_tilde, g_scatt_val, dm_hot, z_lens, nu_ghz=nu_ghz)
288	
289	    if _is_bad(f_tilde) or _is_bad(cool_clump_boost) or float(cool_clump_boost) < 0.0:
290	        f_tilde_cool: float | None = None
291	    else:
292	        f_tilde_cool = float(f_tilde) * float(cool_clump_boost)
293	    cool = tau_scat_ms(f_tilde_cool, g_scatt_val, dm_cool, z_lens, nu_ghz=nu_ghz)
294	
295	    if hot is None and cool is None:
296	        return None
297	    total = (hot or 0.0) + (cool or 0.0)
298	    if not math.isfinite(total):
299	        return None
300	    return float(max(total, 0.0))
301	
302	
303	def scint_bandwidth_khz(tau_scat_ms: float) -> float | None:
304	    """Return scintillation decorrelation bandwidth from scattering time."""
305	    if _is_bad(tau_scat_ms):
306	        return None
307	
308	    tau_ms = float(tau_scat_ms)
309	    if tau_ms <= 0.0:
310	        return None
311	
312	    # Cordes & Rickett 1998 ApJ 507,846 give nu_dc=C1/(2*pi*tau) with
313	    # C1~1.16 for a uniform Kolmogorov medium, linking pulse broadening to
314	    # decorrelation bandwidth by Fourier reciprocity.
315	    bandwidth_hz = 1.16 / (2.0 * math.pi * (tau_ms * 1.0e-3))
316	    if bandwidth_hz <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(bandwidth_hz):
317	        return None
318	    return float(bandwidth_hz / 1.0e3)
319	
320	
321	def predict_mgii_wr(impact_kpc: float, logmstar: float | None = None) -> float | None:
322	    """Return predicted MgII 2796 rest equivalent width in Angstrom."""
323	    if _is_bad(impact_kpc):
324	        return None
325	
326	    r_kpc = float(impact_kpc)
327	    if r_kpc <= 0.0:
328	        return None
329	
330	    r_break = 50.0
331	    w0 = 0.8
332	    if not _is_bad(logmstar):
333	        # Churchill+2013 ApJ 763,L42 and Anand+2021/2024 find stronger cool
334	        # absorption around more massive systems; this bounded 0.3-dex-per-dex
335	        # scaling keeps the Nielsen+2013 radial normalization recognizable.
336	        mass_factor = 10.0 ** (0.3 * (float(logmstar) - 10.5))
337	        w0 *= _clamp(mass_factor, 0.2, 3.0)
338	
339	    # Nielsen+2013 ApJ 776,114 MAGIICAT and Anand+2021/2024 show MgII W_r
340	    # anti-correlates with projected distance; the broken power law allows a
341	    # steeper inner decline and shallower outer halo tail around 50 kpc.
342	    if r_kpc <= r_break:
343	        wr = w0 * (r_kpc / r_break) ** (-1.7)
344	    else:
345	        wr = w0 * (r_kpc / r_break) ** (-0.6)
346	    if wr <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(wr):
347	        return None
348	    return float(wr)
349	
350	
351	def cool_covering_fraction(
352	    b_over_rvir: float,
353	    logmstar: float,
354	    is_star_forming: bool,
355	    phi_deg: float | None = None,
356	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
357	    """Return a prior bracket for the cool CGM covering fraction."""
358	    b_scaled = 10.0 if _is_bad(b_over_rvir) else max(float(b_over_rvir), 0.0)
359	
360	    # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 find cool-gas incidence declines with scaled
361	    # radius and is higher for star-forming galaxies; fc0=0.6/0.3 encodes that
362	    # population split while b_scale=0.5 gives an exponential halo falloff.
363	    fc0 = 0.6 if is_star_forming else 0.3
364	    if not _is_bad(logmstar):
365	        # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 show more cool absorption in more massive
366	        # halos on average, so this bounded tilt is deliberately mild.
367	        mass_tilt = 10.0 ** (0.15 * (float(logmstar) - 10.5))
368	        fc0 *= _clamp(mass_tilt, 0.5, 1.5)
369	    fc = fc0 * math.exp(-b_scaled / 0.5)
370	
371	    if is_star_forming and not _is_bad(phi_deg):
372	        # Bordoloi+2011 ApJ 743,10 and Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 motivate
373	        # stronger cool covering along the minor axis from outflow-fed gas, so
374	        # sin(phi) peaks at phi=90 deg and leaves the major axis unboosted.
375	        fc *= 1.0 + 0.5 * math.sin(math.radians(float(phi_deg)))
376	
377	    fc = _clamp(fc, 0.0, 1.0)
378	    # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 highlight population and azimuthal scatter, so
379	    # the bracket widens around the central prior and gets extra upper room
380	    # when star-forming azimuth information is available.
381	    lo = _clamp(fc * 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)
382	    hi = _clamp(fc * 1.5 + (0.2 if (is_star_forming and phi_deg is not None) else 0.0), 0.0, 1.0)
383	    fc = _clamp(fc, lo, hi)
384	    return float(fc), float(lo), float(hi)
385

"""Network-optional cross-survey enrichment helpers for matched galaxies."""

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord
import astropy.units as u


DESI_LS_MATCH_RADIUS = 1.5 * u.arcsec
WISE_MATCH_RADIUS = 2.5 * u.arcsec
GALEX_MATCH_RADIUS = 4.0 * u.arcsec
XSC_MATCH_RADIUS = 5.0 * u.arcsec

DESI_LS_COLUMNS = (
    "desi_ls_gmag",
    "desi_ls_rmag",
    "desi_ls_zmag",
    "desi_ls_w1mag",
    "desi_ls_w2mag",
    "desi_ls_type",
    "desi_ls_sersic",
    "desi_ls_shape_r",
    "desi_ls_sep_arcsec",
)
ALLWISE_COLUMNS = (
    "W1mag",
    "W2mag",
    "W3mag",
    "W4mag",
    "wise_W1_W2",
    "wise_agn",
    "wise_sep_arcsec",
)
GALEX_COLUMNS = ("galex_fuv", "galex_nuv", "galex_ebv", "galex_sep_arcsec")
XSC_COLUMNS = ("xsc_kmag", "xsc_axis_ratio", "xsc_pa", "xsc_sep_arcsec")
DESI_EMISSION_COLUMNS = (
    "desi_oii_flux",
    "desi_halpha_flux",
    "desi_is_agn",
    "desi_emission_matched",
)


def _blank_object_array(n_rows: int) -> np.ndarray:
    values = np.empty(n_rows, dtype=object)
    values[:] = np.nan
    return values


def _ensure_columns(matches: pd.DataFrame, columns: tuple[str, ...], overwrite: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = matches.copy()
    for column in columns:
        if not overwrite and column in out.columns:
            continue
        if column == "desi_emission_matched":
            out[column] = np.array([False] * len(out), dtype=object)
        elif column in {"desi_ls_type", "wise_agn", "desi_is_agn"}:
            out[column] = _blank_object_array(len(out))

## Codebase findings — foreground search & sightline attribution
*State: HEAD `8ca87f7`, 2026-06-23.*

**The sample.** 12 sightlines, all Dec +70 to +74 (`config.py:21-34`). z spans 0.043–0.51 with **3 placeholder z=1.0** (Freya, Mahi, Johndoeii) flagged as unknown host-z (`sightline_budget.py:77`).

**Search method (production = `galaxies/v2_0/search.py`):**
- Engines: NED cone (`engines.py:23`) + Vizier GLADE+, DESI DR8-North `VII/292`, SDSS DR12 (`config.py:37-41`); opt-in DESI DR1 spec-z (`engines_extra.py`, covers only 3/12) and enrichers (Legacy DR10 tractor, AllWISE, GALEX, 2MASS-XSC) — both **off by default** (`config.py:55-56`).
- Foreground cut: `z < z_frb + 0.01`, photo-z-error-aware (2σ) (`search.py:56-74`); impact cut **100 kpc galaxies / 5 Mpc clusters** (`config.py:9-11`).
- Dedup across catalogs by 10″ + Δz (`search.py:119-149`); PS1 g/i backfill for DESI-only rows lacking mass (`search.py:158-201`).

**Cluster handling — the gap.** Clusters are detected *only* via NED `Type` strings (`GClstr/GGroup/ClG`) caught by a regex (`search.py:31-43`), then given the 5 Mpc impact. **No WHL / redMaPPer / SZ cluster engine is wired into production.** WHL cross-match exists *only in exploratory notebooks* (`galaxies/v2_0/analysis.ipynb` ~46 refs, `notebooks/codetections/interveners.ipynb`). Net result: **zero cluster-classified rows in any of the 9 committed `*_galaxies.csv`** — the 5 Mpc cluster search yielded nothing in practice.

**Other (non-production) search methods present:** WISE-PS1-STRM + Legacy-DR8 photo-z beam search (`galaxies/wise-ps1-strm/`); Tarrío PS1 photo-z SOV-tile impact matching + Gaia (`galaxies/tarrio_ps1_photz/`); a DR8 sweep+photo-z stack built **specifically for the +70°–+75° Dec strip** (`galaxies/dr8_dec70_75/stack.py`) — a direct response to thin high-Dec spectroscopic coverage.

**Search → DM/τ budget** (`build_unified.py` → `scattering_predict.py` → `sightline_budget.py`), all self-citing primary sources:
- Stellar mass priority GLADE→2MASS-K→DESI-SED→WISE-W1→PS1-Taylor→assumed 10¹⁰ (`build_unified.py:26-33,118-155`).
- mNFW hot-halo DM (Prochaska & Zheng 2019, Macquart+2020) `scattering_predict.py:27`; cool-CGM DM via covering fraction + MgII (Lan & Mo 2018, Nielsen+2013) `:126,321`; two-phase τ with clumpy-cool boost ×10 (McCourt+2018, Vedantham & Phinney 2019, Ocker+2021) `:260-300`; intervening-screen geometric leverage D_L·D_LS/D_S (Macquart & Koay 2013) `:192`.
- Budget closure DM_obs − MW(NE2001) − MW-halo(40, Yamasaki & Totani 2020) − cosmic(Macquart) − intervening = host (`sightline_budget.py:124,86,376`). Core-extrapolation cap at b<0.1 R_vir (`:71,463-472`).
- Prior-predictive sensitivity over 3 prior families (`sightline_sensitivity.py`).

**Actual per-sightline distribution** (committed `search_summary.csv` + `sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md`): foreground galaxy counts Zach 2, Whitney 2, Oran **0**, Isha 1, Wilhelm 2, Phineas 3, Freya 1, Hamilton 1, Mahi **0**, Chromatica 2, Casey **0**, Johndoeii 1. Notable intervening-DM sightlines: Phineas (367 capped, GALAXY_INTERIOR), Whitney (200), Johndoeii (213), Zach (143). **Negative host DM** on Zach/Whitney/Wilhelm/Phineas (under-dense, below cosmic mean). Predicted intervening τ is tiny everywhere except Phineas (1.4 ms) — i.e. the code's own verdict is that intervening galaxies rarely dominate scattering in this sample.

# Prior-art: Galaxy clusters along FRB sightlines

Acronyms: ICM — Intracluster Medium; CGM — Circumgalactic Medium; DM — Dispersion Measure; RM — Rotation Measure; SZ — Sunyaev-Zel'dovich; mNFW — modified Navarro-Frenk-White; NCP — North Celestial Pole.

Methods note: firecrawl semantic backend was rate-limited (HTTP 429) and perplexity declined live retrieval, so every number below was verified via direct arXiv/ar5iv full-text reads or web search of primary sources — not via the semantic tool. IDs marked *(verify)* I could not pin to the exact arXiv number; journal refs for those are reliable.

## B1. Galaxy-cluster catalogs (+ high-Dec usability)

- WHL (optical, SDSS). Wen, Han & Liu 2012 (WHL12): 132,684 clusters at 0.05<z<0.8 from SDSS DR8 (~14,000 deg²), friends-of-friends overdensity finder; richness = total r-band luminosity in aperture (R_L*) as mass proxy. Detection rate >90% for M200>2e14 Msun at z<=0.42; z-uncertainty <0.022; ~20% member contamination (ApJS 199, 34; arXiv:1202.6424). Wen & Han 2015 update -> 158,103 clusters/groups, 89% spec-z (arXiv:1503.04332 *(verify)*).
- redMaPPer (optical, SDSS). Rykoff et al. 2014: red-sequence matched-filter over ~10,000 deg² SDSS DR8, ~25,000 clusters, z in [0.08,0.55], richness lambda as low-scatter mass proxy; photo-z scatter sigma_z~0.006 at z~0.1 -> ~0.02 at z~0.5 (ApJ 785,104; arXiv:1303.3562).
- SZ — ACT DR5. Hilton et al. 2021: 4,195 confirmed SZ clusters over 13,211 deg², z=0.04–1.91, S/N>4 (ApJS 253,3; arXiv:2009.11043). Equatorial/southern footprint; does NOT reach Dec>+70.
- SZ — SPT-SZ. Bleem et al. 2015: ~2,500 deg² southern, Dec ~ -65 to -40 (ApJS 216,27; arXiv:1409.0850). Irrelevant at northern high Dec.
- SZ — Planck PSZ2. Planck 2015 results XXVII: 1,653 detections (1,203 confirmed), ALL-SKY incl. NCP, deepest all-sky cluster catalog, >=83% purity (A&A 594,A27; arXiv:1502.01598).
- X-ray — eROSITA eRASS1. Bulbul et al. 2024: 12,247 clusters/groups; covers WESTERN GALACTIC HEMISPHERE ONLY -> primarily southern equatorial sky (A&A 685,A106; cosmology companion arXiv:2402.08458). No useful coverage at northern Dec>+70.
- X-ray — MCXC. Piffaretti et al. 2011: 1,743 ROSAT-based clusters, ALL-SKY meta-catalog (incl. NORAS/REFLEX/NEP), homogenized to M500/R500 (A&A 534,A109; arXiv:1007.1916). MCXC-II 2024 update arXiv:2402.01538.

HIGH-DEC VERDICT (critical for the +70 to +74 sample): SDSS imaging in the N Galactic Cap stops well short of +70 (nominal edge ~+60–65), so WHL and redMaPPer have NO coverage at the sample declinations. ACT/SPT/eROSITA-eRASS1 are southern/equatorial. The only catalogs with genuine Dec>+70 coverage are the all-sky ones: Planck PSZ2 (SZ) and MCXC/MCXC-II (X-ray, RASS-based with NEP). Both are shallow/mass-limited there -> poor completeness for low-mass groups.

## B2. FRB / radio sightlines through clusters

- Connor et al. 2023 (DSA-110) — FRB hosts IN clusters. FRB 20220914A (Abell 2310, offset 520±50 kpc, M500~1.7–1.9e14) and FRB 20220509G (Abell 2311, offset 870±50 kpc, M500~1.6e14). ICM DM (cluster frame): 295–568 pc/cm³ (A2310) and 16–172 pc/cm³ (A2311), 90% CI, using an Arnaud+2010 gNFW profile scaled by X-ray R500. RM = -111.5±1 rad/m² toward 20220509G -> ICM B~0.7–7.5 uG; no RM for the other (ApJ 949,75; arXiv:2302.14788).
- Lee et al. 2023 (FLIMFLAM) — FRB 20190520B through TWO foreground clusters. z=0.187 (b_perp=542 kpc=0.39 r200, DM~300–350) and z=0.217 (b_perp=1156 kpc=0.77 r200, DM~110–180). Total foreground halo DM = 450(+240/-130) to 640(+260/-150) pc/cm³; gas via mNFW (Prochaska & Zheng 2019) (ApJL 954,L7; arXiv:2306.05403).
- "Multi-halo" paper arXiv:2405.14182 — NB: about INDIVIDUAL intervening galaxy halos/CGM, NOT clusters. FRB 20221219A pierces two galaxy halos (M_h~1e11.96, 1e11.52) at small impact (43, 36 kpc), each contributing only ~10 and ~14 pc/cm³ DM; the large tau~19 ms is attributed to a partially-ionized CGM CLOUDLET of an intervening galaxy, not a cluster. Use as a CGM-scattering analogue, not a cluster result.
- FLIMFLAM DR1 (Khrykin et al. 2024) — IGM/CGM baryon-partition from 8 FRB sightlines; foreground-structure DM methodology (arXiv:2402.00505).
- CHIME/FRB Outrigger group/cluster gas fractions (2025) — 3 FRBs through group/cluster-mass halos; DM probes intragroup gas where X-ray/SZ are weak (arXiv:2509.07097).
- FRB 180417 toward Virgo cluster (ASKAP targeted search), DM=474.8 (2019, arXiv:1909.05779). WHIM-beyond-R200 via FRB DM + SZ (2016, arXiv:1609.03566). DSA RM sample (Sherman 2023/24, arXiv:2308.06816).

## B3. Cluster gas -> DM / scattering models

- Profiles in use: (i) Arnaud+2010 gNFW pressure profile scaled by X-ray R500 (Connor 2023); (ii) mNFW gas profile of Prochaska & Zheng 2019 (alpha=2, y0=2), used for both cluster and galaxy halos (Lee 2023; P&Z 2019 MNRAS 485,648, arXiv:1901.11051 *(verify)*). Underlying physical form is the classic beta-model n_e(r)=n0[1+(r/r_c)²]^(-3beta/2), beta~0.6.
- DM vs impact parameter — the central quantitative point: within ~0.4 r200 of a ~1e14.3 Msun cluster -> DM~300 pc/cm³; at ~0.77 r200 still ~110 pc/cm³ (Lee 2023). So clusters contribute VERY meaningful DM (tens–hundreds pc/cm³) provided the sightline passes within ~1–2 r200 (~1–4 Mpc for massive clusters). Falls steeply with impact parameter (centrally-concentrated column).
- SCATTERING: clusters are a DM source, NOT a tau source in observed cases. Connor 2023 saw NO significant scattering in their two cluster-embedded FRBs; Lee 2023 explicitly cites this to argue the foreground clusters do NOT cause FRB 20190520B's large tau (host/engine screen instead). Theory: turbulent ICM can enhance scattering over voids/walls (Zhu/Feng et al. 2018, arXiv:1808.05739), but geometric leverage for a cosmologically-distant cluster screen makes broadening ~nanoseconds — negligible vs ms-scale FRB tau — and intersection probability per sightline is low (Ocker et al. 2022 scattering horizons, arXiv:2203.16716, secondary).

## B4. Disconfirming / limitations

- Multi-Mpc impact is the WRONG regime. Meaningful DM needs the sightline inside ~1–2 r200 (<= a few Mpc for the most massive clusters, less for groups). The 300->110 pc/cm³ falloff over 0.39->0.77 r200 (Lee 2023) shows the steep decline. A 5 Mpc impact radius will MOSTLY return geometric near-misses with negligible DM (<= few–tens pc/cm³) unless the cluster is very massive AND the sightline is well inside its virial sphere. No FRB result demonstrates meaningful DM at >2 r200 — the "5 Mpc = negligible" conclusion is my extrapolation from observed profiles, not a stated literature result.
- Scattering from clusters at any impact is likely negligible (see B3) — don't expect the cluster catalog to explain tau in the co-detection sample.
- High-Dec catalog completeness is the binding limitation. At +70 to +74: SDSS-based WHL/redMaPPer absent; ACT/SPT/eROSITA southern. Left with Planck PSZ2 (shallow, mass-limited ~few×1e14, misses groups) and MCXC/MCXC-II (RASS-based, shallow, incomplete for low-L_X). Expect substantial incompleteness for group-mass systems along these sightlines.
- Photo-z vs spec-z. WHL/redMaPPer rely on photo-z (sigma_z~0.006–0.022 in good regimes); Delta_z~0.02 maps to large LOS-distance/impact-parameter uncertainty. Toward Dec>+70 (outside SDSS) any optical photo-z would come from shallower imaging with worse z and more false positives. SZ/X-ray detections still need optical z confirmation, itself thin at high Dec.

## Key papers (deduplicated, arXiv IDs)
- Wen, Han & Liu 2012, ApJS 199,34 — WHL12 — arXiv:1202.6424
- Wen & Han 2015 — WHL update (158,103) — arXiv:1503.04332 *(verify)*
- Rykoff et al. 2014, ApJ 785,104 — redMaPPer — arXiv:1303.3562
- Hilton et al. 2021, ApJS 253,3 — ACT DR5 SZ — arXiv:2009.11043
- Bleem et al. 2015, ApJS 216,27 — SPT-SZ — arXiv:1409.0850
- Planck Collab. 2016, A&A 594,A27 — PSZ2 (all-sky SZ) — arXiv:1502.01598
- Bulbul et al. 2024, A&A 685,A106 — eROSITA eRASS1 (cosmology companion arXiv:2402.08458)
- Piffaretti et al. 2011, A&A 534,A109 — MCXC (all-sky X-ray) — arXiv:1007.1916; MCXC-II 2024 — arXiv:2402.01538
- Connor et al. 2023, ApJ 949,75 — DSA-110 FRBs in massive clusters (ICM DM + RM) — arXiv:2302.14788
- Lee et al. 2023, ApJL 954,L7 — FRB 20190520B through 2 foreground clusters — arXiv:2306.05403
- DSA-110 2024 — FRB 20221219A intervening galaxy halos/CGM (NOT clusters) — arXiv:2405.14182
- Khrykin et al. 2024 — FLIMFLAM DR1 — arXiv:2402.00505

- WHIM around clusters via FRB DM + SZ 2016 — arXiv:1609.03566
- Ocker et al. 2022 — radio scattering horizons — arXiv:2203.16716 *(secondary, ICM-tau context)*

## Gaps / what I could not confirm
- arXiv IDs flagged *(verify)*: Wen & Han 2015 (1503.04332), Prochaska & Zheng 2019 (1901.11051), and the eROSITA eRASS1 CATALOG paper proper (Bulbul 2024 — I confirmed the cosmology companion 2402.08458 but not the catalog-description ID). Journal refs reliable; double-check exact arXiv numbers before citing.
- No paper directly computes the DISTRIBUTION of cluster-intersection DM at 1–5 Mpc impact for a realistic catalog — the "5 Mpc -> negligible" claim is my extrapolation from Lee/Connor profiles (within ~2 r200), not a stated result. A forward-model paper for this regime would strengthen B4.
- Did not numerically verify the exact SDSS imaging northern edge; "~+60–65, short of +70" rests on SDSS footprint docs. Qualitative conclusion (WHL/redMaPPer don't reach +70) is robust.

Net guidance for the pipeline: at +70 to +74, lean on Planck PSZ2 + MCXC/MCXC-II (the only all-sky catalogs covering the band), expect poor completeness for group-mass systems, treat the search as a DM-budget exercise (clusters are negligible scatterers), and tighten the impact-parameter criterion — a 5 Mpc radius mostly yields negligible-DM near-misses; meaningful DM requires the sightline inside ~1–2 r200.

Identifying intervening/foreground galaxies along FRB sightlines\n- The standard association cut is **impact parameter b⊥ ≲ r200 with a spec-z**;\n  FLIMFLAM operationalizes this with deep narrow-field spectroscopy of galaxies near\n  the sightline plus wide-field spectroscopy for the larger-scale density field\n  (Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024, FLIMFLAM DR1, arXiv:2402.00505).\n- **FLIMFLAM is the canonical end-to-end pipeline**: it reconstructs the ~Mpc matter\n  density field along each sightline (Bayesian ARGO reconstruction), associates\n  halos, and fits a DM model with MW/IGM/halo/host terms, then constrains the\n  CGM/IGM baryon partition — f_IGM = 0.59 (+0.11/−0.10), CGM gas fraction f_gas =\n  0.55 (+0.26/−0.29) (Khrykin et al. 2024, arXiv:2402.00505; method precursors\n  Simha et al. 2020 arXiv:2005.13157, 2021 arXiv:2108.09881; Khrykin et al. 2023\n  arXiv:2303.07387).\n- **Baseband/interferometric foreground searches** are the DSA-110 mode: the\n  first DSA-110 FRB+host catalog (Law/Sharma et al. 2023, arXiv:2307.03344) and the\n  multi-halo burst FRB 20221219A, whose sightline is \"significantly overcrowded\"\n  (CDF ≈ 0.99 vs expected N_halos = 0.18) with two intervening halos identified by\n  optical/IR SED fitting (Connor et al. 2024, arXiv:2405.14182).\n- **Statistical host/intervener association**: PATH Bayesian framework (Aggarwal et\n  al. 2021, arXiv:2102.10627), with chance-coincidence sub-samples (Bhandari et al.\n  2022, arXiv:2009.10747).\n- The **r200 cut is itself a modeling choice**: Prochaska & Zheng 2019 warn the\n  virial \"edge\" is artificial — integrating to 2·r200 adds tens of pc cm⁻³ at b ≳\n  0.5 r200 (arXiv:1901.11051). The code's behavior here is the inverse problem (it\n  caps at 0.1 R_vir for the inner blow-up) but the outer-truncation sensitivity is\n  unhandled.\n\n### B. Galaxy clusters along sightlines, and high-Dec catalog coverage\n- **Cluster catalogs and their declination reach** (the binding constraint for this\n  sample): WHL (Wen, Han & Liu 2012, arXiv:1202.6424; update Wen & Han 2015,\n  arXiv:1503.04332 *(verify)*) and redMaPPer (Rykoff et al. 2014, arXiv:1303.3562)\n  are **SDSS-based and do not cover Dec > +70** (SDSS imaging in the N Galactic Cap\n  ends near +60–65°). SZ catalogs ACT DR5 (Hilton et al. 2021, arXiv:2009.11043)\n  and SPT-SZ (Bleem et al. 2015, arXiv:1409.0850), and X-ray eROSITA eRASS1 (Bulbul\n  et al. 2024, A&A 685,A106; cosmology companion arXiv:2402.08458) are\n  equatorial/southern. **The only catalogs with genuine Dec > +70 coverage are the\n  all-sky ones: Planck PSZ2 (SZ; Planck 2016, arXiv:1502.01598) and MCXC /\n  MCXC-II (X-ray RASS-based; Piffaretti et al. 2011, arXiv:1007.1916; MCXC-II\n  arXiv:2402.01538)** — both shallow and mass-limited there, so poor completeness\n  for group-mass systems.\n- **FRBs through clusters give meaningful DM but negligible scattering.** DSA-110\n  FRBs in Abell 2310/2311 contribute ICM DM of 16–568 pc cm⁻³ but show no\n  significant scattering (Connor et al. 2023, arXiv:2302.14788). FRB 20190520B\n  pierces two foreground clusters (b = 0.39 and 0.77 r200) contributing 450–640 pc\n  cm⁻³ total halo DM, and the authors explicitly argue these clusters do **not**\n  cause the burst's large τ (Lee et al. 2023, arXiv:2306.05403).\n- **DM vs impact parameter is steep**: ~300 pc cm⁻³ at 0.39 r200 falling to ~110 pc\n  cm⁻³ at 0.77 r200 (Lee 2023). Meaningful cluster DM requires the sightline within\n  ~1–2 r200 (≲ a few Mpc for the most massive clusters); a **5 Mpc impact radius\n  mostly returns negligible-DM near-misses** (this last step is an extrapolation\n  from the observed profiles, not a directly stated literature result).\n- Cluster turbulent ICM can in principle enhance scattering (Zhu/Feng et al. 2018,\n  arXiv:1808.05739), but geometric leverage for a cosmologically-distant cluster\n  screen drives broadening to ≪ ms — negligible vs FRB τ (Ocker et al. 2022,\n  arXiv:2203.16716, secondary).\n\n### C. CGM/halo gas → DM and scattering models\n- **mNFW gas profile** ρ_b(r) ∝ 1/[y^(1−α)(y0+y)^(2+α)], fiducial y0 = α = 2, f_b,halo\n  = 0.75 (Prochaska & Zheng 2019, arXiv:1901.11051) — **exactly the form the code\n  implements and cites** (`scattering_predict.py:27-123`). FLIMFLAM uses the same\n  form.\n- **Macquart relation** ⟨DM_cosmic⟩ ∝ ∫ f_IGM(1+z)/E(z) dz (Macquart et al. 2020,\n  Nature 581, arXiv:2005.13161 — verified) — the baseline the code uses for cosmic\n  DM (`sightline_budget.py:124-143`).\n- **Geometric leverage**: τ ≈ 48.03 μs · A_τ F̃ DM_ℓ² G_scatt /[(1+z_ℓ)³ ν⁴], with\n  G_scatt = 2 d_sl d_lo /(L d_so) (Ocker, Cordes & Chatterjee 2021,\n  arXiv:2101.04784). This is the canonical FRB-halo leverage paper; the code cites\n  Macquart & Koay 2013 for the equivalent geometry (`scattering_predict.py:192-217`)\n  and could additionally cite Ocker+2021.\n- **Cool-CGM cloudlet scattering**: foundational model is Vedantham & Phinney 2019\n  (arXiv:1811.10876) on McCourt+2018 \"shattered\" sub-pc cloudlets; refractive\n  cloudlet lensing (arXiv:2309.07256) — see citation caveat in Synthesis. But\n  **CGM cloud-size limits** suggest realistic low-z cool CGM (n_e ≲ 10⁻² cm⁻³) adds\n  little scattering unless clouds are ≲ 0.1 pc (arXiv:2504.19562), and hot-CGM\n  scattering is ≪ 1 μs at 1 GHz (Ocker et al. 2025, arXiv:2503.02329). The code's\n  `COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` (range 3–30) is therefore an **optimistic** cool-phase\n  prior (`scattering_predict.py:254-262`).\n\n### D. MgII absorbers as intervening cool-gas tracers\n- **No published work ties an individual MgII absorber to a measured FRB DM or τ\n  excess on the same sightline** — this is a genuine gap (a claimed link from a\n  secondary source produced only hallucinated IDs and was discarded). MgII↔cool-CGM\n  baseline relations are quasar-based: W(MgII 2796) declines with impact parameter,\n  high covering fraction within ~100–150 kpc of L* galaxies (MAGIICAT — Nielsen et\n  al. 2013; Lan & Mo 2018) — the relations the code's `predict_mgii_wr` and\n  `cool_covering_fraction` encode (`scattering_predict.py:321-384`). MgII in\n  groups/clusters: Anand et al. 2022 (arXiv:2201.07811). The DSA multi-halo burst\n  uses COS-Halos N_HII(b,M⋆) — the same cool photoionized phase MgII traces — as its\n  DM_igh template (arXiv:2405.14182).\n\n### E. Disconfirming evidence & limitations\n- **Scattering is usually host/Milky-Way-dominated, not foreground-dominated.**\n  Halos contribute to DM \"but evidently not to scattering, which is dominated by\n  host galaxies\" (Cordes et al. 2022, arXiv:2108.01172); measured intervening-halo\n  τ is negligible for FRB 181112/191108 (Ocker et al. 2021, arXiv:2101.04784); FRB\n  20190520B is explicitly host-dominated (Ocker et al. 2022, arXiv:2202.13458);\n  CHIME population modeling concurs (arXiv:2502.05838). **Counterpoint:** the DSA\n  multi-halo burst FRB 20221219A is *not* host-dominated — an overcrowded\n  intervening sightline can dominate (Connor et al. 2024, arXiv:2405.14182). That is\n  precisely the regime the co-detection sample is built to probe.\n- **High-Dec photo-z incompleteness / catalog depth.** DESI Legacy photo-z degrade\n  where spec-z training is sparse — directly the Dec > +70 case (Duncan 2022,\n  arXiv:2203.01949; Zhou 2021, arXiv:2001.06018; SOM analyses arXiv:2409.14799). A\n  Rubin-era forecast finds the dominant error is **missing dim/high-z hosts**\n  (catalog depth), degrading inferences ~47–62%, far more than photo-z scatter\n  (~7%) (arXiv:2603.00371). SDSS spectroscopy largely excludes Dec > +70; GLADE+ is\n  shallow; PS1 lacks spectroscopy — so the project's high-Dec search is\n  photometry-limited and spec-z-starved. No paper quantifies FRB-foreground\n  completeness specifically at Dec > +70 (gap).\n- **False-association risk.** PATH quantifies chance coincidence (arXiv:2102.10627);\n  host association degrades once σ_loc ≳ 2″ (arXiv:2502.16791), so large-impact\n  foreground association under coarse localization or photo-z-only redshifts is\n  fragile. No FRB-specific paper gives a contamination number for intervening (vs\n  host) association under photo-z only (gap).\n\n## Synthesis\n\n**The code implements a defensible, literature-grounded version of the standard\nmethod, but a deliberately simplified one.** Its impact-parameter + (photo-z or\nspec-z) cone search, mNFW halo DM, Macquart cosmic baseline, two-phase cool/hot\nscreen, and geometric leverage all map directly onto the canonical references\n(Prochaska & Zheng 2019, Macquart+2020, Ocker+2021, FLIMFLAM), and the modules cite\nthem inline. What it does **not** do — and what FLIMFLAM does — is reconstruct the\nMpc-scale density field or jointly fit the baryon partition; the code instead\nattributes per-halo columns deterministically and brackets the nuisance\nastrophysics with a prior-predictive sensitivity layer. That is an appropriate\nscope choice for a 12-sightline study, not a defect.\n\n**The external consensus validates the code's central scientific verdict.** Across\nCordes 2022, Ocker 2021/2022, and CHIME population work, intervening halos add DM\nbut rarely scattering — exactly what the budget table reports (predicted τ_interv\nnegligible everywhere except Phineas). The one regime where this flips —\novercrowded sightlines (DSA multi-halo, arXiv:2405.14182) — is the regime this\nsample targets, so the scientific payoff lives in the tail, and Phineas (3\nforeground galaxies, GALAXY_INTERIOR, τ_interv = 1.4 ms) is the natural first case\nto scrutinize.\n\n**The cluster search is the clearest weakness, and prior art explains why.**\nClusters are found only by NED object-type strings with a 5 Mpc impact, and **zero\nclusters turn up** on any sightline. Two independent reasons: (1) at Dec +70°–74°,\nthe SDSS-based cluster catalogs (WHL, redMaPPer) have no coverage, and even the\nnotebook WHL cross-match cannot help there — only all-sky Planck PSZ2 and\nMCXC/MCXC-II reach the band, both shallow; (2) a 5 Mpc impact mostly yields\nnegligible-DM near-misses, because meaningful cluster DM needs the sightline within\n~1–2 r200, and clusters contribute essentially no scattering at any impact (Connor\n2023, Lee 2023). So the current cluster machinery is both under-powered (wrong\ncatalogs for this sky) and aimed at a low-yield regime.\n\n### Gaps and open questions\n- **Cluster catalog coverage at Dec > +70.** If clusters matter, the production\n  search needs an all-sky catalog engine (Planck PSZ2 and/or MCXC-II), not NED-type\n  strings — and the 5 Mpc radius should be re-examined against an r200-relative\n  criterion. *(Light recommendation; design deferred to planning.)*\n- **`COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` is optimistic.** Recent cloud-size/turbulence limits\n  (arXiv:2504.19562, arXiv:2503.02329) push the realistic cool-CGM scattering\n  contribution down; the lo bound (3) may be closer to reality. Worth a sensitivity\n  knob already partly present in `sightline_sensitivity.py`.\n- **MgII → FRB DM/τ is an unfilled gap in the literature.** The code already\n  predicts MgII W_r and uses it to boost cool DM, but that proxy has **no direct\n  FRB observational validation** anywhere — it is a modeling assumption, and a\n  potential novelty angle if the sample can test it. Flag clearly in any write-up.\n- **Outer-truncation (2·r200) DM sensitivity** is unhandled; Prochaska & Zheng warn\n  it adds tens of pc cm⁻³ at moderate impact.\n- **Citation to verify before publication.** `docs/codetection-science-plan.md:64`\n  cites \"Sammons 2309.07256\" for CGM cloudlet lensing; the prior-art pass confirms\n  arXiv:2309.07256 is the cloudlet refractive-lensing paper but reports its lead\n  author is **not** Sammons. Confirm\nthose IDs against ADS/arXiv before any reach a manuscript.\n\n## Question / Scope\n\nFor each of the 12 CHIME/DSA co-detected FRB sightlines, what foreground galaxies\nand galaxy clusters lie along the line of sight, and what methods does the project\n(and the wider literature) use to search for them? In scope: the production\nforeground-search machinery, the search→DM/scattering-budget chain it feeds, the\nactual per-sightline distributions currently committed, and the prior-art methods\nfor (a) intervening-galaxy identification, (b) cluster-intersection searches, and\n(c) turning a foreground system into a DM/τ contribution. Out of scope: the\nscattering-fit pipeline itself, host-galaxy (z ≥ z_FRB) association, and the\nflux-calibration work on the current branch.\n\nA defining property of the sample shapes everything below: **all 12 sightlines sit\nat declination +70° to +74°** (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:21-34`), a sky region where\nthe standard optical survey footprints (SDSS, and the catalogs built on it) thin\nout or vanish.\n\n## Codebase Findings\n\n### The sample\n12 sightlines, Dec +70° to +74°, z from 0.043 to 0.51, with **three placeholder\nz = 1.0** values (Freya, Mahi, Johndoeii) that flag an unmeasured host redshift\nrather than a real one (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:21-34`,\n`galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:73-81`). Where z is a placeholder the cosmic and\nhost DM terms are withheld rather than fabricated\n(`galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:504-515`).\n\n### Production foreground search (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py`)\n- **Engines / catalogs.** NED cone search (`galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-54`) plus\n  Vizier for GLADE+ (`VII/291`), DESI DR8-North (`VII/292`), and SDSS DR12\n  (`V/147`) (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:37-41`, `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:57-102`).\n  An opt-in DESI DR1 spec-z TAP engine covers only 3/12 targets\n  (Whitney/Phineas/Casey) and is **off by default**\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:218-221`, `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:45,55`). Enricher\n  catalogs (Legacy DR10 tractor, AllWISE, GALEX, 2MASS-XSC) are likewise off by\n  default (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:48-56`, `galaxies/v2_0/enrichers.py`).\n- **Foreground criterion.** A row is foreground if `z < z_FRB + 0.01`, with a\n  photo-z-error-aware relaxation (`z − 2σ_z < z_limit`)\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:56-74`, `config.py:13`).\n- **Impact-parameter cut.** 100 kpc for galaxies, **5 Mpc for clusters**\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-11`, `search.py:71-74`). The query cone is sized to\n  the larger limit and capped at 2° so low-z cluster cones don't time out Vizier\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:15-17`, `search.py:228-234`).\n- **Dedup & photometry backfill.** Cross-catalog duplicates merged by 10″ + scaled\n  Δz, keeping the smaller-photo-z-error / higher-rank source\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:87-149`); PS1 g/i magnitudes backfilled for rows\n  lacking a catalog stellar mass — the only mass route for DESI-photo-z-only\n  galaxies (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:152-201`, `engines.py:109-148`).\n\n### Cluster handling — the main gap\nGalaxy clusters are detected **only** via object-classification strings — NED\n`Type` values `GClstr`/`GGroup`, plus `ClG`/`Cl`/`cluster` — caught by a regex and\nthen granted the 5 Mpc impact threshold (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43,71-74`,\n`engines.py:36-37`). There is **no dedicated cluster-catalog engine** (no WHL,\nredMaPPer, SZ, or X-ray catalog) in the production path. WHL cross-matching exists\n**only in exploratory notebooks** (`galaxies/v2_0/analysis.ipynb` ~46 WHL\nreferences, `notebooks/codetections/interveners.ipynb`), not in `search.py`.\nConsequence: **zero cluster-classified rows appear in any of the nine committed\n`results/*_galaxies.csv`** — the 5 Mpc cluster search returns nothing in practice\nfor this sample. (Prior art below explains why this is expected at Dec > +70.)\n\n### Other (non-production) search methods present in the tree\nThe repo carries three earlier/parallel search methods, useful as a record of\n\"methods tried\":\n- WISE-PS1-STRM + Legacy-DR8 photo-z **beam search** with an impact cut\n  (`galaxies/wise-ps1-strm/wiseps1_beam_search.py`).\n- Tarrío PS1 photo-z **SOV-tile impact matching** + Gaia cross-match over exactly\n  the 12 targets (`galaxies/tarrio_ps1_photz/find_impact_matches.py`).\n- A DESI **DR8 sweep+photo-z stack built specifically for the +70°–+75° Dec strip**\n  (`galaxies/dr8_dec70_75/stack.py`) — a direct adaptation to the sample's\n  high-declination band.\n\n### Search → DM/τ budget chain\nThe found galaxies feed a documented, primary-source-citing physics chain\n(`build_unified.py` → `scattering_predict.py` → `sightline_budget.py`):\n- **Stellar-mass ladder** GLADE → 2MASS-K → DESI-SED → WISE-W1 → PS1-Taylor →\n  assumed 10¹⁰ M⊙ (`galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:26-33,118-155`); Nielsen et al. 2013) (`scattering_predict.py:126-150,321-384`).\n- **Two-phase intervening τ**: smooth hot halo + clumpy cool CGM carrying a\n  fluctuation-parameter boost `COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` (McCourt et al. 2018;\n  Vedantham & Phinney 2019; matches the science plan's \"host\nsearch 9/12\"):\n\n| Sightline | z | N foreground gal. | N clusters | DM_interv (capped) | regime | predicted τ_interv (ms) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Zach | 0.043 | 2 | 0 | 143 | CGM | 0.006 |\n| Whitney | 0.479 | 2 | 0 | 200 | GALAXY_INTERIOR | 0.27 |\n| Oran | 0.300 | 0 | 0 | 0 | none | 0 |\n| Isha | 0.251 | 1 | 0 | 23 | CGM | 0.0015 |\n| Wilhelm | 0.510 | 2 | 0 | 103 | CGM | 0.008 |\n| Phineas | 0.271 | 3 | 0 | 367 | GALAXY_INTERIOR | 1.4 |\n| Freya | 1.000 (placeholder) | 1 | 0 | 5 | CGM | 3.5e-05 |\n| Hamilton | 0.302 | 1 | 0 | 58 | CGM | 0.022 |\n| Mahi | 1.000 (placeholder) | 0 | 0 | 0 | none | 0 |\n| Chromatica | 0.074 | 2 | 0 | 0 | none | 0 |\n| Casey | 0.287 | 0 | 0 | 0 | none | 0 |\n| Johndoeii | 1.000 (placeholder) | 1 | 0 | 213 | GALAXY_INTERIOR | 0.23 |\n\nObservations: (1) **No clusters found on any sightline.** (2) Foreground galaxy\ncounts are low (0–3), consistent with a shallow high-Dec catalog floor.
