(4) **Negative host\nDM** on Zach/Whitney/Wilhelm/Phineas — under-dense sightlines that fall below the\nMacquart cosmic mean (`sightline_budget.py:356-368`), already diagnosed in the\nscience plan as expected scatter, not a bug. (5) The code's own verdict is that\n**predicted intervening τ is negligible everywhere except Phineas (1.4 ms)** — i.e.\nintervening galaxies rarely dominate scattering in this sample.\n\n## Prior Art\n\nExternal pass run via direct arXiv/ar5iv full-text reads and primary-source web\nsearch (the semantic search backend was rate-limited; the sub-agents report that\nevery ID below was verified against the primary source except where flagged\n`[unverified]` in *References*, which only means the local hook could not\nre-confirm offline this session).\n\n### A. Identifying intervening/foreground galaxies along FRB sightlines\n- The standard association cut is **impact parameter b⊥ ≲ r200 with a spec-z**;\n  FLIMFLAM operationalizes this with deep narrow-field spectroscopy of galaxies near\n  the sightline plus wide-field spectroscopy for the larger-scale density field\n  (Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024, FLIMFLAM DR1).\n- **FLIMFLAM is the canonical end-to-end pipeline**: it reconstructs the ~Mpc matter\n  density field along each sightline (Bayesian ARGO reconstruction), associates\n  halos, and fits a DM model with MW/IGM/halo/host terms, then constrains the\n  CGM/IGM baryon partition — f_IGM = 0.59 (+0.11/−0.10), CGM gas fraction f_gas =\n  0.55 (+0.26/−0.29) (Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024; method precursors Simha et\n  al. 2020, 2021; Khrykin et al. 2023).\n- **Baseband/interferometric foreground searches** are the DSA-110 mode: the\n  first DSA-110 FRB+host catalog (Law, Sharma et al. 2023) and the multi-halo burst\n  FRB 20221219A, whose sightline is \"significantly overcrowded\" (CDF ≈ 0.99 vs\n  expected N_halos = 0.18) with two intervening halos identified by optical/IR SED\n  fitting (Connor et al. 2024).\n- **Statistical host/intervener association**: PATH Bayesian framework (Aggarwal et\n  al. 2021), with chance-coincidence sub-samples (Bhandari et al. 2022).\n- The **r200 cut is itself a modeling choice**: Prochaska & Zheng 2019 warn the\n  virial \"edge\" is artificial — integrating to 2·r200 adds tens of pc cm⁻³ at b ≳\n  0.5 r200. The code's behavior here is the inverse problem (it caps at 0.1 R_vir\n  for the inner blow-up) but the outer-truncation sensitivity is unhandled.\n\n### B. Galaxy clusters along sightlines, and high-Dec catalog coverage\n- **Cluster catalogs and their declination reach** (the binding constraint for this\n  sample): WHL (Wen, Han & Liu 2012; update Wen & Han 2015) and redMaPPer (Rykoff et\n  al. 2014) are **SDSS-based and do not cover Dec > +70** (SDSS imaging in the N\n  Galactic Cap ends near +60–65°). SZ catalogs ACT DR5 (Hilton et al. 2021) and\n  SPT-SZ (Bleem et al. 2015), and X-ray eROSITA eRASS1 (Bulbul et al. 2024) are\n  equatorial/southern. **The only catalogs with genuine Dec > +70 coverage are the\n  all-sky ones: Planck PSZ2 (SZ; Planck Collab. 2016) and MCXC / MCXC-II (X-ray\n  RASS-based; Piffaretti et al. 2011; MCXC-II 2024)** — both shallow and\n  mass-limited there, so poor completeness for group-mass systems.\n- **FRBs through clusters give meaningful DM but negligible scattering.** DSA-110\n  FRBs in Abell 2310/2311 contribute ICM DM of 16–568 pc cm⁻³ but show no\n  significant scattering (Connor et al. 2023). FRB 20190520B pierces two foreground\n  clusters (b = 0.39 and 0.77 r200) contributing 450–640 pc cm⁻³ total halo DM, and\n  the authors explicitly argue these clusters do **not** cause the burst's large τ\n  (Lee et al. 2023).\n- **DM vs impact parameter is steep**: ~300 pc cm⁻³ at 0.39 r200 falling to ~110 pc\n  cm⁻³ at 0.77 r200 (Lee et al. 2023). Meaningful cluster DM requires the sightline\n  within ~1–2 r200 (≲ a few Mpc for the most massive clusters); a **5 Mpc impact\n  radius mostly returns negligible-DM near-misses** (this last step is an\n  extrapolation from the observed profiles, not a directly stated literature\n  result).\n- Cluster turbulent ICM can in principle enhance scattering (Zhu, Feng et al. 2018),\n  but geometric leverage for a cosmologically-distant cluster screen drives\n  broadening to ≪ ms — negligible vs FRB τ (Ocker et al. 2022, scattering horizons;\n  secondary).\n\n### C. CGM/halo gas → DM and scattering models\n- **mNFW gas profile** ρ_b(r) ∝ 1/[y^(1−α)(y0+y)^(2+α)], fiducial y0 = α = 2, f_b,halo\n  = 0.75 (Prochaska & Zheng 2019) — **exactly the form the code implements and\n  cites** (`scattering_predict.py:27-123`). FLIMFLAM uses the same form.\n- **Macquart relation** ⟨DM_cosmic⟩ ∝ ∫ f_IGM(1+z)/E(z) dz (Macquart et al. 2020,\n  Nature 581) — the baseline the code uses for cosmic DM\n  (`sightline_budget.py:124-143`).\n- **Geometric leverage**: τ ≈ 48.03 μs · A_τ F̃ DM_ℓ² G_scatt /[(1+z_ℓ)³ ν⁴], with\n  G_scatt = 2 d_sl d_lo /(L d_so) (Ocker, Cordes & Chatterjee 2021). This is the\n  canonical FRB-halo leverage paper; the code cites Macquart & Koay 2013 for the\n  equivalent geometry (`scattering_predict.py:192-217`) and could additionally cite\n  Ocker et al. 2021.\n- **Cool-CGM cloudlet scattering**: foundational model is Vedantham & Phinney 2019\n  on McCourt et al. 2018 \"shattered\" sub-pc cloudlets; refractive cloudlet lensing\n  (Pradeep et al. 2023 — see citation caveat in *Synthesis*). But **CGM cloud-size\n  limits** suggest realistic low-z cool CGM (n_e ≲ 10⁻² cm⁻³) adds little scattering\n  unless clouds are ≲ 0.1 pc (Sammons et al. 2025 / cloud-size limits), and hot-CGM\n  scattering is ≪ 1 μs at 1 GHz (Ocker et al. 2025). The code's\n  `COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` (range 3–30) is therefore an **optimistic** cool-phase\n  prior (`scattering_predict.py:254-262`).\n\n### D. MgII absorbers as intervening cool-gas tracers\n- **No published work ties an individual MgII absorber to a measured FRB DM or τ\n  excess on the same sightline** — this is a genuine gap (a claimed link from a\n  secondary source produced only hallucinated IDs and was discarded). MgII↔cool-CGM\n  baseline relations are quasar-based: W(MgII 2796) declines with impact parameter,\n  high covering fraction within ~100–150 kpc of L* galaxies (MAGIICAT — Nielsen et\n  al. 2013; Lan & Mo 2018) — the relations the code's `predict_mgii_wr` and\n  `cool_covering_fraction` encode (`scattering_predict.py:321-384`). MgII in\n  groups/clusters: Anand et al. 2022. The DSA multi-halo burst uses COS-Halos\n  N_HII(b,M⋆) — the same cool photoionized phase MgII traces — as its DM_igh\n  template (Connor et al. 2024).\n\n### E. Disconfirming evidence & limitations\n- **Scattering is usually host/Milky-Way-dominated, not foreground-dominated.**\n  Halos contribute to DM \"but evidently not to scattering, which is dominated by\n  host galaxies\" (Cordes et al. 2022); measured intervening-halo τ is negligible for\n  FRB 181112/191108 (Ocker et al. 2021); FRB 20190520B is explicitly host-dominated\n  (Ocker et al. 2022, host-dominated); CHIME population modeling concurs (Chawla et\n  al. 2025 / CHIME population). **Counterpoint:** the DSA multi-halo burst FRB\n  20221219A is *not* host-dominated — an overcrowded intervening sightline can\n  dominate (Connor et al. 2024). That is precisely the regime the co-detection\n  sample is built to probe.\n- **High-Dec photo-z incompleteness / catalog depth.** DESI Legacy photo-z degrade\n  where spec-z training is sparse — directly the Dec > +70 case (Duncan 2022; Zhou\n  et al. 2021; SOM photo-z analyses). A Rubin-era forecast finds the dominant error\n  is **missing dim/high-z hosts** (catalog depth), degrading inferences ~47–62%, far\n  more than photo-z scatter (~7%) (Rubin-era FRB photo-z forecast). SDSS\n  spectroscopy largely excludes Dec > +70; GLADE+ is shallow; PS1 lacks\n  spectroscopy — so the project's high-Dec search is photometry-limited and\n  spec-z-starved. No paper quantifies FRB-foreground completeness specifically at\n  Dec > +70 (gap).\n- **False-association risk.** PATH quantifies chance coincidence (Aggarwal et al.\n  2021); host association degrades once σ_loc ≳ 2″ (localization-precision bias\n  study), so large-impact foreground association under coarse localization or\n  photo-z-only redshifts is fragile. Radio selection (high-DM/low-scattering) skews\n  the sample and biases foreground-incidence statistics (Seebeck, Shannon et al.\n  2021). No FRB-specific paper gives a contamination number for intervening (vs\n  host) association under photo-z only (gap).\n\n## Synthesis\n\n**The code implements a defensible, literature-grounded version of the standard\nmethod, but a deliberately simplified one.** Its impact-parameter + (photo-z or\nspec-z) cone search, mNFW halo DM, Macquart cosmic baseline, two-phase cool/hot\nscreen, and geometric leverage all map directly onto the canonical references\n(Prochaska & Zheng 2019, Macquart et al. 2020, Ocker et al. 2021, FLIMFLAM), and\nthe modules cite them inline. What it does **not** do — and what FLIMFLAM does — is\nreconstruct the Mpc-scale density field or jointly fit the baryon partition; the\ncode instead attributes per-halo columns deterministically and brackets the\nnuisance astrophysics with a prior-predictive sensitivity layer. That is an\nappropriate scope choice for a 12-sightline study, not a defect.\n\n**The external consensus validates the code's central scientific verdict.** Across\nCordes et al. 2022, Ocker et al. 2021/2022, and CHIME population work, intervening\nhalos add DM but rarely scattering — exactly what the budget table reports\n(predicted τ_interv negligible everywhere except Phineas). The one regime where this\nflips — overcrowded sightlines (Connor et al. 2024) — is the regime this sample\ntargets, so the scientific payoff lives in the tail, and Phineas (3 foreground\ngalaxies, GALAXY_INTERIOR, τ_interv = 1.4 ms) is the natural first case to\nscrutinize.\n\n**The cluster search is the clearest weakness, and prior art explains why.**\nClusters are found only by NED object-type strings with a 5 Mpc impact, and **zero\nclusters turn up** on any sightline. Two independent reasons: (1) at Dec +70°–74°,\nthe SDSS-based cluster catalogs (WHL, redMaPPer) have no coverage, and even the\nnotebook WHL cross-match cannot help there — only all-sky Planck PSZ2 and\nMCXC/MCXC-II reach the band, both shallow; (2) a 5 Mpc impact mostly yields\nnegligible-DM near-misses, because meaningful cluster DM needs the sightline within\n~1–2 r200, and clusters contribute essentially no scattering at any impact (Connor\net al. 2023, Lee et al. 2023). So the current cluster machinery is both\nunder-powered (wrong catalogs for this sky) and aimed at a low-yield regime.\n\n### Gaps and open questions\n- **Cluster catalog coverage at Dec > +70.** If clusters matter, the production\n  search needs an all-sky catalog engine (Planck PSZ2 and/or MCXC-II), not NED-type\n  strings — and the 5 Mpc radius should be re-examined against an r200-relative\n  criterion. *(Light recommendation; design deferred to planning.)*\n- **`COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` is optimistic.** Recent cloud-size/turbulence limits\n  (Ocker et al. 2025; cloud-size-limits study) push the realistic cool-CGM\n  scattering contribution down; the lo bound (3) may be closer to reality. Worth a\n  sensitivity knob already partly present in `sightline_sensitivity.py`.\n- **MgII → FRB DM/τ is an unfilled gap in the literature.** The code already\n  predicts MgII W_r and uses it to boost cool DM, but that proxy has **no direct\n  FRB observational validation** anywhere — it is a modeling assumption, and a\n  potential novelty angle if the sample can test it. Flag clearly in any write-up.\n- **Outer-truncation (2·r200) DM sensitivity** is unhandled; Prochaska & Zheng warn\n  it adds tens of pc cm⁻³ at moderate impact.\n- **Citation to verify before publication.** `docs/codetection-science-plan.md:64`\n  cites \"Sammons 2309.07256\" for CGM cloudlet lensing; the prior-art pass reports\n  arXiv:2309.07256 is the cloudlet refractive-lensing paper but that its lead author\n  is **not** Sammons (a separate Sammons et al. FRB-scattering paper may exist).\n  Re-check the author/ID pairing via an ADS author search before this citation\n  reaches a manuscript. *(Left in place pending confirmation; not silently edited\n  because the correct attribution was not established this pass.)*\n\n## References / Sources\n\n### Code (commit `8ca87f7`)\n- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-17,21-56` — targets, catalogs, impact/redshift defaults\n- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43,56-74,87-201,204-332` — cluster regex, foreground\n  mask, dedup, PS1 backfill, search driver\n- `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-148` — NED / Vizier / PS1 engines\n- `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py` — opt-in DESI DR1 spec-z engine\n- `galaxies/v2_0/enrichers.py` — opt-in cross-survey enrichment\n- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:26-33,118-155,246-474` — mass ladder, per-galaxy\n  CGM record assembly\n- `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:27-385` — mNFW DM, cool DM, MgII W_r,\n  covering fraction, two-phase τ, g_scatt\n- `galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:71-143,340-608` — DM/τ budget closure, caps,\n  verdicts\n- `galaxies/v2_0/sightline_sensitivity.py` — prior-predictive sensitivity layer\n- `galaxies/wise-ps1-strm/wiseps1_beam_search.py`,\n  `galaxies/tarrio_ps1_photz/find_impact_matches.py`,\n  `galaxies/dr8_dec70_75/stack.py` — non-production / earlier search methods\n- `notebooks/codetections/interveners.ipynb`, `galaxies/v2_0/analysis.ipynb` —\n  exploratory WHL cluster cross-match (notebook-only)\n- `results/search_summary.csv`, `results/sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md`,\n  `results/*_galaxies.csv` — committed per-sightline outputs\n\n### External (arXiv IDs; `[unverified]` = sub-agent-reported but not re-confirmed by the local hook offline this session)\n- Prochaska & Zheng 2019, mNFW halo gas/DM — arXiv:1901.11051\n- Macquart et al. 2020, Nature 581, Macquart relation — arXiv:2005.13161\n- Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024, FLIMFLAM DR1 — arXiv:2402.00505\n- Khrykin et al. 2023, FLIMFLAM excess-DM — arXiv:2303.07387\n- Simha et al. 2020 (FRB 190608) — arXiv:2005.13157; Simha et al. 2021 (FRB 180924) — arXiv:2108.09881\n- Ocker, Cordes & Chatterjee 2021, halo scattering + G_scatt — arXiv:2101.04784 [unverified]\n- Cordes et al. 2022, DM/τ, host-dominated scattering — arXiv:2108.01172 [unverified]; see Synthesis)\n- Ocker et al. 2025, CGM turbulence microphysics — arXiv:2503.02329 [unverified]\n- CGM cloud-size limits — arXiv:2504.19562 [unverified]\n- Ocker et al. 2022, radio scattering horizons — arXiv:2203.16716\n- Connor et al. 2023, DSA-110 FRBs in clusters (ICM DM + RM) — arXiv:2302.14788\n- Lee et al. 2023, FRB 20190520B through 2 foreground clusters — arXiv:2306.05403\n- Ocker et al. 2022, FRB 20190520B host-dominated — arXiv:2202.13458 [unverified]\n- Connor et al. 2024, DSA-110 multi-halo FRB 20221219A — arXiv:2405.14182\n- Law, Sharma et al. 2023, DSA-110 first FRB+host catalog — arXiv:2307.03344\n- Aggarwal et al. 2021, PATH — arXiv:2102.10627;   "content": "# Research: Foreground galaxy & galaxy-cluster distributions along the co-detected sightlines, and the methods used to search for them\n\n**Date:** 2026-06-23\n**Scope:** both internal codebase and external prior art\n**Codebase state researched against:** commit `8ca87f7`, 2026-06-23 (branch `feature/radiometer-flux-cal`)\n**Related Documents:**\n- `docs/codetection-science-plan.md` (the parent science plan; §B/§D ground this question)\n- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-19-sightline-budget-sensitivity.md`\n- `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/0001-two-band-leverage-positioning.md`\n\n**Citation note:** inline references use author-year; full arXiv IDs are in\n*References* below. IDs marked `[unverified]` there were reported as\nread/verified by the prior-art sub-agents but could **not** be re-confirmed by the\nlocal citation-check hook this session (network unreachable, no cache). Confirm\nthose IDs against ADS/arXiv before any reach a manuscript.\n\n## Question / Scope\n\nFor each of the 12 CHIME/DSA co-detected FRB sightlines, what foreground galaxies\nand galaxy clusters lie along the line of sight, and what methods does the project\n(and the wider literature) use to search for them? In scope: the production\nforeground-search machinery, the search→DM/scattering-budget chain it feeds, the\nactual per-sightline distributions currently committed, and the prior-art methods\nfor (a) intervening-galaxy identification, (b) cluster-intersection searches, and\n(c) turning a foreground system into a DM/τ contribution. Out of scope: the\nscattering-fit pipeline itself, host-galaxy (z ≥ z_FRB) association, and the\nflux-calibration work on the current branch.\n\nA defining property of the sample shapes everything below: **all 12 sightlines sit\nat declination +70° to +74°** (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:21-34`), a sky region where\nthe standard optical survey footprints (SDSS, and the catalogs built on it) thin\nout or vanish.\n\n## Codebase Findings\n\n### The sample\n12 sightlines, Dec +70° to +74°, z from 0.043 to 0.51, with **three placeholder\nz = 1.0** values (Freya, Mahi, Johndoeii) that flag an unmeasured host redshift\nrather than a real one (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:21-34`,\n`galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:73-81`). Where z is a placeholder the cosmic and\nhost DM terms are withheld rather than fabricated\n(`galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:504-515`).\n\n### Production foreground search (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py`)\n- **Engines / catalogs.** NED cone search (`galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-54`) plus\n  Vizier for GLADE+ (`VII/291`), DESI DR8-North (`VII/292`), and SDSS DR12\n  (`V/147`) (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:37-41`, `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:57-102`).\n  An opt-in DESI DR1 spec-z TAP engine covers only 3/12 targets\n  (Whitney/Phineas/Casey) and is **off by default**\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:218-221`, `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:45,55`). Enricher\n  catalogs (Legacy DR10 tractor, AllWISE, GALEX, 2MASS-XSC) are likewise off by\n  default (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:48-56`, `galaxies/v2_0/enrichers.py`).\n- **Foreground criterion.** A row is foreground if `z < z_FRB + 0.01`, with a\n  photo-z-error-aware relaxation (`z − 2σ_z < z_limit`)\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:56-74`, `config.py:13`).\n- **Impact-parameter cut.** 100 kpc for galaxies, **5 Mpc for clusters**\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-11`, `search.py:71-74`). The query cone is sized to\n  the larger limit and capped at 2° so low-z cluster cones don't time out Vizier\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/config.py:15-17`, `search.py:228-234`).\n- **Dedup & photometry backfill.** Cross-catalog duplicates merged by 10″ + scaled\n  Δz, keeping the smaller-photo-z-error / higher-rank source\n  (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:87-149`); PS1 g/i magnitudes backfilled for rows\n  lacking a catalog stellar mass — the only mass route for DESI-photo-z-only\n  galaxies (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:152-201`, `engines.py:109-148`).\n\n### Cluster handling — the main gap\nGalaxy clusters are detected **only** via object-classification strings — NED\n`Type` values `GClstr`/`GGroup`, plus `ClG`/`Cl`/`cluster` — caught by a regex and\nthen granted the 5 Mpc impact threshold (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43,71-74`,\n`engines.py:36-37`). There is **no dedicated cluster-catalog engine** (no WHL,\nredMaPPer, SZ, or X-ray catalog) in the production path. WHL cross-matching exists\n**only in exploratory notebooks** (`galaxies/v2_0/analysis.ipynb` ~46 WHL\nreferences, `notebooks/codetections/interveners.ipynb`), not in `search.py`.\nConsequence: **zero cluster-classified rows appear in any of the nine committed\n`results/*_galaxies.csv`** — the 5 Mpc cluster search returns nothing in practice\nfor this sample. (Prior art below explains why this is expected at Dec > +70.)\n\n### Other (non-production) search methods present in the tree\nThe repo carries three earlier/parallel search methods, useful as a record of\n\"methods tried\":\n- WISE-PS1-STRM + Legacy-DR8 photo-z **beam search** with an impact cut\n  (`galaxies/wise-ps1-strm/wiseps1_beam_search.py`).\n- Tarrío PS1 photo-z **SOV-tile impact matching** + Gaia cross-match over exactly\n  the 12 targets (`galaxies/tarrio_ps1_photz/find_impact_matches.py`).\n- A DESI **DR8 sweep+photo-z stack built specifically for the +70°–+75° Dec strip**\n  (`galaxies/dr8_dec70_75/stack.py`) — a direct adaptation to the sample's\n  high-declination band.\n\n### Search → DM/τ budget chain\nThe found galaxies feed a documented, primary-source-citing physics chain\n(`build_unified.py` → `scattering_predict.py` → `sightline_budget.py`):\n- **Stellar-mass ladder** GLADE → 2MASS-K → DESI-SED → WISE-W1 → PS1-Taylor →\n  assumed 10¹⁰ M⊙ (`galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:26-33,118-155`); Identifying intervening/foreground galaxies along FRB sightlines\n- The standard association cut is **impact parameter b⊥ ≲ r200 with a spec-z**;\n  FLIMFLAM operationalizes this with deep narrow-field spectroscopy of galaxies near\n  the sightline plus wide-field spectroscopy for the larger-scale density field\n  (Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024, FLIMFLAM DR1).\n- **FLIMFLAM is the canonical end-to-end pipeline**: it reconstructs the ~Mpc matter\n  density field along each sightline (Bayesian ARGO reconstruction), associates\n  halos, and fits a DM model with MW/IGM/halo/host terms, then constrains the\n  CGM/IGM baryon partition — f_IGM = 0.59 (+0.11/−0.10), CGM gas fraction f_gas =\n  0.55 (+0.26/−0.29) (Khrykin, Lee, Simha et al. 2024; method precursors Simha et\n  al. 2020, 2021; Khrykin et al. 2023).\n- **Baseband/interferometric foreground searches** are the DSA-110 mode: the\n  first DSA-110 FRB+host catalog (Law, Sharma et al. 2023) and the multi-halo burst\n  FRB 20221219A, whose sightline is \"significantly overcrowded\" (CDF ≈ 0.99 vs\n  expected N_halos = 0.18) with two intervening halos identified by optical/IR SED\n  fitting (Connor et al. 2024).\n- **Statistical host/intervener association**: PATH Bayesian framework (Aggarwal et\n  al. 2021), with chance-coincidence sub-samples (Bhandari et al. 2022).\n- The **r200 cut is itself a modeling choice**: Prochaska & Zheng 2019 warn the\n  virial \"edge\" is artificial — integrating to 2·r200 adds tens of pc cm⁻³ at b ≳\n  0.5 r200. The code's behavior here is the inverse problem (it caps at 0.1 R_vir\n  for the inner blow-up) but the outer-truncation sensitivity is unhandled.\n\n### B. Galaxy clusters along sightlines, and high-Dec catalog coverage\n- **Cluster catalogs and their declination reach** (the binding constraint for this\n  sample): WHL (Wen, Han & Liu 2012; update Wen & Han 2015) and redMaPPer (Rykoff et\n  al. 2014) are **SDSS-based and do not cover Dec > +70** (SDSS imaging in the N\n  Galactic Cap ends near +60–65°). SZ catalogs ACT DR5 (Hilton et al. 2021) and\n  SPT-SZ (Bleem et al. 2015), and X-ray eROSITA eRASS1 (Bulbul et al. 2024) are\n  equatorial/southern. **The only catalogs with genuine Dec > +70 coverage are the\n  all-sky ones: Planck PSZ2 (SZ; Planck Collab. 2016) and MCXC / MCXC-II (X-ray\n  RASS-based; Piffaretti et al. 2011; MCXC-II 2024)** — both shallow and\n  mass-limited there, so poor completeness for group-mass systems.\n- **FRBs through clusters give meaningful DM but negligible scattering.** DSA-110\n  FRBs in Abell 2310/2311 contribute ICM DM of 16–568 pc cm⁻³ but show no\n  significant scattering (Connor et al. 2023). FRB 20190520B pierces two foreground\n  clusters (b = 0.39 and 0.77 r200) contributing 450–640 pc cm⁻³ total halo DM, and\n  the authors explicitly argue these clusters do **not** cause the burst's large τ\n  (Lee et al. 2023).\n- **DM vs impact parameter is steep**: ~300 pc cm⁻³ at 0.39 r200 falling to ~110 pc\n  cm⁻³ at 0.77 r200 (Lee et al. 2023). Meaningful cluster DM requires the sightline\n  within ~1–2 r200 (≲ a few Mpc for the most massive clusters); a **5 Mpc impact\n  radius mostly returns negligible-DM near-misses** (this last step is an\n  extrapolation from the observed profiles, not a directly stated literature\n  result).\n- Cluster turbulent ICM can in principle enhance scattering (Zhu, Feng et al. 2018),\n  but geometric leverage for a cosmologically-distant cluster screen drives\n  broadening to ≪ ms — negligible vs FRB τ (Ocker et al. 2022, scattering horizons;\n  secondary).\n\n### C. CGM/halo gas → DM and scattering models\n- **mNFW gas profile** ρ_b(r) ∝ 1/[y^(1−α)(y0+y)^(2+α)], fiducial y0 = α = 2, f_b,halo\n  = 0.75 (Prochaska & Zheng 2019) — **exactly the form the code implements and\n  cites** (`scattering_predict.py:27-123`). FLIMFLAM uses the same form.\n- **Macquart relation** ⟨DM_cosmic⟩ ∝ ∫ f_IGM(1+z)/E(z) dz (Macquart et al. 2020,\n  Nature 581) — the baseline the code uses for cosmic DM\n  (`sightline_budget.py:124-143`).\n- **Geometric leverage**: τ ≈ 48.03 μs · A_τ F̃ DM_ℓ² G_scatt /[(1+z_ℓ)³ ν⁴], with\n  G_scatt = 2 d_sl d_lo /(L d_so) (Ocker, Cordes & Chatterjee 2021). This is the\n  canonical FRB-halo leverage paper; the code cites Macquart & Koay 2013 for the\n  equivalent geometry (`scattering_predict.py:192-217`) and could additionally cite\n  Ocker et al. 2021.\n- **Cool-CGM cloudlet scattering**: foundational model is Vedantham & Phinney 2019\n  on McCourt et al. 2018 \"shattered\" sub-pc cloudlets; plus a refractive cloudlet\n  lensing paper (see citation caveat in *Synthesis*). But **CGM cloud-size limits**\n  suggest realistic low-z cool CGM (n_e ≲ 10⁻² cm⁻³) adds little scattering unless\n  clouds are ≲ 0.1 pc (cloud-size-limits study), and hot-CGM scattering is ≪ 1 μs at\n  1 GHz (Ocker et al. 2025). The code's `COOL_CLUMP_BOOST = 10` (range 3–30) is\n  therefore an **optimistic** cool-phase prior (`scattering_predict.py:254-262`).\n\n### D. MgII in\n  groups/clusters: Anand et al. 2022. The DSA multi-halo burst uses COS-Halos\n  N_HII(b,M⋆) — the same cool photoionized phase MgII traces — as its DM_igh\n  template (Connor et al. 2024).\n\n### E. Disconfirming evidence & limitations\n- **Scattering is usually host/Milky-Way-dominated, not foreground-dominated.**\n  Halos contribute to DM \"but evidently not to scattering, which is dominated by\n  host galaxies\" (Cordes et al. 2022); measured intervening-halo τ is negligible for\n  FRB 181112/191108 (Ocker et al. 2021); FRB 20190520B is explicitly host-dominated\n  (Ocker et al. 2022, host-dominated); CHIME population modeling concurs (CHIME\n  population study). **Counterpoint:** the DSA multi-halo burst FRB 20221219A is\n  *not* host-dominated — an overcrowded intervening sightline can dominate (Connor et\n  al. 2024). That is precisely the regime the co-detection sample is built to probe.\n- **High-Dec photo-z incompleteness / catalog depth.** DESI Legacy photo-z degrade\n  where spec-z training is sparse — directly the Dec > +70 case (Duncan 2022; Zhou\n  et al. 2021; SOM photo-z analyses). A Rubin-era forecast finds the dominant error\n  is **missing dim/high-z hosts** (catalog depth), degrading inferences ~47–62%, far\n  more than photo-z scatter (~7%) (Rubin-era FRB photo-z forecast). SDSS\n  spectroscopy largely excludes Dec > +70; GLADE+ is shallow; PS1 lacks\n  spectroscopy — so the project's high-Dec search is photometry-limited and\n  spec-z-starved. No paper quantifies FRB-foreground completeness specifically at\n  Dec > +70 (gap).\n- **False-association risk.** PATH quantifies chance coincidence (Aggarwal et al.\n  2021); host association degrades once σ_loc ≳ 2″ (localization-precision bias\n  study), so large-impact foreground association under coarse localization or\n  photo-z-only redshifts is fragile. Radio selection (high-DM/low-scattering) skews\n  the sample and biases foreground-incidence statistics (Seebeck, Shannon et al.\n  2021). 13	
14	
15	def _mask_sentinels(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
16	    """Convert survey sentinel values to NaN without changing nonnumeric fields."""
17	    if df.empty:
18	        return df
19	    return df.replace(-9999, np.nan)
20	
21	
22	def _tap_search_to_dataframe(tap_url: str, adql: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
23	    svc = pyvo.dal.TAPService(tap_url)
24	    table = svc.search(adql).to_table()
25	    return _mask_sentinels(table.to_pandas())
26	
27	
28	def _ensure_standard_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, catalog: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
29	    df = df.copy()
30	    for column in ["ra", "dec", "z"]:
31	        if column not in df.columns:
32	            df[column] = np.nan
33	    df["catalog"] = catalog
34	    return df
35	
36	
37	def _tap_box_query(
38	    tap_url,
39	    table,
40	    coord,
41	    radius,
42	    columns,
43	    where=None,
44	    ra_col="ra",
45	    dec_col="dec",
46	) -> pd.DataFrame:
47	    """Query Data Lab TAP with a box prefilter, then enforce a true sky circle.
48	
49	    NOIRLab Astro Data Lab rejects ADQL geometry functions for these tables
50	    ("function point does not exist"), so use a portable RA/Dec BETWEEN box and
51	    perform the physically correct circular cut with Astropy on the client side.
52	    """
53	    try:
54	        radius_deg = radius.to(u.deg).value
55	        ra0 = coord.ra.deg
56	        dec0 = coord.dec.deg
57	        ddec = radius_deg
58	        cos_dec = max(abs(np.cos(np.radians(dec0))), 1.0e-6)
59	        dra = radius_deg / cos_dec
60	
61	        predicates = [
62	            f"{dec_col} BETWEEN {dec0 - ddec:.12g} AND {dec0 + ddec:.12g}",
63	            f"{ra_col} BETWEEN {ra0 - dra:.12g} AND {ra0 + dra:.12g}",
64	        ]
65	        if where is not None:
66	            predicates.append(f"({where})")
67	
68	        adql = (
69	            f"SELECT {', '.join(columns)} "
70	            f"FROM {table} "
71	            f"WHERE {' AND '.join(predicates)}"
72	        )
73	        df = _tap_search_to_dataframe(tap_url, adql)
74	        if df.empty:
75	            return pd.DataFrame()
76	
77	        matches = SkyCoord(df[ra_col].to_numpy() * u.deg, df[dec_col].to_numpy() * u.deg)
78	        df = df.loc[coord.separation(matches) <= radius].copy()
79	        if df.empty:
80	            return pd.DataFrame()
81	        return df.rename(columns={ra_col: "ra", dec_col: "dec"})
82	    except Exception:
83	        return pd.DataFrame()
84	
85

89	        self.require_primary = require_primary
90	
91	    def query(self, coord, radius) -> pd.DataFrame:
92	        columns = [
93	            "mean_fiber_ra",
94	            "mean_fiber_dec",
95	            "z",
96	            "zerr",
97	            "zwarn",
98	            "spectype",
99	            "deltachi2",
100	            "targetid",
101	            "zcat_primary",
102	        ]
103	        where = "zcat_primary='true' AND zwarn=0" if self.require_primary else "zwarn=0"
104	        df = _tap_box_query(
105	            self.tap_url,
106	            "desi_dr1.zpix",
107	            coord,
108	            radius,
109	            columns,
110	            where=where,
111	            ra_col="mean_fiber_ra",
112	            dec_col="mean_fiber_dec",
113	        )
114	        if df.empty:
115	            return pd.DataFrame()
116	
117	        return _ensure_standard_columns(df, "DESI_DR1")
118	
119	    def query_emfit(self, targetids) -> pd.DataFrame:
120	        return self._query_targetid_table("desi_dr1.emfit", targetids)
121	
122	    def query_agngal(self, targetids) -> pd.DataFrame:
123	        return self._query_targetid_table("desi_dr1.agngal", targetids)
124	
125	    def _query_targetid_table(self, table, targetids) -> pd.DataFrame:
126	        ids = [int(targetid) for targetid in targetids]
127	        if not ids:
128	            return pd.DataFrame()
129	
130	        try:
131	            adql = f"SELECT * FROM {table} WHERE targetid IN ({', '.join(map(str, ids))})"
132	            return _tap_search_to_dataframe(self.tap_url, adql)
133	        except Exception:
134	            return pd.DataFrame()

1	"""Utility functions for galaxy search v2.0."""
2	
3	import numpy as np
4	from astropy import units as u
5	from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord
6	from .config import COSMO
7	
8	def get_angular_radius(z: float, impact_kpc: float) -> u.Quantity:
9	    """Calculate angular radius for a given physical impact parameter at redshift z."""
10	    if z <= 0:
11	        return 0.0 * u.arcmin
12	    
13	    d_a = COSMO.angular_diameter_distance(z)
14	    with u.set_enabled_equivalencies(u.dimensionless_angles()):
15	        theta_rad = (impact_kpc * u.kpc / d_a).to(u.rad)
16	    return theta_rad.to(u.arcmin)
17	
18	def calculate_impact_parameter(
19	    ra_gal: float, 
20	    dec_gal: float, 
21	    z_gal: float, 
22	    ra_sight: float, 
23	    dec_sight: float
24	) -> float:
25	    """Calculate physical impact parameter in kpc."""
26	    if z_gal <= 0:
27	        return np.nan
28	        
29	    c_sight = SkyCoord(ra_sight, dec_sight, unit='deg', frame='icrs')
30	    c_gal = SkyCoord(ra_gal, dec_gal, unit='deg', frame='icrs')
31	    sep = c_sight.separation(c_gal)
32	    
33	    d_a = COSMO.angular_diameter_distance(z_gal)
34	    impact_kpc = (sep.radian * d_a).to(u.kpc).value
35	    return impact_kpc
36	
37	def parse_coord(ra_str: str, dec_str: str) -> SkyCoord:
38	    """Parse RA/Dec strings into a SkyCoord object."""
39	    return SkyCoord(ra_str, dec_str, frame='icrs')
40

def estimate_halo_mass(log_mstar):
    """Halo mass from stellar mass via the Moster+2013 (Eq. 2) SMHM relation.

    M*(M_h) is monotonic in M_h over the plotted range, so we invert Eq. 2
    numerically with brentq rather than using a sinh fitting form. Bracket
    spans dwarf to cluster halos (log M_h in [9.5, 15.5]).
    """
    log_mh = brentq(lambda lmh: _moster_log_mstar(lmh) - log_mstar, 9.5, 15.5)
    return 10 ** log_mh


def get_rvir_and_rs(m_halo_msun, z):
=== get_rvir_and_rs body ===
def get_rvir_and_rs(m_halo_msun, z):
    """R_200 and NFW scale radius r_s in kpc."""
    M_h = m_halo_msun * u.Msun
    H_z = cosmo.H(z)
    G = const.G
    r_vir = ((G * M_h / (100 * H_z**2))**(1/3)).to(u.kpc).value
    # Dutton & Maccio 2014 (MNRAS 441, 3359) c-M relation at z=0.
    log_c = 0.905 - 0.101 * np.log10(m_halo_msun / 1e12)
    # First-order redshift evolution (concentration declines with z); D&M14
    # give d(log c)/dz ~ -0.08 over the low-z regime probed here.
    log_c *= (1.0 - 0.08 * z)
    c = 10**log_c
    r_s = r_vir / c
    return r_vir, r_s, c
```

import sys
import os
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord

# Add project root to sys.path
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

from galaxies.v2_0.config import TARGETS, VIZIER_CATALOGS
from galaxies.v2_0.utils import parse_coord, get_angular_radius
from galaxies.v2_0.engines import NedEngine, VizierEngine

def test_engines():
    # Test with M31 (Andromeda) to verify engines are working
    coord = SkyCoord(10.6847, 41.2687, unit='deg', frame='icrs')
    radius = 10.0 * u.arcmin
    
    print(f"Testing M31 with {radius} radius")
    
    ned = NedEngine()
    ned_df = ned.query(coord, radius)
    print(f"NED returned {len(ned_df)} rows")
    
    # Try AllWISE as a fallback/test
    wise = VizierEngine("II/328/allwise")
    wise_df = wise.query(coord, radius)
    print(f"AllWISE returned {len(wise_df)} rows")
    if not wise_df.empty:
        print("AllWISE columns:", wise_df.columns.tolist())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_engines()

=== test_search_pipeline.py (how search/_foreground_mask tested) ===
import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from galaxies.v2_0 import search as search_mod
from galaxies.v2_0.config import COSMO
from galaxies.v2_0.engines import _add_desi_stellar_mass
from galaxies.v2_0.search import (
    _deduplicate_matches,
    _enrich_with_ps1_photometry,
    _foreground_mask,
)


def test_foreground_mask_uses_two_sigma_photo_z_error():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "z": [0.545, 0.610, 0.545],
            "z_phot_err": [0.057, 0.057, math.nan],
            "impact_kpc": [50.0, 50.0, 50.0],
        }
    )

    mask = _foreground_mask(df, z_frb=0.479, z_eps=0.01, impact_kpc=100.0)

    assert mask.tolist() == [True, False, False]


def test_foreground_mask_applies_cluster_impact_threshold():
    # Same impact (1000 kpc): a galaxy is rejected (>100 kpc) but a cluster is
    # kept (<5000 kpc). Cluster flagged via NED 'GClstr' / SDSS 'ClG' classifications.
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "z": [0.10, 0.10, 0.10],
            "impact_kpc": [1000.0, 1000.0, 1000.0],
            "classification": ["G", "GClstr", "ClG"],
        }
    )

    mask = _foreground_mask(
        df, z_frb=0.479, z_eps=0.01, impact_kpc=100.0, cluster_impact_kpc=5000.0
    )

    assert mask.tolist() == [False, True, True]


def test_deduplicate_matches_requires_close_redshift_and_prefers_better_source():
    matches = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "name": ["desi_photo", "ned_spec", "high_z_pair"],
            "ra": [10.0, 10.0 + 1.0 / 3600.0, 10.0 + 2.0 / 3600.0],
            "dec": [20.0, 20.0, 20.0],
            "z": [0.300, 0.301, 0.420],
            "z_phot_err": [0.05, math.nan, 0.05],
            "catalog": ["VII/292/north", "NED", "VII/292/north"],
        }
    )

    deduped = _deduplicate_matches(matches)

    assert deduped["name"].tolist() == ["ned_spec", "high_z_pair"]


def test_deduplicate_matches_prefers_smaller_redshift_error():
    matches = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "name": ["large_error", "small_error"],
            "ra": [10.0, 10.0 + 1.0 / 3600.0],
            "dec": [20.0, 20.0],
            "z": [0.300, 0.301],
            "z_phot_err": [0.05, 0.01],
            "catalog": ["VII/292/north", "VII/292/north"],
        }
    )

    deduped = _deduplicate_matches(matches)

    assert deduped["name"].tolist() == ["small_error"]

  "content": "# Implementation Plan: All-sky galaxy-cluster engine + r200-relative impact cut\n\n---\n**Date:** 2026-06-23\n**Author:** AI Assistant\n**Status:** Draft\n**Related Documents:**\n- [Research: Foreground galaxy & galaxy-cluster distributions along the co-detected sightlines](research-foreground-galaxies-sightlines.md)\n- [CHIME/DSA Co-detection Science Plan](../../codetection-science-plan.md)\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nThe foreground-search pipeline (`galaxies/v2_0/`) currently detects galaxy\nclusters **only** by NED object-type strings (`GClstr`/`GGroup`/`ClG`) and applies\na flat 5 Mpc impact cut. The research pass found this yields **zero clusters** on\nall 12 sightlines, for two independent reasons: (1) at the sample's declination\n(+70° to +74°) the SDSS-based cluster catalogs (WHL, redMaPPer) have no coverage —\nonly all-sky catalogs reach the band; (2) a fixed 5 Mpc cut is mass-blind, so it\nmostly admits negligible-DM near-misses while a real DM contribution needs the\nsightline within ~1–2 r200 of the cluster.\n\nThis plan adds an **all-sky cluster-catalog engine** (Planck PSZ2 + MCXC +\nMCXC-II, queried through Vizier) that supplies each cluster's redshift and M500\nmass, replaces the flat 5 Mpc cut with a **mass-scaled r200-relative criterion**\n(keep within 2·r200), turns an intersected cluster's ICM into a dispersion-measure\ncontribution with a **β-model electron-density profile** anchored to the catalog\nmass, and integrates that cluster DM into the existing per-sightline budget. Per\nthe literature, clusters contribute DM but negligible scattering, so cluster τ is\nset to zero.\n\n**Goal:** the production search finds the real foreground clusters along each\nsightline (where any exist), assigns each a physically-scaled impact criterion,\nand folds a defensible cluster ICM DM into `sightline_dm_scattering_budget`.\n\n**Motivation:** sightline attribution (CGM/groups/clusters of the intervening\nsystems) is a headline science goal; the current cluster path is both\nunder-powered (wrong catalogs for this sky) and aimed at a low-yield regime.\n\n## Current State Analysis\n\n**Existing Implementation:**\n- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-17` — `DEFAULT_IMPACT_KPC=100`,\n  `DEFAULT_CLUSTER_IMPACT_KPC=5000.0` (flat 5 Mpc), cone caps.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:37-56` — `VIZIER_CATALOGS`, opt-in engine/enricher flags.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43` — `_CLUSTER_RE` + `_cluster_mask` (classification-string detection).\n- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:56-74` — `_foreground_mask`: per-row impact limit, cluster rows get the flat `cluster_impact_kpc`.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:215-234` — engine list assembly + cone sizing from `max(impact_kpc, cluster_impact_kpc)`.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-102` — `NedEngine`, `VizierEngine` (standardize ra/dec/z + `catalog` tag).\n- `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-221` — thin Vizier-wrapper engine pattern (`AllWiseEngine`, `XscEngine`).\n- `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:27-123` — `dm_halo_mnfw` (mNFW hot-halo DM via `scipy.quad`; the style to mirror for the β-model).\n- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:118-155` — `select_stellar_mass` ladder; `:266-277` — `m_halo = estimate_halo_mass(logm_best)` then `get_rvir_and_rs`.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:338-403` — per-galaxy cool-CGM/MgII/two-phase-τ derivation.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/generate_galaxy_plots.py:65` — `get_rvir_and_rs(m,z)` returns R200 (= `(G·M/(100 H_z²))^{1/3}`).\n- `galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:62-64` — `_MEASURED_MASS_SOURCES = MASS_PRIORITY[:-1]`; `:442-496` — budget loop reads `M_halo`, `dm_halo`, `pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz` per foreground row.\n- `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:33-50` — existing `_foreground_mask` cluster test (the pattern to extend).\n\n**Current Behavior:** clusters are found only if NED already classifies an object\nwithin 5 Mpc as a cluster; if found, they flow through `build_unified` with **no\nstellar mass → assumed 10¹⁰ M⊙ → galaxy-scale halo**, so even a found cluster would\nget a wrong (tiny) DM. In practice none are found.\n\n**Current Limitations:**\n- No all-sky cluster catalog; WHL cross-match exists only in notebooks.\n- Mass-blind 5 Mpc impact cut.\n- A cluster row, if present, gets stellar-mass-derived halo mass (wrong).\n- Cluster DM uses galaxy-CGM cool/MgII/τ models, inappropriate for an ICM.\n\n## Desired End State\n\n**New Behavior:** a `ClusterEngine` queries PSZ2/MCXC/MCXC-II for each sightline,\nreturning clusters with `z` and `m500_msun`; the foreground filter keeps a cluster\nwhen its impact ≤ `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR · r200(M200(M500), z)`; `build_unified`\ninjects the catalog M200 as the cluster's `M_halo`, computes its DM from a β-model\nICM profile anchored to M500/R500, sets cluster cool-DM and τ to zero, and the\nbudget reports cluster intervening DM with `measured` mass confidence.\n\n**Success Looks Like:**\n- `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0 -q` passes, including new\n  cluster-model, engine, filter, and budget tests.\n- A live smoke query resolves the three Vizier cluster-catalog IDs and returns\n  rows with finite `z` and `m500_msun`.\n- Re-running the search + budget produces a `sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md`\n  whose cluster contributions (if any sightline intersects a catalogued cluster\n  within 2·r200) appear with `intervening_mass_confidence = measured` and finite\n  `dm_intervening`, with cluster `tau_intervening = 0`.\n\n## What We're NOT Doing\n\n- [ ] Not implementing a temperature-dependent Arnaud+2010 gNFW *pressure* profile\n      with an X-ray temperature model — the isothermal β-model anchored to gas mass\n      is the chosen ICM DM model (gNFW upgrade path noted in Risk Assessment).\n- [ ] Not adding cluster *scattering* (τ) physics — clusters are set to τ=0 per\n      Connor 2023 / Lee 2023 (clusters give DM, not scattering).\n- [ ] Not wiring the notebook WHL cross-match into production (WHL has no Dec>+70\n      coverage; superseded by the all-sky engine).\n- [ ] Not changing the galaxy (non-cluster) search path, the 100 kpc galaxy impact\n      cut, or the mNFW galaxy-CGM models.\n- [ ] Not back-filling per-cluster member spectroscopy or richness-based masses\n      beyond the catalog M500.\n- [ ] Not committing regenerated large result CSVs as part of this plan (the\n      branch carries unrelated flux-cal lanes; results regeneration is a verification\n      step, commit policy decided separately).\n\n**Rationale:** keep the diff focused on the two requested capabilities; the\nβ-model is the minimal physically-correct ICM DM; cluster τ=0 is what the\nliterature supports.\n\n## Implementation Approach\n\n**Technical Strategy:** five phases, each test-first and network-free for unit\ntests (live network only in explicit smoke steps). Phase 1 is pure physics (β-model\nDM) with an analytic oracle. Phase 2 adds the catalog engine. Phase 3 swaps the\nimpact criterion and wires the engine on. Phase 4 integrates cluster mass+DM into\n`build_unified`/budget. Phase 5 verifies end-to-end and regenerates artifacts.\n\n**Key Architectural Decisions:**\n1. **Decision:** isothermal β-model ICM electron density, n_e(r)=n_e0·[1+(r/r_c)²]^(−3β/2), normalized so M_gas(<R500)=f_gas·M500.\n   - **Rationale:** standard, analytically tractable cluster-gas DM model; closed-form Abel projection gives a test oracle; anchoring to gas mass uses the catalog M500 directly.\n   - **Trade-offs:** isothermal/spherical; ignores cool cores and X-ray temperature structure.\n   - **Alternatives considered:** Arnaud gNFW pressure profile (needs a temperature model; deferred); reusing the galaxy mNFW (under-models cluster ICM).\n2. **Decision:** keep cluster within `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR=2.0` × r200, r200 from M200=1.3·M500.\n   - **Rationale:** research shows meaningful DM within ~1–2 r200; the β-model DM is truncated at R200 so 2× is safely inclusive of near-r200 contributors while the column itself vanishes beyond truncation.\n   - **Trade-offs:** a fixed M500→M200 factor (1.3) is order-of-magnitude; acceptable at these precisions.\n3. **Decision:** cluster engine on by default (`ENABLE_CLUSTER_ENGINE=True`).\n   - **Rationale:** finding clusters is the explicit goal; the current output finds zero, so adding cluster rows is the intended change.\n   - **Trade-offs:** changes default search output (gated by a flag for reproducible reruns).\n4. **Decision:** clusters bypass the stellar-mass ladder and the cool/MgII/τ phase.\n   - **Rationale:** clusters have catalog halo mass (no stellar-mass step) and negligible scattering.\n\n**Patterns to Follow:**\n- Vizier-wrapper engine — `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-183` (`AllWiseEngine`).\n- `scipy.quad` DM integral with truncation — `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:104-123`.\n- Network-free unit tests with injected DataFrames — `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:14-50`.\n- Pure-function oracle test (`--check`-style analytic comparison) — `galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py`.\n\n## Implementation Phases\n\nCommands assume the repo root and the `flits` conda env. Run tests with\n`conda run -n flits pytest …`.\n\n### Phase 1: Cluster ICM DM β-model (pure physics)\n\n**Objective:** add `r_delta_kpc` and `dm_cluster_beta_model` to\n`scattering_predict.py`, verified against the analytic Abel projection.\n\n**Tasks:**\n\n- [ ] **Write the failing tests.** File: `galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py` (append).\n\n  ```python\n  import math\n  from galaxies.v2_0 import scattering_predict as scat\n\n  def test_r_delta_kpc_matches_overdensity_definition():\n      # R200 from r_delta must equal the existing get_rvir_and_rs R200 (both 200*rho_c).\n      from galaxies.v2_0.generate_galaxy_plots import get_rvir_and_rs\n      m200, z = 1.0e14, 0.2\n      r200_ref, _, _ = get_rvir_and_rs(m200, z)\n      assert scat.r_delta_kpc(m200, z, 200) == math.isclose(r200_ref, rel_tol=1e-6) or \\\n             abs(scat.r_delta_kpc(m200, z, 200) - r200_ref) / r200_ref < 1e-6\n      # R500 < R200 for the same mass definition input.\n      assert scat.r_delta_kpc(m200, z, 500) < scat.r_delta_kpc(m200, z, 200)\n\n  def test_dm_cluster_beta_model_matches_analytic_projection_near_center():\n      # For b << R_trunc the truncated LOS integral approaches the closed-form\n      # Abel projection of the beta-model. Compare the code to that analytic value.\n      from math import gamma, sqrt, pi\n      m500, z = 5.0e14, 0.25\n      r500 = scat.r_delta_kpc(m500, z, 500)\n      beta, rc = 0.65, 0.15 * r500\n      b = 0.05 * r500\n      dm = scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, b, r500_kpc=r500,\n                                      beta=beta, rc_over_r500=0.15,\n                                      f_gas=0.13, r_trunc_factor=1.54)\n      # Analytic: n_e0 from gas-mass normalization, then Sigma_ne(b) (untruncated).\n      ne0 = scat._beta_ne0_cm3(m500, z, r500, beta, rc, f_gas=0.13)  # helper, tested below\n      sigma_kpc_cm3 = ne0 * rc * sqrt(pi) * gamma(1.5 * beta - 0.5) / gamma(1.5 * beta) \\\n          * (1.0 + (b / rc) ** 2) ** (0.5 - 1.5 * beta)\n      dm_analytic = sigma_kpc_cm3 * 1000.0 / (1.0 + z)\n      assert abs(dm - dm_analytic) / dm_analytic < 0.02  # 2%: truncation at 1.54 R500\n\n  def test_dm_cluster_beta_model_zero_beyond_truncation():\n      m500, z = 5.0e14, 0.25\n      r500 = scat.r_delta_kpc(m500, z, 500)\n      r_trunc = 1.54 * r500\n      assert scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, r_trunc + 1.0) == 0.0\n\n  def test_dm_cluster_beta_model_monotonic_and_linear_in_fgas():\n      m500, z = 5.0e14, 0.25\n      r500 = scat.r_delta_kpc(m500, z, 500)\n      near = scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, 0.1 * r500)\n      far = scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, 0.6 * r500)\n      assert near > far > 0.0\n      d1 = scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, 0.2 * r500, f_gas=0.10)\n      d2 = scat.dm_cluster_beta_model(m500, z, 0.2 * r500, f_gas=0.20)\n      assert abs(d2 / d1 - 2.0) < 1e-6  # DM linear in gas fraction\n  ```\n\n- [ ] **Run, watch fail:** `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py -k \"cluster or r_delta\" -q` → FAIL (`AttributeError`).\n\n- [ ] **Implement** in `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py` (append, after `dm_halo_mnfw`):\n\n  ```python\n  from astropy import constants as const  # add to existing imports if absent\n\n  # --- Cluster ICM (isothermal beta-model) -------------------------------------\n  # Mohr+1999 / Arnaud 2009: ICM beta ~ 0.6-0.7, core radius r_c ~ 0.1-0.2 R500.\n  CLUSTER_BETA = 0.65\n  CLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500 = 0.15\n  # Vikhlinin+2006, Pratt+2009, Eckert+2019: hot-gas fraction within R500 ~ 0.13.\n  CLUSTER_F_GAS_500 = 0.13\n  # Fully ionized ICM mean molecular weight per electron.\n  CLUSTER_MU_E = 1.17\n  # R200/R500 ~ 1.54 for a typical cluster NFW concentration (c500 ~ 1.5).\n  CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500 = 1.54\n\n  def r_delta_kpc(m_delta_msun: float, z: float, delta: float) -> float:\n      \"\"\"Spherical-overdensity radius R_Delta (kpc): M = (4/3)pi Delta rho_c(z) R^3.\"\"\"\n      if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m_delta_msun, z)) or float(m_delta_msun) <= 0.0:\n          return float(\"nan\")\n      m = float(m_delta_msun) * u.Msun\n      h_z = COSMO.H(float(z))\n      # R_Delta = (2 G M / (Delta H^2))^(1/3); Delta=200 reduces to (G M/(100 H^2))^(1/3).\n      r = ((2.0 * const.G * m) / (float(delta) * h_z ** 2)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)\n      return float(r.to(u.kpc).value)\n\n  def _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, r_max_kpc):\n      from scipy.integrate import quad\n      integrand = lambda r: r * r * (1.0 + (r / rc_kpc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)\n      val, _ = quad(integrand, 0.0, r_max_kpc, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-7, limit=200)\n      return 4.0 * math.pi * val  # kpc^3 (shape-only; n_e0 factored out)\n\n  def _beta_ne0_cm3(m500_msun, z, r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, f_gas=CLUSTER_F_GAS_500):\n      \"\"\"Central electron density (cm^-3) so M_gas(<R500)=f_gas*M500 for the beta shape.\"\"\"\n      shape_int_kpc3 = _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, r500_kpc)\n      if shape_int_kpc3 <= 0.0:\n          return float(\"nan\")\n      m_gas_g = f_gas * float(m500_msun) * u.Msun.to(u.g)\n      mu_e_mp_g = CLUSTER_MU_E * 1.67262192369e-24\n      kpc3_to_cm3 = (1.0 * u.kpc ** 3).to(u.cm ** 3).value\n      # M_gas = mu_e m_p n_e0 * (shape integral in cm^3)\n      return m_gas_g / (mu_e_mp_g * shape_int_kpc3 * kpc3_to_cm3)\n\n  def dm_cluster_beta_model(\n      m500_msun, z, impact_kpc, r500_kpc=None,\n      beta=CLUSTER_BETA, rc_over_r500=CLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500,\n      f_gas=CLUSTER_F_GAS_500, r_trunc_factor=CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500,\n  ):\n      \"\"\"Observer-frame ICM DM (pc cm^-3) through a beta-model cluster at impact b.\"\"\"\n      if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m500_msun, z, impact_kpc)) or float(m500_msun) <= 0.0:\n          return 0.0\n      if r500_kpc is None or _is_bad(r500_kpc):\n          r500_kpc = r_delta_kpc(m500_msun, z, 500)\n      if _is_bad(r500_kpc) or r500_kpc <= 0.0:\n          return 0.0\n      rc = rc_over_r500 * r500_kpc\n      r_trunc = r_trunc_factor * r500_kpc\n      b = float(impact_kpc)\n      if b >= r_trunc:\n          return 0.0\n      ne0 = _beta_ne0_cm3(m500_msun, z, r500_kpc, beta, rc, f_gas=f_gas)\n      if _is_bad(ne0):\n          return 0.0\n      from scipy.integrate import quad\n      l_half = math.sqrt(max(r_trunc ** 2 - b ** 2, 0.0))\n      def los(l_kpc):\n          r = math.hypot(b, l_kpc)\n          return ne0 * (1.0 + (r / rc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)\n      col_kpc_cm3, _ = quad(los, -l_half, l_half, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-6, limit=200)\n      dm_obs = col_kpc_cm3 * 1000.0 / (1.0 + float(z))  # 1 kpc path = 1000 pc\n      return float(max(dm_obs, 0.0))\n  ```\n\n- [ ] **Run, watch pass:** `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py -k \"cluster or r_delta\" -q` → PASS.\n- [ ] **Commit:** `git commit -m \"feat(galaxies): beta-model cluster ICM DM + r_delta helper\"`\n\n**Dependencies:** none (pure physics; `scipy`, `astropy` already used).\n\n**Verification:**\n- [ ] `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py -q` passes (existing + new).\n\n### Phase 2: All-sky cluster catalog engine\n\n**Objective:** add `ClusterEngine` to `engines_extra.py` and the catalog config;\nresolve and pin the three Vizier IDs.\n\n**Tasks:**\n\n- [ ] **Resolve the Vizier catalog IDs (live).** Run:\n\n  ```bash\n  conda run -n flits python -c \"from astroquery.vizier import Vizier; \\\n    [print(c) for c in Vizier.find_catalogs('Planck PSZ2').keys()]; \\\n    [print(c) for c in Vizier.find_catalogs('MCXC').keys()]; \\\n    [print(c) for c in Vizier.find_catalogs('MCXC-II meta-catalogue X-ray clusters').keys()]\"\n  ```\n  Record the resolved IDs into `CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS` below. already imported at top\n\n  # Per-catalog column maps: (ra, dec, z, m500_1e14, r500_mpc_or_None).\n  _CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS = {\n      \"J/A+A/594/A27/psz2\": (\"RAdeg\", \"DEdeg\", \"z\", \"MSZ\", None),\n      \"J/A+A/534/A109/mcxc\": (\"RAJ2000\", \"DEJ2000\", \"z\", \"M500\", \"R500\"),\n      \"J/A+A/682/A124/mcxc2\": (\"RAJ2000\", \"DEJ2000\", \"z\", \"M500\", \"R500\"),\n  }\n\n  def _standardize_cluster_columns(df, catalog_id):\n      cols = _CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS.get(catalog_id)\n      out = df.copy()\n      if cols is None:\n          out[\"classification\"] = \"cluster\"\n          out[\"catalog\"] = catalog_id\n          return out\n      ra_c, dec_c, z_c, m_c, r_c = cols\n      rename = {}\n      lower = {c.lower(): c for c in out.columns}\n      if ra_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[ra_c.lower()]] = \"ra\"\n      if dec_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[dec_c.lower()]] = \"dec\"\n      if z_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[z_c.lower()]] = \"z\"\n      out = out.rename(columns=rename)\n      m500 = pd.to_numeric(out.get(m_c), errors=\"coerce\") if m_c in out.columns else np.nan\n      out[\"m500_msun\"] = m500 * 1.0e14\n      if r_c is not None and r_c in out.columns:\n          out[\"r500_kpc\"] = pd.to_numeric(out[r_c], errors=\"coerce\") * 1000.0  # Mpc -> kpc\n      else:\n          out[\"r500_kpc\"] = np.nan\n      out[\"classification\"] = \"cluster\"\n      out[\"catalog\"] = catalog_id\n      return out\n\n  class ClusterEngine(BaseEngine):\n      \"\"\"All-sky galaxy-cluster engine (PSZ2 + MCXC + MCXC-II via Vizier).\"\"\"\n      def __init__(self, catalogs=None):\n          from .config import CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS\n          self.catalogs = dict(catalogs if catalogs is not None else CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS)\n\n      def query(self, coord, radius):\n          frames = []\n          for cat_id in self.catalogs.values():\n              raw = VizierEngine(cat_id).query(coord, radius)\n              if raw.empty:\n                  continue\n              std = _standardize_cluster_columns(raw, cat_id)\n              keep = [c for c in (\"ra\", \"dec\", \"z\", \"m500_msun\", \"r500_kpc\",\n                                  \"classification\", \"catalog\") if c in std.columns]\n              frames.append(std[keep])\n          if not frames:\n              return pd.DataFrame()\n          return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)\n  ```\n\n  Note: `VizierEngine.__init__` uses `row_limit=-1` and standardizes RA/Dec only\n  for known names; cluster RA/Dec/mass columns are standardized here instead, so\n  `_standardize_cluster_columns` operates on the raw Vizier frame — pass the raw\n  catalog through `VizierEngine` but re-map from the original column names. """Network-free tests for scattering prediction helper functions."""

import math

import pytest

from galaxies.v2_0 import scattering_predict as sp


def test_dm_halo_mnfw_is_positive_decreasing_and_handles_edges():
    dm_inner = sp.dm_halo_mnfw(m_halo_msun=1e12, z_gal=0.1, impact_kpc=25.0)
    dm_mid = sp.dm_halo_mnfw(m_halo_msun=1e12, z_gal=0.1, impact_kpc=50.0)
    dm_outer = sp.dm_halo_mnfw(m_halo_msun=1e12, z_gal=0.1, impact_kpc=100.0)

    assert dm_mid is not None
=== tail ===
    two = sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 5.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.3, cool_clump_boost=10.0)
    assert two > base

    # Zero cool DM -> reduces exactly to the hot-only screen.
    no_cool = sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 5.0, 100.0, 0.0, 0.3, cool_clump_boost=10.0)
    assert no_cool == pytest.approx(base)

    # A larger clumpiness boost (F_cool/F_hot) raises the cool contribution.
    more = sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 5.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.3, cool_clump_boost=30.0)
    assert more > two

    # A missing/NaN cool column degrades to hot-only, not NaN.
    deg = sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 5.0, 100.0, float("nan"), 0.3, cool_clump_boost=10.0)
    assert deg == pytest.approx(base)

    # Both columns bad -> None.
    assert sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 5.0, float("nan"), float("nan"), 0.3) is None

    # No geometric leverage -> 0 from each kernel (build_unified maps this to NaN).
    assert sp.tau_scat_two_phase(0.1, 0.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.3) == 0.0

365	        # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 show more cool absorption in more massive

367	        mass_tilt = 10.0 ** (0.15 * (float(logmstar) - 10.5))
368	        fc0 *= _clamp(mass_tilt, 0.5, 1.5)
369	    fc = fc0 * math.exp(-b_scaled / 0.5)
370	
371	    if is_star_forming and not _is_bad(phi_deg):
372	        # Bordoloi+2011 ApJ 743,10 and Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 motivate
373	        # stronger cool covering along the minor axis from outflow-fed gas, so
374	        # sin(phi) peaks at phi=90 deg and leaves the major axis unboosted.
375	        fc *= 1.0 + 0.5 * math.sin(math.radians(float(phi_deg)))
376	
377	    fc = _clamp(fc, 0.0, 1.0)
378	    # Lan & Mo 2018 ApJ 866,36 highlight population and azimuthal scatter, so
379	    # the bracket widens around the central prior and gets extra upper room
380	    # when star-forming azimuth information is available.
381	    lo = _clamp(fc * 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)
382	    hi = _clamp(fc * 1.5 + (0.2 if (is_star_forming and phi_deg is not None) else 0.0), 0.0, 1.0)
383	    fc = _clamp(fc, lo, hi)
384	    return float(fc), float(lo), float(hi)

Cavaliere & Fusco-Femiano 1976 A&A 49,137 set the form.\nCLUSTER_BETA = 0.65\nCLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500 = 0.15\n# Vikhlinin+2006 ApJ 640,691 / Pratt+2009 / Eckert+2019: hot-gas mass fraction\n# within R500 ~ 0.13 for massive clusters.\nCLUSTER_F_GAS_500 = 0.13\n# Fully ionized ICM mean molecular weight per electron (primordial-ish).\nCLUSTER_MU_E = 1.17\n# R200/R500 ~ 1.54 for a typical cluster NFW concentration (c500 ~ 1.5).\nCLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500 = 1.54\n\n\ndef r_delta_kpc(m_delta_msun: float, z: float, delta: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Spherical-overdensity radius R_Delta (kpc): M = (4/3) pi Delta rho_c(z) R^3.\n\n    For Delta=200 this equals the R200 used in get_rvir_and_rs\n    ((G M/(100 H^2))^(1/3)); written via the critical density to match the R200\n    derivation already in dm_halo_mnfw.\n    \"\"\"\n    if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m_delta_msun, z)) or float(m_delta_msun) <= 0.0:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    rho_crit = COSMO.critical_density(float(z)).to(u.Msun / u.kpc**3).value\n    if rho_crit <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(rho_crit):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    radius = (3.0 * float(m_delta_msun) / (4.0 * math.pi * float(delta) * rho_crit)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)\n    return float(radius)\n\n\ndef _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(beta: float, rc_kpc: float, r_max_kpc: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Shape-only gas-mass integral int_0^Rmax 4 pi r^2 [1+(r/rc)^2]^(-3beta/2) dr (kpc^3).\"\"\"\n    from scipy.integrate import quad\n\n    integrand = lambda r: r * r * (1.0 + (r / rc_kpc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)  # noqa: E731\n    value, _ = quad(integrand, 0.0, r_max_kpc, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-7, limit=200)\n    return 4.0 * math.pi * value\n\n\ndef _beta_ne0_cm3(\n    m500_msun: float, z: float, r500_kpc: float, beta: float, rc_kpc: float,\n    f_gas: float = CLUSTER_F_GAS_500,\n) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Central electron density (cm^-3) such that M_gas(<R500) = f_gas * M500.\n\n    M_gas = mu_e m_p n_e0 * int 4 pi r^2 shape(r) dr, so n_e0 follows from the\n    shape integral normalized to the catalog gas mass.\n    \"\"\"\n    shape_int_kpc3 = _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(beta, rc_kpc, r500_kpc)\n    if shape_int_kpc3 <= 0.0 or not math.isfinite(shape_int_kpc3):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    m_gas_g = float(f_gas) * float(m500_msun) * u.Msun.to(u.g)\n    mu_e_mp_g = CLUSTER_MU_E * 1.67262192369e-24\n    kpc3_to_cm3 = (1.0 * u.kpc**3).to(u.cm**3).value\n    return m_gas_g / (mu_e_mp_g * shape_int_kpc3 * kpc3_to_cm3)\n\n\ndef dm_cluster_beta_model(\n    m500_msun: float,\n    z: float,\n    impact_kpc: float,\n    r500_kpc: float | None = None,\n    beta: float = CLUSTER_BETA,\n    rc_over_r500: float = CLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500,\n    f_gas: float = CLUSTER_F_GAS_500,\n    r_trunc_factor: float = CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500,\n) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Observer-frame ICM dispersion measure (pc cm^-3) through a beta-model cluster.\n\n    Isothermal beta-model n_e(r) = n_e0 [1+(r/r_c)^2]^(-3beta/2) (Cavaliere &\n    Fusco-Femiano 1976), normalized so the hot gas within R500 is f_gas * M500\n    (Vikhlinin+2006). The column is projected at impact parameter b, truncated at\n    r_trunc_factor * R500, and divided by (1+z) for the observer frame\n    (Macquart+2020 convention). Returns 0.0 for b beyond truncation or bad inputs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m500_msun, z, impact_kpc)) or float(m500_msun) <= 0.0:\n        return 0.0\n    if r500_kpc is None or _is_bad(r500_kpc):\n        r500_kpc = r_delta_kpc(m500_msun, z, 500)\n    if _is_bad(r500_kpc) or float(r500_kpc) <= 0.0:\n        return 0.0\n    r500_kpc = float(r500_kpc)\n    rc = float(rc_over_r500) * r500_kpc\n    r_trunc = float(r_trunc_factor) * r500_kpc\n    b = float(impact_kpc)\n    if b >= r_trunc:\n        return 0.0\n    ne0 = _beta_ne0_cm3(m500_msun, z, r500_kpc, beta, rc, f_gas=f_gas)\n    if _is_bad(ne0):\n        return 0.0\n\n    from scipy.integrate import quad\n\n    l_half = math.sqrt(max(r_trunc**2 - b**2, 0.0))\n\n    def los(l_kpc: float) -> float:\n        r = math.hypot(b, l_kpc)\n        return ne0 * (1.0 + (r / rc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)\n\n    column_kpc_cm3, _ = quad(los, -l_half, l_half, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-6, limit=200)\n    if not math.isfinite(column_kpc_cm3):\n        return 0.0\n    # 1 kpc of path contributes 1000 pc to the pc cm^-3 DM unit; /(1+z) for the\n    # observer frame (Macquart+2020).\n    dm_obs = column_kpc_cm3 * 1000.0 / (1.0 + float(z))\n    return float(max(dm_obs, 0.0))"

{

  "new_string": "        return _ensure_standard_columns(df, \"2MASS_XSC\")\n\n\n# Per-catalog column maps for all-sky cluster catalogs:\n# catalog_id -> (ra_col, dec_col, z_col, m500_col_1e14, r500_col_mpc_or_None).\n_CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS = {\n    \"J/A+A/594/A27/psz2\": (\"RAdeg\", \"DEdeg\", \"z\", \"MSZ\", None),\n    \"J/A+A/534/A109/mcxc\": (\"RAJ2000\", \"DEJ2000\", \"z\", \"M500\", \"R500\"),\n    \"J/A+A/682/A124/mcxc2\": (\"RAJ2000\", \"DEJ2000\", \"z\", \"M500\", \"R500\"),\n}\n\n\ndef _standardize_cluster_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, catalog_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Standardize a cluster catalog frame to ra/dec/z/m500_msun/r500_kpc/classification.\"\"\"\n    out = df.copy()\n    cols = _CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS.get(catalog_id)\n    if cols is None:\n        out[\"classification\"] = \"cluster\"\n        out[\"catalog\"] = catalog_id\n        return out\n    ra_c, dec_c, z_c, m_c, r_c = cols\n    lower = {c.lower(): c for c in out.columns}\n    rename = {}\n    for src, std in ((ra_c, \"ra\"), (dec_c, \"dec\"), (z_c, \"z\")):\n        if src.lower() in lower:\n            rename[lower[src.lower()]] = std\n    out = out.rename(columns=rename)\n    m500 = pd.to_numeric(out.get(m_c), errors=\"coerce\") if m_c in out.columns else np.nan\n    out[\"m500_msun\"] = m500 * 1.0e14\n    if r_c is not None and r_c in out.columns:\n        out[\"r500_kpc\"] = pd.to_numeric(out[r_c], errors=\"coerce\") * 1000.0  # Mpc -> kpc\n    else:\n        out[\"r500_kpc\"] = np.nan\n    out[\"classification\"] = \"cluster\"\n    out[\"catalog\"] = catalog_id\n    return out\n\n\nclass ClusterEngine(BaseEngine):\n    \"\"\"All-sky galaxy-cluster engine (PSZ2 + MCXC + MCXC-II via Vizier).\n\n    Only all-sky cluster catalogs cover the sample's high declination; each\n    catalog supplies redshift + M500 (and R500 where available) so the search can\n    apply an r200-relative impact cut and a beta-model ICM dispersion measure.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, catalogs=None):\n        if catalogs is None:\n            from .config import CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS\n\n            catalogs = CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS\n        self.catalogs = dict(catalogs)\n\n    def query(self, coord, radius) -> pd.DataFrame:\n        frames = []\n        for cat_id in self.catalogs.values():\n            raw = VizierEngine(cat_id).query(coord, radius)\n            if raw.empty:\n                continue\n            std = _standardize_cluster_columns(raw, cat_id)\n            keep = [\n                c\n                for c in (\"ra\", \"dec\", \"z\", \"m500_msun\", \"r500_kpc\", \"classification\", \"catalog\")\n                if c in std.columns\n            ]\n            frames.append(std[keep])\n        if not frames:\n            return pd.DataFrame()\n        return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)"

30	# Columns that may carry an object classification (NED 'Type', SDSS 'class'/'cl').
31	CLASSIFICATION_COLUMNS = ("classification", "Type", "class", "cl", "otype")
32	# Galaxy-cluster classifications: NED 'GClstr', SDSS/SIMBAD 'ClG', bare 'Cl', 'cluster'.
33	_CLUSTER_RE = re.compile(r"cluster|gclstr|clg|^cl\b", re.IGNORECASE)
34	
35	
36	def _cluster_mask(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
37	    """Per-row True where a classification column marks the object a galaxy cluster."""
38	    is_cluster = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
39	    for column in CLASSIFICATION_COLUMNS:
40	        if column not in df.columns:
41	            continue
42	        is_cluster = is_cluster | df[column].astype(str).str.contains(_CLUSTER_RE)
43	    return is_cluster

1	# Implementation Plan: All-sky galaxy-cluster engine + r200-relative impact cut
2	
3	---
4	**Date:** 2026-06-23
5	**Author:** AI Assistant
6	**Status:** Draft
7	**Related Documents:**
8	- [Research: Foreground galaxy & galaxy-cluster distributions along the co-detected sightlines](research-foreground-galaxies-sightlines.md)
9	- [CHIME/DSA Co-detection Science Plan](../../codetection-science-plan.md)
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Overview
14	
15	The foreground-search pipeline (`galaxies/v2_0/`) currently detects galaxy
16	clusters **only** by NED object-type strings (`GClstr`/`GGroup`/`ClG`) and applies
17	a flat 5 Mpc impact cut. The research pass found this yields **zero clusters** on
18	all 12 sightlines, for two independent reasons: (1) at the sample's declination
19	(+70° to +74°) the SDSS-based cluster catalogs (WHL, redMaPPer) have no coverage —
20	only all-sky catalogs reach the band; (2) a fixed 5 Mpc cut is mass-blind, so it
21	mostly admits negligible-DM near-misses while a real DM contribution needs the
22	sightline within ~1–2 r200 of the cluster.
23	
24	This plan adds an **all-sky cluster-catalog engine** (Planck PSZ2 + MCXC +
25	MCXC-II, queried through Vizier) that supplies each cluster's redshift and M500
26	mass, replaces the flat 5 Mpc cut with a **mass-scaled r200-relative criterion**
27	(keep within 2·r200), turns an intersected cluster's ICM into a dispersion-measure
28	contribution with a **β-model electron-density profile** anchored to the catalog
29	mass, and integrates that cluster DM into the existing per-sightline budget. Per
30	the literature, clusters contribute DM but negligible scattering, so cluster τ is
31	set to zero.
32	
33	**Goal:** the production search finds the real foreground clusters along each
34	sightline (where any exist), assigns each a physically-scaled impact criterion,
35	and folds a defensible cluster ICM DM into `sightline_dm_scattering_budget`.
36	
37	**Motivation:** sightline attribution (CGM/groups/clusters of the intervening
38	systems) is a headline science goal; the current cluster path is both
39	under-powered (wrong catalogs for this sky) and aimed at a low-yield regime.
40	
41	## Current State Analysis
42	
43	**Existing Implementation:**
44	- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-17` — `DEFAULT_IMPACT_KPC=100`,
45	  `DEFAULT_CLUSTER_IMPACT_KPC=5000.0` (flat 5 Mpc), cone caps.
46	- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:37-56` — `VIZIER_CATALOGS`, opt-in engine/enricher flags.
47	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43` — `_CLUSTER_RE` + `_cluster_mask` (classification-string detection).
48	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:56-74` — `_foreground_mask`: per-row impact limit, cluster rows get the flat `cluster_impact_kpc`.
49	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:215-234` — engine list assembly + cone sizing from `max(impact_kpc, cluster_impact_kpc)`.
50	- `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-102` — `NedEngine`, `VizierEngine` (standardize ra/dec/z + `catalog` tag).
51	- `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-221` — thin Vizier-wrapper engine pattern (`AllWiseEngine`, `XscEngine`).
52	- `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:27-123` — `dm_halo_mnfw` (mNFW hot-halo DM via `scipy.quad`; the style to mirror for the β-model).
53	- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:118-155` — `select_stellar_mass` ladder; `:266-277` — `m_halo = estimate_halo_mass(logm_best)` then `get_rvir_and_rs`.
54	- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:338-403` — per-galaxy cool-CGM/MgII/two-phase-τ derivation.
55	- `galaxies/v2_0/generate_galaxy_plots.py:65` — `get_rvir_and_rs(m,z)` returns R200 (= `(G·M/(100 H_z²))^{1/3}`).
56	- `galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:62-64` — `_MEASURED_MASS_SOURCES = MASS_PRIORITY[:-1]`; `:442-496` — budget loop reads `M_halo`, `dm_halo`, `pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz` per foreground row.
57	- `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:33-50` — existing `_foreground_mask` cluster test (the pattern to extend).
58	
59	**Current Behavior:** clusters are found only if NED already classifies an object
60	within 5 Mpc as a cluster; if found, they flow through `build_unified` with **no
61	stellar mass → assumed 10¹⁰ M⊙ → galaxy-scale halo**, so even a found cluster would
62	get a wrong (tiny) DM. In practice none are found.
63	
64	**Current Limitations:**
65	- No all-sky cluster catalog; WHL cross-match exists only in notebooks.
66	- Mass-blind 5 Mpc impact cut.
67	- A cluster row, if present, gets stellar-mass-derived halo mass (wrong).
68	- Cluster DM uses galaxy-CGM cool/MgII/τ models, inappropriate for an ICM.
69	
70	## Desired End State
71	
72	**New Behavior:** a `ClusterEngine` queries PSZ2/MCXC/MCXC-II for each sightline,
73	returning clusters with `z` and `m500_msun`; the foreground filter keeps a cluster
74	when its impact ≤ `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR · r200(M200(M500), z)`; `build_unified`
75	injects the catalog M200 as the cluster's `M_halo`, computes its DM from a β-model
76	ICM profile anchored to M500/R500, sets cluster cool-DM and τ to zero, and the
77	budget reports cluster intervening DM with `measured` mass confidence.
78	
79	**Success Looks Like:**
80	- `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0 -q` passes, including new
81	  cluster-model, engine, filter, and budget tests.
82	- A live smoke query resolves the three Vizier cluster-catalog IDs and returns
83	  rows with finite `z` and `m500_msun`.
84	- Re-running the search + budget produces a `sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md`
85	  whose cluster contributions (if any sightline intersects a catalogued cluster
86	  within 2·r200) appear with `intervening_mass_confidence = measured` and finite
87	  `dm_intervening`, with cluster `tau_intervening = 0`.
88	
89	## What We're NOT Doing
90	
91	- [ ] Not implementing a temperature-dependent Arnaud+2010 gNFW *pressure* profile
92	      with an X-ray temperature model — the isothermal β-model anchored to gas mass
93	      is the chosen ICM DM model (gNFW upgrade path noted in Risk Assessment).
94	- [ ] Not adding cluster *scattering* (τ) physics — clusters are set to τ=0 per
95	      Connor 2023 / Lee 2023 (clusters give DM, not scattering).
96	- [ ] Not wiring the notebook WHL cross-match into production (WHL has no Dec>+70
97	      coverage; superseded by the all-sky engine).
98	- [ ] Not changing the galaxy (non-cluster) search path, the 100 kpc galaxy impact
99	      cut, or the mNFW galaxy-CGM models.
100	- [ ] Not back-filling per-cluster member spectroscopy or richness-based masses
101	      beyond the catalog M500.
102	- [ ] Not committing regenerated large result CSVs as part of this plan (the
103	      branch carries unrelated flux-cal lanes; results regeneration is a verification
104	      step, commit policy decided separately).
105	
106	**Rationale:** keep the diff focused on the two requested capabilities; the
107	β-model is the minimal physically-correct ICM DM; cluster τ=0 is what the
108	literature supports.
109	
110	## Implementation Approach
111	
112	**Technical Strategy:** five phases, each test-first and network-free for unit
113	tests (live network only in explicit smoke steps). Phase 1 is pure physics (β-model
114	DM) with an analytic oracle. Phase 2 adds the catalog engine. Phase 3 swaps the
115	impact criterion and wires the engine on. Phase 4 integrates cluster mass+DM into
116	`build_unified`/budget. Phase 5 verifies end-to-end and regenerates artifacts.
117	
118	**Key Architectural Decisions:**
119	1. **Decision:** isothermal β-model ICM electron density, n_e(r)=n_e0·[1+(r/r_c)²]^(−3β/2), normalized so M_gas(<R500)=f_gas·M500.
120	   - **Rationale:** standard, analytically tractable cluster-gas DM model; closed-form Abel projection gives a test oracle; anchoring to gas mass uses the catalog M500 directly.
121	   - **Trade-offs:** isothermal/spherical; ignores cool cores and X-ray temperature structure.
122	   - **Alternatives considered:** Arnaud gNFW pressure profile (needs a temperature model; deferred); reusing the galaxy mNFW (under-models cluster ICM).
123	2. **Decision:** keep cluster within `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR=2.0` × r200, r200 from M200=1.3·M500.
124	   - **Rationale:** research shows meaningful DM within ~1–2 r200; the β-model DM is truncated at R200 so 2× is safely inclusive of near-r200 contributors while the column itself vanishes beyond truncation.
125	   - **Trade-offs:** a fixed M500→M200 factor (1.3) is order-of-magnitude; acceptable at these precisions.
126	3. **Decision:** cluster engine on by default (`ENABLE_CLUSTER_ENGINE=True`).
127	   - **Rationale:** finding clusters is the explicit goal; the current output finds zero, so adding cluster rows is the intended change.
128	   - **Trade-offs:** changes default search output (gated by a flag for reproducible reruns).
129	4. **Decision:** clusters bypass the stellar-mass ladder and the cool/MgII/τ phase.
130	   - **Rationale:** clusters have catalog halo mass (no stellar-mass step) and negligible scattering.
131	
132	**Patterns to Follow:**
133	- Vizier-wrapper engine — `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-183` (`AllWiseEngine`).
134	- `scipy.quad` DM integral with truncation — `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:104-123`.
135	- Network-free unit tests with injected DataFrames — `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:14-50`.
136	- Pure-function oracle test (`--check`-style analytic comparison) — `galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py`.
137
