65	def get_rvir_and_rs(m_halo_msun, z):
66	    """R_200 and NFW scale radius r_s in kpc."""
67	    M_h = m_halo_msun * u.Msun
68	    H_z = cosmo.H(z)
69	    G = const.G
70	    r_vir = ((G * M_h / (100 * H_z**2))**(1/3)).to(u.kpc).value
71	    # Dutton & Maccio 2014 (MNRAS 441, 3359) c-M relation at z=0.
72	    log_c = 0.905 - 0.101 * np.log10(m_halo_msun / 1e12)
73	    # First-order redshift evolution (concentration declines with z); D&M14
74	    # give d(log c)/dz ~ -0.08 over the low-z regime probed here.
75	    log_c *= (1.0 - 0.08 * z)
76	    c = 10**log_c
77	    r_s = r_vir / c
78	    return r_vir, r_s, c
79	
80	
81	def estimate_logmstar_from_photometry(row, z_gal):
82	    """Taylor+2011 (MNRAS 418, 1587, Eq. 8) color-mass estimate.
83	
84	        log(M*/Msun) = 1.15 + 0.70 (g - i) - 0.4 M_i
85	
86	    DESI Legacy imaging provides g, r, z; the Taylor calibration is in g-i and
87	    M_i, so this only fires when an i-band magnitude is also present. Returns
88	    None when the required bands are missing (caller falls back to 'assumed').
89	    """
90	    g = _get_mag(row, 'g')
91	    i = _get_mag(row, 'i')
92	    if g is None or i is None:
93	        return None
94	    dist_mod = cosmo.distmod(z_gal).value
95	    M_i = i - dist_mod  # absolute i-band (rest-frame k-correction neglected)
96	    return 1.15 + 0.70 * (g - i) - 0.4 * M_i
97	
98	
99	def _get_mag(row, band):
100	    """Return an apparent magnitude for ``band`` from common column spellings, or None."""
101	    for col in (band, f'{band}mag', f'mag_{band}', f'{band}_mag', f'{band}MAG'):
102	        if col in row and pd.notna(row[col]):
103	            return float(row[col])
104	    return None
105	
106	
107	def nfw_enclosed_mass(r, m_halo, r_vir, r_s, c):
108	    x = r / r_s
109	    f_x = np.log(1 + x) - x / (1 + x)
110	    f_c = np.log(1 + c) - c / (1 + c)
111	    return m_halo * f_x / f_c

387	            </tr>"""

389	        panels_html += f"""
390	<div class="tab-panel{active}" id="{tid}">
391	  <div class="grid-2">
392	    <div class="card">
393	      <h2 class="card-title">{sec['name']} — Sightline Spatial Distribution</h2>

395	      <div class="info-panel"><strong>Note:</strong> Shaded regions = virial radii (R₂₀₀). Horizontal line = FRB sightline (b=0). Overlap ⇒ sightline intersects the halo.</div>
396	    </div>
397	    <div class="card">

400	      <div class="info-panel"><strong>Note:</strong> Dotted vertical lines = impact parameter; dashed = R₂₀₀. Scatter = enclosed mass at b.</div>
401	    </div>
402	  </div>
403	  <div class="card">
404	    <h2 class="card-title">{sec['name']} — Galaxy & Halo Properties</h2>
405	    <table>
406	      <thead><tr>
407	        <th>Galaxy</th><th>z (FRB)</th><th>Comoving Dist</th><th>Impact b</th>
408	        <th>R_vir</th><th>Stellar Mass (source)</th><th>Halo Mass</th><th>Encl. Mass %</th><th>Intersects R₂₀₀</th>
409	      </tr></thead>
410	      <tbody>{trows}</tbody>
411	    </table>
412	  </div>
413	</div>"""
414	
415	    html = _HTML_HEAD.replace(
416	        '__N_SIGHTLINES__', str(len(target_sections))
417	    ).replace(
418	        '<div class="tabs" id="tabs"></div>',
419	        f'<div class="tabs" id="tabs">{tabs_html}</div>'
420	    ).replace(
421	        '<div id="panels"></div>',
422	        f'<div id="panels">{panels_html}</div>'
423	    )
424	    return html

427	# --------------- main ---------------
428	
429	def main():
430	    # Resolve paths relative to the repo root
431	    base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
432	    results_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "results")
433	    docs_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "docs")
434	
435	    # Import targets from config
436	    sys.path.insert(0, base_dir)
437	    from galaxies.v2_0.config import TARGETS
438	
439	    target_sections = []
440	
441	    for name, ra_str, dec_str, z_frb in TARGETS:
442	        csv_path = os.path.join(results_dir, f"{name.lower()}_galaxies.csv")
443	        if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
444	            print(f"  {name}: no CSV found, skipping.")
445	            continue
446	
447	        df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
448	        if df.empty:
449	            print(f"  {name}: CSV empty, skipping.")
450	            continue
451	
452	        # Build per-galaxy data
453	        gal_rows = []
454	        for _, row in df.iterrows():
455	            z_gal = row['z']
456	            impact = row['impact_kpc']
457	
458	            if 'M_star' in row and not np.isnan(row['M_star']) and row['M_star'] > 0:
459	                log_mstar = row['M_star']
460	                mass_source = 'catalog'
461	            else:
462	                phot = estimate_logmstar_from_photometry(row, z_gal)
463	                if phot is not None:
464	                    log_mstar, mass_source = phot, 'photometric'
465	                else:
466	                    # No catalog M* and no usable photometry (e.g. DESI grz
467	                    # without i-band): assume a typical L* galaxy.
468	                    log_mstar, mass_source = 10.0, 'assumed'
469	
470	            m_halo = estimate_halo_mass(log_mstar)
471	            r_vir, r_s, c = get_rvir_and_rs(m_halo, z_gal)
472	            d_com = cosmo.comoving_distance(z_gal).to(u.Mpc).value
473	
474	            gal_rows.append({
475	                'z_gal': z_gal,
476	                'd_com': d_com,
477	                'impact': impact,
478	                'log_mstar': log_mstar,
479	                'mass_source': mass_source,
480	                'm_halo': m_halo,
481	                'r_vir': r_vir,
482	                'r_s': r_s,
483	                'c': c,
484	            })
485	
486	        if not gal_rows:
487	            continue
488	
489	        print(f"  {name}: {len(gal_rows)} galaxies")
490	
491	        # Generate per-target figures
492	        fig1, b64_sl = make_sightline_fig(name, z_frb, gal_rows)
493	        sl_path = os.path.join(results_dir, f"{name.lower()}_sightline.png")
494	        fig1.savefig(sl_path, dpi=300)
495	        plt.close(fig1)
496	        print(f"    → {sl_path}")
497	
498	        fig2, b64_mp = make_mass_profile_fig(name, z_frb, gal_rows)
499	        mp_path = os.path.join(results_dir, f"{name.lower()}_mass_profile.png")
500	        fig2.savefig(mp_path, dpi=300)
501	        plt.close(fig2)
502	        print(f"    → {mp_path}")
503	
504	        target_sections.append({
505	            'name': name,
506	            'z_frb': z_frb,
507	            'gal_rows': gal_rows,
508	            'b64_sightline': b64_sl,
509	            'b64_mass': b64_mp,
510	        })
511	
512	    if not target_sections:
513	        print("No galaxy data found. Exiting.")
514	        return
515	
516	    # Build HTML
517	    html = build_html(target_sections)
518	
519	    html_path = os.path.join(results_dir, 'galaxy_sightlines_report.html')
520	    with open(html_path, 'w') as f:
521	        f.write(html)
522	    print(f"\nSaved HTML report → {html_path}")
523	
524	    # Copy to docs/ for GitHub Pages
525	    os.makedirs(docs_dir, exist_ok=True)
526	    docs_path = os.path.join(docs_dir, 'index.html')
527	    shutil.copy2(html_path, docs_path)
528	    print(f"Copied to → {docs_path}")
529	
530	
531	if __name__ == '__main__':
532	    main()
533

57	def estimate_halo_mass(log_mstar):
58	    """Halo mass from stellar mass via the Moster+2013 (Eq. 2) SMHM relation.
59	
60	    M*(M_h) is monotonic in M_h over the plotted range, so we invert Eq. 2
61	    numerically with brentq rather than using a sinh fitting form. Bracket
62	    spans dwarf to cluster halos (log M_h in [9.5, 15.5]).
63	    """
64	    log_mh = brentq(lambda lmh: _moster_log_mstar(lmh) - log_mstar, 9.5, 15.5)
65	    return 10**log_mh

69	    """R_200 and NFW scale radius r_s in kpc."""
70	    M_h = m_halo_msun * u.Msun
71	    H_z = cosmo.H(z)
72	    G = const.G

**Policy mechanism** (commits `ea91839` + `258d643`):
- `.agents/deferred-tasks.md` — tagged checklist (`@agent` blocks, `@human`/`@decision`/`@separate-lane` don't).
- `.claude/hooks/deferred-task-gate.sh` — Stop hook; smoke-tested: silent-pass with no open `@agent`, emits `{"decision":"block",…}` when one exists.
- Registered in `.claude/settings.json`; prose in `CLAUDE.md`.

**`@agent` items the policy required me to clear** (commit `30a21f5`):
- `plot_sightline` — adjustText label deconfliction (phineas' 9 overlapping cluster labels); 12 sky maps regenerated, visually verified.
- `generate_galaxy_plots` dashboard — excludes cluster rows (galaxy-only NFW view) and clamps degenerate `z~0.001` stellar masses into the SMHM bracket (was crashing `brentq` on Isha). Dashboard + `docs/index.html` rebuilt, figures visually verified, 115 tests pass.

Workflow done — 12 proposed, 9 killed by the adversarial pass (mostly because the failure they'd catch is already fixed at source, or the mechanism was unbuildable/toothless). 3 survived, plus one strong signal salvaged from the killed pile.

**Worth adding:**

**1. no-commit-to-main guard** (high value, low friction) — nothing mechanically stops a commit landing on `main`; oneway-guard only classifies push/merge. It's already happened: `a2333b5`/`42803fd`/`a5c499a` ("auto-commit CLAUDE.md") and `eed6f04` (WIP snapshot) are direct non-PR commits on main. Minimal form: one guard line in `commit-claude-md.sh` (the actual repeat offender — refuse when `HEAD` is main/master) + a small PreToolUse hook refusing `git commit` on main, fail-open if git/HEAD absent.

**2. MCMC seed determinism** (medium) — emcee walker init (`burstfit.py:1044`) and `run_mcmc` draw from unseeded global `np.random`, and no seed is stored in `safe_results`. Published `tau_1ghz_err`/`alpha_err` (e.g. the zach ΔlnZ fit) are **not regenerable**. Minimal form: thread one `np.random.Generator` through `FRBFitter`, store the seed in results, and one CI test fitting a fixture twice with the same seed asserting identical posteriors (and differing on different seeds). No Stop hook.

**3. frequency-orientation flip test** (medium) — loader flips to ascending purely on the `freq_descending` flag with no inverse check; a double-flip silently fit `tau(nu)` backwards once already (`c66358a`). Minimal form: one pytest round-trip (synthetic descending array → ascending exactly once; ascending left untouched). Skip the runtime physical assertion — author-confirmed undecidable from DSA data (bandpass destroyed by per-channel z-score).

**Salvage from the killed pile (a real, uncovered bug):** the binding validation contract and the code **disagree on the gate thresholds**. `.cursor/rules/AGENT_CONFIGURATION_FLITS.md` + `fit-verify.js` say α∈[1.5, 6.0] and τ≤100 ms; `burstfit.py` encodes α lower bound **3.0** and τ ceiling **1000 ms** (and a dead χ²_red PASS ceiling 3.0 vs contract 1.5). A code-vs-code test passes green (the two Python copies agree); the worthwhile version is a ~15-line test asserting **code matches a canonical CONTRACT dict** — it fails today on `ALPHA_GOOD_MIN`. This is the highest-signal finding: fits could be PASS-gated against the wrong α floor.

The 9 killed were correctly killed — e.g. secret/large-file guard (zero base rate; the real leak is untracked `.entire/*.jsonl`, wrong extension), subagent write-scope (already done via agent frontmatter `tools:`), MARGINAL-fit gate (`classify_fit_quality` is dead code, never called).

Want me to implement #1 and the contract-threshold test now (both low-risk, no science judgment)? #2 and #3 touch the fit kernel — I'd do those as a separate reviewed change.

  "description": "Map+propose+prune agent efficacy/accuracy practice policies"
}

None would have been caught by any proposed gate.

Why all 12 died, in one sentence each pattern:
- **Token/comment/prose greps are gameable** — "claim-to-artifact binding", "live-confirm IDs", "baseline-then-compare", "assumptions ledger", "smallest-repro" all reduce to *assert a string exists*, which an agent satisfies without doing the work. A before/after pair computed with the *same buggy constant* passes the grep while being totally wrong.
- **Built on nonexistent substrate** — "regression-guard", "no-FAIL-cited", "stale-claim re-check" depend on an MCMC seed / a `quality` JSON field / `src:` provenance tokens that don't exist (and `classify_fit_quality` has **zero call sites** — its verdict is never serialized).

**The real root cause it surfaced:** a skill-**application** gap, not a skill-content gap. The agent who wrote the original blind DM-phase test *had* the Iron Law available and didn't apply it. 2	
3	Research note (codebase investigation, 2026-06-22). Scope: does the absence of absolute

9	| Question | Answer | Confidence |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Q1. Are `c0_C` and `c0_D` in commensurable units? | **No** — independent per-telescope arbitrary units | High (code-confirmed) |
12	| Q2. Is summing `E_CHIME + E_DSA` defensible? | **No** — adds two independently-scaled bands; corrupts even cross-burst *ranking* of the total | High |

14	
15	**Bottom line:** the table cannot be published as absolute energies, and the CHIME+DSA *sum*
16	is not even a reliable relative-ordering statistic. Salvageable only as a single
17	calibrated-band, order-of-magnitude estimate (see Recommendations).

19	## Methodology
20	
21	Traced the amplitude `c0` from the joint-fit output back through the model likelihood to the
22	data ingest, and inspected the stored posteriors. Files: `burstfit_joint.py`, `burstfit.py`,
23	`analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/run_joint_fit.py`, `joint_json/*_joint_fit.json`.
24	
25	## Evidence
26	
27	1. **`c0` is fit in per-channel S/N units (corrected 2026-06-22).** Earlier this note said `c0`
28	   "inherits whatever units the `.npy` carries." Direct read of the loader corrects that: before the
29	   data reaches `FRBModel`, `BurstDataset._bandpass_correct` (`io.py:131-137`) **z-scores every
30	   channel** by its own off-pulse mean/std, and `io.py:143-146` downsamples without renormalizing,
31	   keeping "units as S/N." So the fitted `c0` is the per-channel **signal-to-noise** spectral
32	   amplitude, with the arbitrary instrumental gain divided out — not raw native units. This does
33	   **not** weaken the verdict: S/N is still telescope-specific (the S/N→Jy factor σ_S = SEFD/(√(n_pol·Δν·Δt)·G)
34	   differs per band per channel), so `c0_C` and `c0_D` remain incommensurable and unsummable. It
35	   sharpens the fix: multiply each band's S/N by its own σ_S(ν) (the radiometer step) — see
36	   `docs/rse/specs/plan-radiometer-flux-cal.md`.
37	
38	2. **No flux/units metadata anywhere.** `*_joint_fit.json` keys are
39	   `[burst, alpha, tau_1ghz, log_evidence, log_evidence_err, alpha_bounds, percentiles, ncall]`
40	   — no `units`, `calibration`, or `Jy` field. Nothing asserts the `.npy` is in Jy·ms.
41	
42	3. **`c0_C` and `c0_D` show no common scale** (medians):
43	
44	   ```
45	   burst        c0_C    c0_D        burst        c0_C    c0_D
46	   chromatica  0.719   0.107        oran        0.827   0.082
47	   freya       0.743   0.294        phineas     0.342   0.361
48	   hamilton    0.124   0.049        whitney     0.077   0.253
49	   isha        1.451   0.027        wilhelm     0.127   0.763
50	   johndoeII   0.131   0.219        zach        1.929   0.185
51	   mahi        0.059   4.181
52	   ```
53	   Each band is ~O(0.01–4) in its own normalization, set by its own telescope's pipeline. CHIME
54	   (transit cylinder) and DSA-110 (separate array) share no flux standard — there is no
55	   cross-band tie anywhere in the config or loader.
56	
57	4. **The pipeline's own design treats the per-channel amplitude/spectrum as a nuisance.** The
58	   gain-marginalized path (`burstfit_joint.py:95-97`, `burstfit.py:728-742`) integrates the
59	   per-channel gain out analytically — "the gain absorbs the burst spectrum AND scintillation…
60	   c0 and gamma drop out of the sampled vector." The energetics calc resurrects `c0/γ` from the
61	   *other* (sampled) path and treats them as physical flux densities. This is an internal
62	   contradiction: the pipeline marginalizes the spectrum away precisely because the per-channel
63	   amplitude is not trusted as an absolute physical quantity.
64	
65	5. **No bandpass flattening in the `c0/γ` path.** A smooth power law is fit to the channel
66	   amplitudes as-is. Any uncorrected frequency-dependent gain (band-edge rolloff) is absorbed
67	   into `γ`. The DSA `γ_D` posteriors rail at the −5 prior floor for several bursts (Phineas
68	   median −4.998, posterior `[-4.9995, -4.9954]`, err ±0.001-0.003; Chromatica/Zach/Hamilton/Oran
69	   similar), and Whitney sits at the opposite extreme (`γ_D=+2.91`). A railed/extreme index that
70	   tracks the band edge is the signature of an uncorrected bandpass, not an astrophysical spectrum.
71	
72	## Findings per question
73	
74	**Q1 — commensurability.** `c0_C` and `c0_D` are amplitudes in independent, uncalibrated,
75	per-telescope units (Evidence 1–3). They are not comparable; their ratio carries no physical
76	meaning.
77	
78	**Q2 — the sum.** `E_iso = E_CHIME + E_DSA` adds `c0_C·(CHIME scale)` to `c0_D·(DSA scale)` with
79	two *different* unknown scales. This is worse than "absolute scale unknown": because the
80	CHIME:DSA energy mix swings per burst (Isha 0.5% DSA → Wilhelm 74% DSA), the unknown per-band
81	factors reshuffle the bursts differently, so even the *relative ordering* of the total is not
82	preserved. The code's caveat ("a common unknown factor leaves ordering intact") assumes ONE
83	factor; there are two.
84	
85	**Q3 — the rail.** The `c0/γ` path does not flatten the bandpass, so an uncorrected DSA rolloff
86	would be absorbed into `γ_D` and drive it to the prior floor — a plausible, possibly dominant,
87	explanation for the −5 rail. Confirm by overplotting a raw DSA channel-amplitude spectrum against
88	the fitted power law (or by comparing to the gain-marginal `gain_spectrum`, which is the
89	calibration-robust per-channel estimate).
90	
91	## Recommendations (prioritized)
92	
93	1. **Do not sum the two bands.** Drop `E_iso = E_CHIME + E_DSA` from the table.
94	2. **Anchor one band and report it alone.** CHIME publishes catalog fluences (Jy·ms, with
95	   realistic beam-model uncertainties). Tie each CHIME waterfall to its catalog fluence, then
96	   report **CHIME-band `E_iso`** as an order-of-magnitude value with explicit uncertainty.
97	3. **Fix the bandpass before trusting `γ`.** Flatten the per-channel gain (or use the
98	   gain-marginal `gain_spectrum`) and re-fit; the −5 rail may relax. Until then, mark railed
99	   `γ_D` as prior-limited, not measured.
100	4. **If neither band is calibratable:** do not report absolute energies. Report only
101	   calibration-robust quantities (τ, Δν_d, spectral *shape* with caveats) or fluence *ratios*
102	   within a single band.
103	5. **Add posterior-propagated error bars** to whatever energy is reported; for railed parameters
104	   report a one-sided limit.

146	## Prior-art recon — how the field calibrates these bursts (verified refs)
147	
148	Sweep 2026-06-22 (perplexity scholar + ADS/SciX; every reference below resolved via the ADS API,
149	BibTeX in `references.bib`). The path to a quotable energy is standard radio practice, not a
150	backend dig.
151	
152	**The one equation, both bands.** Signal-to-noise → flux density via the radiometer equation:
153	
154	```
155	S_nu = (S/N) * SEFD / [ sqrt(n_pol * d_nu * d_t) * G(theta,phi,nu) ]
156	SEFD = 2 k_B T_sys / A_eff          fluence F = integral S_nu dt  [Jy*ms]
157	```
158	
159	The only missing ingredients are each telescope's **SEFD** and the **beam response `G`** at the
160	burst's sky position. FLITS already whitens by off-pulse MAD, so the data is effectively in S/N
161	units — it is one SEFD multiply (× beam correction) away from Jy.
162	
163	**CHIME (400–800 MHz) — templates:**
164	- Andersen+ 2023 (AJ 166, 138), *Flux Calibration of CHIME/FRB Intensity Data* — the dedicated
165	  method paper (radiometer + primary-beam model; the equation above).
166	- CHIME/FRB Collab. 2024 (ApJ 969, 145), *Updating the First CHIME/FRB Catalog with Baseband
167	  Data* — recomputes Catalog-1 fluences from **lower limits** to true values once the baseband
168	  position fixes the beam gain. Catalog-1 numbers are lower limits precisely because position
169	  uncertainty leaves `G` unknown.
170	- Michilli+ 2021 (ApJ 910, 147), baseband pipeline — flux cal at a **known** position against
171	  steady calibrators (Crab, Cas A). Co-detections have good positions, so this regime (not the
172	  real-time intensity one) applies.
173	
174	**DSA-110 (1.3–1.5 GHz) — templates:**
175	- Law+ 2024 (ApJ 967, 29), *DSA Science: First FRB and Host Galaxy Catalog* — DSA's catalog/
176	  flux-cal paper; SEFD, calibrators (3C286/3C48) + noise-diode scale, single-burst fluence.
177	  **Gap:** the standalone DSA-110 *system* paper (Ravi et al.) is still unpublished, so the
178	  SEFD/beam description lives in Law+2024 (+ Connor+ 2023, ApJ 949, L26) and the DSA-110 thesis —
179	  cite those, not an instrument paper.
180	
181	**Energetics — the field does NOT sum raw bands.** Standard band-limited isotropic energy
182	(Zhang 2018, ApJ 867, L21):
183	
184	```
185	E_iso = 4*pi*D_L(z)^2 / (1+z) * F_nu * d_nu          (flat-spectrum form; the 1/(1+z) is the
186	                                                       bandwidth k-correction)
187	```
188	
189	For a power law F ∝ nu^beta the k-correction generalizes to
190	`K = integral_rest nu^beta d_nu / integral_obs nu^beta d_nu` with nu_rest = (1+z) nu_obs.
191	Best practice for two bands is a **joint spectral fit on a common absolute (Jy) scale**, then one
192	integrated `E_iso` — *not* two independently-scaled per-band energies added together. FLITS
193	already does a joint fit; it just needs calibrated inputs. (z-from-DM via Macquart+ 2020,
194	Nature 581, 391, is not needed here — these sightlines have spectroscopic z.)
195	
196	**Two concrete errors this surfaces in the current `burst_energies.tex`:** (i) it applies **no
197	`(1+z)`** k-correction; (ii) it **sums** two uncalibrated bands (compounding the Q2 problem).
198

206	## Absolute-scale audit (2026-06-23) — DSA coherent-beam SEFD + estimator caveat
207	
208	After wiring the per-channel radiometer calibration (Phase 5), the first DSA fluences were
209	~100x too high (band-avg 218-6860 Jy*ms vs published tens of Jy*ms). Audited against Law et al.
210	2024 (DSA First FRB & Host Catalog, arXiv:2307.03344, Table 1), cross-matched by detection S/N:
211	
212	| burst | catalog FRB | Heimdall S/N | catalog fluence | first code | ratio |
213	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
214	| zach    | FRB 20220207C | 60.0 | 16.2 Jy*ms | 1680 | 104x |
215	| whitney | FRB 20220310F | 68.4 | 26.2 Jy*ms | 2728 | 104x |
216	| oran    | FRB 20220506D | 48.9 | 13.2 Jy*ms |  570 |  43x |
217	
218	**Two distinct errors found:**
219	
220	1. **Wrong SEFD (dominant, ~N_ant).** `sigma_S` used the dsa110-rt dashboard SEFD (~8016 Jy),
221	   which `estimate_sefd.py` computes **per baseline** (`compute_sefd_per_baseline`) — i.e. the
222	   ~per-**element** SEFD. The `cntr_bpc` arrays are the **coherent detection beam** (Law+2024:
223	   **48 antennas** combined), whose SEFD = SEFD_element / N_ant. Fix:
224	   `flux_cal.load_dsa_sefd_beam = load_dsa_sefd / DSA_N_ANT` (N_ant=48 -> ~167 Jy). This collapses
225	   the ~100x. The empirical matched-filter anchor is ~234 Jy (single value reproduces all three
226	   catalog fluences exactly via `F=(S/N)*SEFD*sqrt(W)/sqrt(n_pol*dnu)`), implying N_eff~34
227	   (~70% beamforming efficiency vs the nominal 48).
228	
229	2. **Estimator difference (residual ~1-3x, burst-dependent).** With the beam SEFD the fluences are
230	   physical (4.6-143 Jy*ms) but still differ from the catalog by a burst-dependent factor
231	   (oran 0.90x, whitney/zach ~2.2x). This is **not** a window/crop bug: oran and whitney are both
232	   compact (>=95% of flux within +-0.5 ms) yet differ 2.4x. The cause is that the per-channel
233	   **linear band integral** `int S dt dnu` (the true fluence) and the catalog **boxcar
234	   matched-filter** fluence are *different estimators*; for peaked/structured bursts they diverge
235	   by the burst structure factor. The shape/slope (gamma_D) result is scale-independent and
236	   unaffected; the absolute energy is not, so this estimator reconciliation is tracked before any
237	   E_iso ships. (TNS-suffix note: the local detection log lists ...207A/310A/506A; the catalog/TNS
238	   list ...207C/310F/506D — same bursts by S/N, local suffix likely wrong.)
239	
240	## Estimator choice — physics justification (linear integral over boxcar matched-filter)
241	
242	The residual ~1-3x (Section above) is a choice between two fluence estimators. The physics
243	selects the linear integral:
244	
245	1. **Fluence is conserved under scattering.** Scattering convolves the intrinsic profile with a
246	   unit-area exponential kernel (timescale tau): it redistributes flux in time but conserves
247	   `int S dt`. The physically meaningful fluence for E_iso (total radiated energy) is therefore the
248	   integral over the FULL scattered profile, tail included.
249	
250	2. **The boxcar matched-filter is biased low for scattered bursts.** The catalog fluence
251	   `F = (S/N) SEFD sqrt(W) / sqrt(n_pol dnu)` assumes a top-hat of the S/N-maximizing width W. For a
252	   scattered burst the S/N-optimal boxcar is narrower than the full scattered extent (adding tail
253	   past the e-folding grows noise faster than signal), so it misses tail flux. The bias goes as
254	   `W_box / W_eff < 1`, with `W_eff = int P dt / P_peak` the equivalent width.
255	
256	3. **The data show this signature.** The linear-vs-catalog ratio tracks burst structure: compact
257	   oran (95% of flux within +-0.5 ms) agrees (0.90x); tailed/structured zach and whitney sit ~2.2x
258	   high — the `W_eff/W_box > 1` pattern of a catalog that under-counts the tail.
259	
260	**Decision: the linear integral is the correct E_iso estimator** (conserved, tail-complete), made
261	robust by integrating the burst's significant extent (to the noise floor, off-pulse baseline
262	subtracted) rather than an arbitrary wide window (zach's far +-3 ms blob is noise/structure, not a
263	clean tail, and must be excluded). The robust realization is the **model-based fluence from the
264	calibrated scattering fit**: the fit gives the profile (intrinsic width (x) exp-tau tail) and the
265	calibrated amplitude c0(nu); integrating the MODEL includes the tail and excludes noise. This
266	unifies the estimator with the 5c-B re-fit — one calibrated fit yields both the relaxed gamma_D and
267	the tail-complete fluence. Report the catalog matched-filter value alongside, ratio = tail-fraction
268	diagnostic.
269	
270	## Rigorous calibrated re-fit of gamma_D (2026-06-23) — `refit_calibrated.py`
271	
272	The bandpass proxy (Section "bandpass diagnostic", `plot_bandpass_check.py`) only measured a log-log
273	slope and ignored noise weighting. This re-runs the **actual M2 MCMC** (c0, t0, gamma, tau_1ghz)
274	twice per railed burst with an identical setup — on the S/N data d(nu,t), and on the flux-calibrated
275	data d·sigma_S(nu) with per-channel noise sigma_S(nu) — so the beam-edge channels are down-weighted
276	self-consistently. The gamma prior floor is opened from the default -5 to **-10** so the calibration
277	shift is not clipped at the old rail. Figure `refit_calibrated.png` (figure-reviewed: match).
278	
279	**Analytic backbone (oracle).** For a power-law spectrum the noise-weighted fit satisfies
280	`gamma_cal = gamma_SN + slope(sigma_S)` exactly: multiplying the data by sigma_S tilts the spectrum
281	and the matching 1/sigma_S noise weighting leaves the channel weights unchanged, so the recovered
282	index shifts by precisely the beam slope. `slope(sigma_S) > 0` off-axis (sigma_S rises where G falls
283	toward the band edges) ⇒ calibrating makes gamma LESS negative; on-axis (flat sigma_S) it does not
284	move.
285	
286	**Results** (median, with the analytic prediction `slope_s` as cross-check):
287	
288	| burst | G(1.4GHz) | gamma_SN | gamma_cal | d_gamma (MCMC) | slope_s (analytic) |
289	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
290	| chromatica | 0.25 | -9.91 | -9.90 | +0.01 | +2.15 |
291	| oran | 0.67 | -8.49 | -7.84 | +0.65 | +0.62 |
292	| phineas | 1.00 | -9.91 | -9.95 | -0.04 | +0.00 |
293	| zach | 0.68 | -7.50 | -7.05 | +0.45 | +0.57 |
294	| freya | 0.20 | -6.04 | -3.81 | +2.23 | +2.56 |
295	
296	**Three findings:**
297	
298	1. **The -5 rail is a real single-band DSA preference, not a joint-coupling artifact.** With the
299	   floor opened, gamma_SN plunges to -6…-9.9 for every burst — the DSA band alone pushes hard against
300	   whatever floor is set. The joint fit's gamma_D ≈ -5 (blue marks) was literally the old prior floor.
301	
302	2. **The calibration mechanism is verified.** d_gamma(MCMC) matches slope(sigma_S) for the four
303	   bursts not pinned at the floor: oran 0.65 vs 0.62, zach 0.45 vs 0.57, freya 2.23 vs 2.56, phineas
304	   -0.04 vs 0.00. The relaxation is real and beam-correlated — largest for the lowest-G (most
305	   off-axis) bursts. freya (G=0.20) lifts -6.04 → **-3.81**, a physically plausible index.
306	
307	3. **Beam vs astrophysics splits by on/off-axis.** On-axis **phineas** (G≈1.0, slope_s≈0) does NOT
308	   relax (-9.91 → -9.95): its steepness is astrophysical or a non-beam instrumental effect, NOT
309	   band-edge. **chromatica** (G=0.25) is so steep it pins at the -10 floor even calibrated — a
310	   beam-dominated near-total edge dropout (its +2.15 shift stays clipped).
311	
312	**Implication for E_iso.** gamma_D as a free per-band index does not reliably recover an astrophysical
313	spectral index from the narrow (14%) DSA band — it is dominated by beam-edge sensitivity off-axis and
314	a residual steep falloff on-axis. So the energy estimate must NOT extrapolate the gamma_D power law;
315	the **calibrated per-channel fluence integral** (which integrates the measured channels directly) is
316	the robust estimator and is insensitive to the gamma rail. This reinforces the estimator decision
317	above.
318

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lift the joint-fit JSONs (scratch) into a committed trusted/untrusted summary.

Trust is a HUMAN verdict (4-lens adversarial workflow wf_417320dd, 2026-06-19),
NOT mechanically derived from log-evidence. The mechanical columns (railed,
unconstrained) are supporting evidence only. Output → repo results/joint_fit_summary.md.

ponytail: generator stays here (reads uncommitted scratch JSONs); only its
markdown output is committed. Run: python gen_joint_summary.py
"""

import glob
import json
from pathlib import Path

JOINT_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "joint_json"
OUT = Path(
    "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/dsa110/dsa110-FLITS/results/joint_fit_summary.md"
)

# Explicit human verdict — see flits-joint-fit-shallow-alpha memory.
TRUST = {
    "johndoeII": "trusted",
    "wilhelm": "trusted",
    "phineas": "trusted",
    "oran": "refuted",
}  # all others: unadjudicated
REASON = {
    "johndoeII": "4-lens adversarial verify; sub-Kolmogorov α survives α=4 rejection at Δ(−2lnL)≈2400",
    "wilhelm": "4-lens adversarial verify; tight, clean",
    "phineas": "4-lens adversarial verify; tight",
    "oran": "REFUTED — CHIME ζ_C unconstrained/railed; α is not a measurement",
    "chromatica": "α railed at upper bound (6.0) → not a measurement",
    "freya": "α railed at upper bound (6.0) → not a measurement",
    "hamilton": "α railed at upper bound (6.0) → not a measurement",
    "isha": "α unconstrained (σ ≈ 2.6) → not a measurement",
    "mahi": "α near upper rail (5.53), wide posterior → not a measurement",
    "whitney": "shallow α=1.46 but NOT adversarially verified; pending multicomponent refit",
    "zach": "tight α but anomalous lnZ (~−1.7e5); pending multicomponent refit",
}


def rows():
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(JOINT_DIR / "*_joint_fit.json"))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        b = d["burst"]
        a, t = d["alpha"], d["tau_1ghz"]
        lo, hi = d.get("alpha_bounds", [1.0, 6.0])
        railed = min(abs(a["median"] - lo), abs(a["median"] - hi)) < 0.05
        unconstrained = max(a["err_plus"], a["err_minus"]) > 0.5
        yield {
            "burst": b,
            "alpha": a["median"],
            "a_ep": a["err_plus"],
            "a_em": a["err_minus"],
            "tau": t["median"],
            "lnZ": d.get("log_evidence", float("nan")),
            "railed": railed,
            "unconstrained": unconstrained,
            "trust": TRUST.get(b, "unadjudicated"),
            "reason": REASON.get(b, ""),
        }


def main():
    rs = sorted(rows(), key=lambda r: {"trusted": 0, "unadjudicated": 1, "refuted": 2}[r["trust"]])
    trusted = [r for r in rs if r["trust"] == "trusted"]
    L = []
    L.append("# CHIME+DSA joint scattering-fit summary")
    L.append("")
    L.append(
        "Per-sightline shared (τ₁GHz, α) from the joint CHIME+DSA fit "
        "(`scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py`). Source results: "
        "`~/Developer/scratch/2026-06/flits-refit/joint_json/` (uncommitted)."
    )
    L.append("")
    L.append("## ⚠️ Trust: only 3 of 11 fits are trustworthy")
    L.append("")
    L.append(
        f"**Trusted (use): {', '.join(r['burst'] for r in trusted)}** — verified via a 4-lens "
        "adversarial workflow (wf_417320dd, 2026-06-19). Trusted α span **1.37→3.58** "
        "(johndoeII is genuinely sub-Kolmogorov)."
    )
    L.append("")
    L.append(
        "**Do NOT cite the other 8.** Trust is a human adversarial verdict, *not* derived from "
        "log-evidence. Most other sources rail α at the upper bound (6.0), are unconstrained, or "
        "are unadjudicated pending the multicomponent hidden-pulse refit. `oran` is explicitly "
        "refuted (CHIME nuisance railed). A tight error bar alone (e.g. whitney, zach) does NOT "
        "imply trust."
    )
    L.append("")
    L.append("| burst | trust | α | τ₁GHz (ms) | lnZ | railed | unconstrained | reason |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    badge = {"trusted": "✅ trusted", "refuted": "❌ refuted", "unadjudicated": "⏳ unadjudicated"}
    for r in rs:
        L.append(
            f"| {r['burst']} | {badge[r['trust']]} | "
            f"{r['alpha']:.2f} +{r['a_ep']:.2f}/−{r['a_em']:.2f} | {r['tau']:.4f} | "
            f"{r['lnZ']:.0f} | {'yes' if r['railed'] else '—'} | "
            f"{'yes' if r['unconstrained'] else '—'} | {r['reason']} |"
        )
    L.append("")
    L.append(
        "_Generated by `scratch/2026-06/flits-refit/gen_joint_summary.py` from the joint-fit "
        "JSONs. Regenerate after any refit._"
    )
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {OUT}  ({len(rs)} sources, {len(trusted)} trusted)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	# Implementation Plan: All-sky galaxy-cluster engine + r200-relative impact cut
2	
3	---
4	**Date:** 2026-06-23
5	**Author:** AI Assistant
6	**Status:** Draft
7	**Related Documents:**
8	- [Research: Foreground galaxy & galaxy-cluster distributions along the co-detected sightlines](research-foreground-galaxies-sightlines.md)
9	- [CHIME/DSA Co-detection Science Plan](../../codetection-science-plan.md)
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Overview
14	
15	The foreground-search pipeline (`galaxies/v2_0/`) currently detects galaxy
16	clusters **only** by NED object-type strings (`GClstr`/`GGroup`/`ClG`) and applies
17	a flat 5 Mpc impact cut. The research pass found this yields **zero clusters** on
18	all 12 sightlines, for two independent reasons: (1) at the sample's declination
19	(+70° to +74°) the SDSS-based cluster catalogs (WHL, redMaPPer) have no coverage —
20	only all-sky catalogs reach the band; (2) a fixed 5 Mpc cut is mass-blind, so it
21	mostly admits negligible-DM near-misses while a real DM contribution needs the
22	sightline within ~1–2 r200 of the cluster.
23	
24	This plan adds an **all-sky cluster-catalog engine** (Planck PSZ2 + MCXC +
25	MCXC-II, queried through Vizier) that supplies each cluster's redshift and M500
26	mass, replaces the flat 5 Mpc cut with a **mass-scaled r200-relative criterion**
27	(keep within 2·r200), turns an intersected cluster's ICM into a dispersion-measure
28	contribution with a **β-model electron-density profile** anchored to the catalog
29	mass, and integrates that cluster DM into the existing per-sightline budget. Per
30	the literature, clusters contribute DM but negligible scattering, so cluster τ is
31	set to zero.
32	
33	**Goal:** the production search finds the real foreground clusters along each
34	sightline (where any exist), assigns each a physically-scaled impact criterion,
35	and folds a defensible cluster ICM DM into `sightline_dm_scattering_budget`.
36	
37	**Motivation:** sightline attribution (CGM/groups/clusters of the intervening
38	systems) is a headline science goal; the current cluster path is both
39	under-powered (wrong catalogs for this sky) and aimed at a low-yield regime.
40	
41	## Current State Analysis
42	
43	**Existing Implementation:**
44	- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:9-17` — `DEFAULT_IMPACT_KPC=100`,
45	  `DEFAULT_CLUSTER_IMPACT_KPC=5000.0` (flat 5 Mpc), cone caps.
46	- `galaxies/v2_0/config.py:37-56` — `VIZIER_CATALOGS`, opt-in engine/enricher flags.
47	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:31-43` — `_CLUSTER_RE` + `_cluster_mask` (classification-string detection).
48	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:56-74` — `_foreground_mask`: per-row impact limit, cluster rows get the flat `cluster_impact_kpc`.
49	- `galaxies/v2_0/search.py:215-234` — engine list assembly + cone sizing from `max(impact_kpc, cluster_impact_kpc)`.
50	- `galaxies/v2_0/engines.py:23-102` — `NedEngine`, `VizierEngine` (standardize ra/dec/z + `catalog` tag).
51	- `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-221` — thin Vizier-wrapper engine pattern (`AllWiseEngine`, `XscEngine`).
52	- `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:27-123` — `dm_halo_mnfw` (mNFW hot-halo DM via `scipy.quad`; the style to mirror for the β-model).
53	- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:118-155` — `select_stellar_mass` ladder; `:266-277` — `m_halo = estimate_halo_mass(logm_best)` then `get_rvir_and_rs`.
54	- `galaxies/v2_0/build_unified.py:338-403` — per-galaxy cool-CGM/MgII/two-phase-τ derivation.
55	- `galaxies/v2_0/generate_galaxy_plots.py:65` — `get_rvir_and_rs(m,z)` returns R200 (= `(G·M/(100 H_z²))^{1/3}`).
56	- `galaxies/v2_0/sightline_budget.py:62-64` — `_MEASURED_MASS_SOURCES = MASS_PRIORITY[:-1]`; `:442-496` — budget loop reads `M_halo`, `dm_halo`, `pred_tau_scat_ms_1GHz` per foreground row.
57	- `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:33-50` — existing `_foreground_mask` cluster test (the pattern to extend).
58	
59	**Current Behavior:** clusters are found only if NED already classifies an object
60	within 5 Mpc as a cluster; if found, they flow through `build_unified` with **no
61	stellar mass → assumed 10¹⁰ M⊙ → galaxy-scale halo**, so even a found cluster would
62	get a wrong (tiny) DM. In practice none are found.
63	
64	**Current Limitations:**
65	- No all-sky cluster catalog; WHL cross-match exists only in notebooks.
66	- Mass-blind 5 Mpc impact cut.
67	- A cluster row, if present, gets stellar-mass-derived halo mass (wrong).
68	- Cluster DM uses galaxy-CGM cool/MgII/τ models, inappropriate for an ICM.
69	
70	## Desired End State
71	
72	**New Behavior:** a `ClusterEngine` queries PSZ2/MCXC/MCXC-II for each sightline,
73	returning clusters with `z` and `m500_msun`; the foreground filter keeps a cluster
74	when its impact ≤ `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR · r200(M200(M500), z)`; `build_unified`
75	injects the catalog M200 as the cluster's `M_halo`, computes its DM from a β-model
76	ICM profile anchored to M500/R500, sets cluster cool-DM and τ to zero, and the
77	budget reports cluster intervening DM with `measured` mass confidence.
78	
79	**Success Looks Like:**
80	- `conda run -n flits pytest galaxies/v2_0 -q` passes, including new
81	  cluster-model, engine, filter, and budget tests.
82	- A live smoke query resolves the three Vizier cluster-catalog IDs and returns
83	  rows with finite `z` and `m500_msun`.
84	- Re-running the search + budget produces a `sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md`
85	  whose cluster contributions (if any sightline intersects a catalogued cluster
86	  within 2·r200) appear with `intervening_mass_confidence = measured` and finite
87	  `dm_intervening`, with cluster `tau_intervening = 0`.
88	
89	## What We're NOT Doing
90	
91	- [ ] Not implementing a temperature-dependent Arnaud+2010 gNFW *pressure* profile
92	      with an X-ray temperature model — the isothermal β-model anchored to gas mass
93	      is the chosen ICM DM model (gNFW upgrade path noted in Risk Assessment).
94	- [ ] Not adding cluster *scattering* (τ) physics — clusters are set to τ=0 per
95	      Connor 2023 / Lee 2023 (clusters give DM, not scattering).
96	- [ ] Not wiring the notebook WHL cross-match into production (WHL has no Dec>+70
97	      coverage; superseded by the all-sky engine).
98	- [ ] Not changing the galaxy (non-cluster) search path, the 100 kpc galaxy impact
99	      cut, or the mNFW galaxy-CGM models.
100	- [ ] Not back-filling per-cluster member spectroscopy or richness-based masses
101	      beyond the catalog M500.
102	- [ ] Not committing regenerated large result CSVs as part of this plan (the
103	      branch carries unrelated flux-cal lanes; results regeneration is a verification
104	      step, commit policy decided separately).
105	
106	**Rationale:** keep the diff focused on the two requested capabilities; the
107	β-model is the minimal physically-correct ICM DM; cluster τ=0 is what the
108	literature supports.
109	
110	## Implementation Approach
111	
112	**Technical Strategy:** five phases, each test-first and network-free for unit
113	tests (live network only in explicit smoke steps). Phase 1 is pure physics (β-model
114	DM) with an analytic oracle. Phase 2 adds the catalog engine. Phase 3 swaps the
115	impact criterion and wires the engine on. Phase 4 integrates cluster mass+DM into
116	`build_unified`/budget. Phase 5 verifies end-to-end and regenerates artifacts.
117	
118	**Key Architectural Decisions:**
119	1. **Decision:** isothermal β-model ICM electron density, n_e(r)=n_e0·[1+(r/r_c)²]^(−3β/2), normalized so M_gas(<R500)=f_gas·M500.
120	   - **Rationale:** standard, analytically tractable cluster-gas DM model; closed-form Abel projection gives a test oracle; anchoring to gas mass uses the catalog M500 directly.
121	   - **Trade-offs:** isothermal/spherical; ignores cool cores and X-ray temperature structure.
122	   - **Alternatives considered:** Arnaud gNFW pressure profile (needs a temperature model; deferred); reusing the galaxy mNFW (under-models cluster ICM).
123	2. **Decision:** keep cluster within `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR=2.0` × r200, r200 from M200=1.3·M500.
124	   - **Rationale:** research shows meaningful DM within ~1–2 r200; the β-model DM is truncated at R200 so 2× is safely inclusive of near-r200 contributors while the column itself vanishes beyond truncation.
125	   - **Trade-offs:** a fixed M500→M200 factor (1.3) is order-of-magnitude; acceptable at these precisions.
126	3. **Decision:** cluster engine on by default (`ENABLE_CLUSTER_ENGINE=True`).
127	   - **Rationale:** finding clusters is the explicit goal; the current output finds zero, so adding cluster rows is the intended change.
128	   - **Trade-offs:** changes default search output (gated by a flag for reproducible reruns).
129	4. **Decision:** clusters bypass the stellar-mass ladder and the cool/MgII/τ phase.
130	   - **Rationale:** clusters have catalog halo mass (no stellar-mass step) and negligible scattering.
131	
132	**Patterns to Follow:**
133	- Vizier-wrapper engine — `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py:174-183` (`AllWiseEngine`).
134	- `scipy.quad` DM integral with truncation — `galaxies/v2_0/scattering_predict.py:104-123`.
135	- Network-free unit tests with injected DataFrames — `galaxies/v2_0/test_search_pipeline.py:14-50`.
136	- Pure-function oracle test (`--check`-style analytic comparison) — `galaxies/v2_0/test_scattering_predict.py`.

204	
205	  ```python
206	  from astropy import constants as const  # add to existing imports if absent
207	
208	  # --- Cluster ICM (isothermal beta-model) -------------------------------------
209	  # Mohr+1999 / Arnaud 2009: ICM beta ~ 0.6-0.7, core radius r_c ~ 0.1-0.2 R500.
210	  CLUSTER_BETA = 0.65
211	  CLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500 = 0.15
212	  # Vikhlinin+2006, Pratt+2009, Eckert+2019: hot-gas fraction within R500 ~ 0.13.
213	  CLUSTER_F_GAS_500 = 0.13
214	  # Fully ionized ICM mean molecular weight per electron.
215	  CLUSTER_MU_E = 1.17
216	  # R200/R500 ~ 1.54 for a typical cluster NFW concentration (c500 ~ 1.5).
217	  CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500 = 1.54
218	
219	  def r_delta_kpc(m_delta_msun: float, z: float, delta: float) -> float:
220	      """Spherical-overdensity radius R_Delta (kpc): M = (4/3)pi Delta rho_c(z) R^3."""
221	      if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m_delta_msun, z)) or float(m_delta_msun) <= 0.0:
222	          return float("nan")
223	      m = float(m_delta_msun) * u.Msun
224	      h_z = COSMO.H(float(z))
225	      # R_Delta = (2 G M / (Delta H^2))^(1/3); Delta=200 reduces to (G M/(100 H^2))^(1/3).
226	      r = ((2.0 * const.G * m) / (float(delta) * h_z ** 2)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)
227	      return float(r.to(u.kpc).value)
228	
229	  def _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, r_max_kpc):
230	      from scipy.integrate import quad
231	      integrand = lambda r: r * r * (1.0 + (r / rc_kpc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)
232	      val, _ = quad(integrand, 0.0, r_max_kpc, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-7, limit=200)
233	      return 4.0 * math.pi * val  # kpc^3 (shape-only; n_e0 factored out)
234	
235	  def _beta_ne0_cm3(m500_msun, z, r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, f_gas=CLUSTER_F_GAS_500):
236	      """Central electron density (cm^-3) so M_gas(<R500)=f_gas*M500 for the beta shape."""
237	      shape_int_kpc3 = _beta_mass_integral_kpc3(r500_kpc, beta, rc_kpc, r500_kpc)
238	      if shape_int_kpc3 <= 0.0:
239	          return float("nan")
240	      m_gas_g = f_gas * float(m500_msun) * u.Msun.to(u.g)
241	      mu_e_mp_g = CLUSTER_MU_E * 1.67262192369e-24
242	      kpc3_to_cm3 = (1.0 * u.kpc ** 3).to(u.cm ** 3).value
243	      # M_gas = mu_e m_p n_e0 * (shape integral in cm^3)
244	      return m_gas_g / (mu_e_mp_g * shape_int_kpc3 * kpc3_to_cm3)
245	
246	  def dm_cluster_beta_model(
247	      m500_msun, z, impact_kpc, r500_kpc=None,
248	      beta=CLUSTER_BETA, rc_over_r500=CLUSTER_RC_OVER_R500,
249	      f_gas=CLUSTER_F_GAS_500, r_trunc_factor=CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500,
250	  ):
251	      """Observer-frame ICM DM (pc cm^-3) through a beta-model cluster at impact b."""
252	      if any(_is_bad(x) for x in (m500_msun, z, impact_kpc)) or float(m500_msun) <= 0.0:
253	          return 0.0
254	      if r500_kpc is None or _is_bad(r500_kpc):
255	          r500_kpc = r_delta_kpc(m500_msun, z, 500)
256	      if _is_bad(r500_kpc) or r500_kpc <= 0.0:
257	          return 0.0
258	      rc = rc_over_r500 * r500_kpc
259	      r_trunc = r_trunc_factor * r500_kpc
260	      b = float(impact_kpc)
261	      if b >= r_trunc:
262	          return 0.0
263	      ne0 = _beta_ne0_cm3(m500_msun, z, r500_kpc, beta, rc, f_gas=f_gas)
264	      if _is_bad(ne0):
265	          return 0.0
266	      from scipy.integrate import quad
267	      l_half = math.sqrt(max(r_trunc ** 2 - b ** 2, 0.0))
268	      def los(l_kpc):
269	          r = math.hypot(b, l_kpc)
270	          return ne0 * (1.0 + (r / rc) ** 2) ** (-1.5 * beta)
271	      col_kpc_cm3, _ = quad(los, -l_half, l_half, epsabs=0.0, epsrel=1e-6, limit=200)
272	      dm_obs = col_kpc_cm3 * 1000.0 / (1.0 + float(z))  # 1 kpc path = 1000 pc
273	      return float(max(dm_obs, 0.0))
274	  ```

352	  and the engine in `galaxies/v2_0/engines_extra.py` (append):
353	
354	  ```python
355	  from .engines import BaseEngine, VizierEngine  # already imported at top
356	
357	  # Per-catalog column maps: (ra, dec, z, m500_1e14, r500_mpc_or_None).
358	  _CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS = {
359	      "J/A+A/594/A27/psz2": ("RAdeg", "DEdeg", "z", "MSZ", None),
360	      "J/A+A/534/A109/mcxc": ("RAJ2000", "DEJ2000", "z", "M500", "R500"),
361	      "J/A+A/682/A124/mcxc2": ("RAJ2000", "DEJ2000", "z", "M500", "R500"),
362	  }
363	
364	  def _standardize_cluster_columns(df, catalog_id):
365	      cols = _CLUSTER_COLUMN_MAPS.get(catalog_id)
366	      out = df.copy()
367	      if cols is None:
368	          out["classification"] = "cluster"
369	          out["catalog"] = catalog_id
370	          return out
371	      ra_c, dec_c, z_c, m_c, r_c = cols
372	      rename = {}
373	      lower = {c.lower(): c for c in out.columns}
374	      if ra_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[ra_c.lower()]] = "ra"
375	      if dec_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[dec_c.lower()]] = "dec"
376	      if z_c.lower() in lower: rename[lower[z_c.lower()]] = "z"
377	      out = out.rename(columns=rename)
378	      m500 = pd.to_numeric(out.get(m_c), errors="coerce") if m_c in out.columns else np.nan
379	      out["m500_msun"] = m500 * 1.0e14
380	      if r_c is not None and r_c in out.columns:
381	          out["r500_kpc"] = pd.to_numeric(out[r_c], errors="coerce") * 1000.0  # Mpc -> kpc
382	      else:
383	          out["r500_kpc"] = np.nan
384	      out["classification"] = "cluster"
385	      out["catalog"] = catalog_id
386	      return out
387	
388	  class ClusterEngine(BaseEngine):
389	      """All-sky galaxy-cluster engine (PSZ2 + MCXC + MCXC-II via Vizier)."""
390	      def __init__(self, catalogs=None):
391	          from .config import CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS
392	          self.catalogs = dict(catalogs if catalogs is not None else CLUSTER_VIZIER_CATALOGS)
393	
394	      def query(self, coord, radius):
395	          frames = []
396	          for cat_id in self.catalogs.values():
397	              raw = VizierEngine(cat_id).query(coord, radius)
398	              if raw.empty:
399	                  continue
400	              std = _standardize_cluster_columns(raw, cat_id)
401	              keep = [c for c in ("ra", "dec", "z", "m500_msun", "r500_kpc",
402	                                  "classification", "catalog") if c in std.columns]
403	              frames.append(std[keep])
404	          if not frames:
405	              return pd.DataFrame()
406	          return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
407	  ```
408	
409	  Note: `VizierEngine.__init__` uses `row_limit=-1` and standardizes RA/Dec only
410	  for known names; cluster RA/Dec/mass columns are standardized here instead, so
411	  `_standardize_cluster_columns` operates on the raw Vizier frame — pass the raw
412	  catalog through `VizierEngine` but re-map from the original column names. (If
413	  `VizierEngine` has already renamed `z`-like columns, the lower-case lookup still
414	  finds `ra`/`dec`; mass columns `MSZ`/`M500` are untouched by `VizierEngine`.)

483	  def _cluster_impact_limit_kpc(df, impact_kpc, r200_factor=CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR,
484	                                fallback_kpc=DEFAULT_CLUSTER_IMPACT_KPC):
485	      """Per-row impact limit: galaxies->impact_kpc; clusters->r200_factor*r200,
486	      or fallback_kpc when a cluster row carries no catalog mass."""
487	      limit = pd.Series(float(impact_kpc), index=df.index, dtype="float64")
488	      is_cluster = _cluster_mask(df)
489	      m500 = pd.to_numeric(df.get("m500_msun"), errors="coerce") if "m500_msun" in df.columns \
490	          else pd.Series(math.nan, index=df.index)
491	      z = pd.to_numeric(df["z"], errors="coerce")
492	      for i in df.index[is_cluster]:
493	          mi, zi = m500.get(i, math.nan), z.get(i, math.nan)
494	          if pd.notna(mi) and mi > 0.0 and pd.notna(zi) and zi > 0.0:
495	              r200 = scat.r_delta_kpc(CLUSTER_M500_TO_M200 * float(mi), float(zi), 200)
496	              limit.at[i] = r200_factor * r200 if math.isfinite(r200) else fallback_kpc
497	          else:
498	              limit.at[i] = fallback_kpc
499	      return limit
500	  ```
501	
502	  Then in `_foreground_mask`, replace the two lines that set the cluster impact
503	  limit (`galaxies/v2_0/search.py:71-74`) with:
504	
505	  ```python
506	      impact_limit = _cluster_impact_limit_kpc(df, impact_kpc, fallback_kpc=cluster_impact_kpc)
507	      return foreground & (impact <= impact_limit)
508	  ```

725	## Risk Assessment
726	
727	1. **Risk:** MCXC-II Vizier ID wrong/unverifiable offline.
728	   - **Likelihood:** Medium · **Impact:** Low
729	   - **Mitigation:** Phase 2 step 1 resolves it via `Vizier.find_catalogs`; engine degrades to empty per-catalog, so a wrong ID drops one catalog without breaking the others; live smoke surfaces it.
730	2. **Risk:** β-model isothermal/spherical under/over-estimates cluster DM vs a real ICM.
731	   - **Likelihood:** Medium · **Impact:** Medium
732	   - **Mitigation:** anchored to measured M500 + f_gas; constants are exposed knobs; gNFW pressure-profile upgrade is a documented follow-up (out of scope here).
733	3. **Risk:** PSZ2 mass `MSZ` column name or unit differs from assumption.
734	   - **Likelihood:** Low · **Impact:** Low
735	   - **Mitigation:** `_standardize_cluster_columns` is unit-tested; live smoke prints `m500_msun` for sanity.
736	
737	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
738	
739	**Edge Cases:**
740	1. **Cluster with no catalog mass (NED-Type only):** falls back to the 5000 kpc cut and the existing galaxy mass path — handled in `_cluster_impact_limit_kpc` and the `is_cluster = m500 finite` guard.
741	2. **PSZ2 cluster without a redshift (unconfirmed):** `z` NaN → dropped by the existing `dropna(subset=["ra","dec","z"])` in `run_search` (`search.py:265`).
742	3. **Sightline at impact > 2·r200 of every cluster:** zero cluster rows kept — legitimate; budget shows no cluster term.
743	4. **Impact beyond R200 truncation:** `dm_cluster_beta_model` returns 0.0.
744	
745	**Error Scenarios:**
746	1. **Vizier query failure / bad catalog ID:** `VizierEngine.query` catches and returns empty; `ClusterEngine` skips that catalog.
747	2. **Non-finite mass/redshift:** `_is_bad` guards in the physics functions return 0.0/NaN, not exceptions.

15	mass-scaled r200-relative criterion (keep within `CLUSTER_R200_FACTOR · r200`),
16	modelled an intersected cluster's ICM dispersion measure with an isothermal
17	β-model anchored to the catalog M500, and wired catalog cluster rows through
18	`build_unified` and the per-sightline DM/scattering budget with `measured` mass
19	confidence and zero scattering (clusters give DM, not τ).

61	- **Deviation 3:** β-model oracle test compares the truncated LOS integral to the
62	  untruncated analytic Abel projection by calling `dm_cluster_beta_model` with
63	  `r_trunc_factor=1000` (effectively untruncated), with a separate test for the
64	  truncation-to-zero behaviour.
65	  - **Reason:** the plan's 2% tolerance against the analytic form would fail at
66	    the real R200 truncation (~7% column loss near b≈0); isolating quadrature
67	    accuracy from the physical truncation keeps the oracle exact (<1%).
68	  - **Impact:** stronger test — exact analytic agreement plus an explicit
69	    truncation invariant.

237	- **NED engine replaced.** `astroquery.ipac.ned` uses the deprecated legacy

242	    engine, but NED's async result host (`rc.ned.ipac.caltech.edu`) is
243	    unreachable, so the engine uses *synchronous* TAP with a cone cap
244	    (`FLITS_NED_TAP_MAX_DEG`, default 0.5°; sync caps near 60s — 0.3°~9s,
245	    0.5°~27s, 0.7°~39s, ≥1° fails). The cap is >10× the foreground-galaxy
246	    footprint (100 kpc impact ≤ ~0.05° at the sample's lowest z) and clusters
247	    come from `ClusterEngine`, so no galaxy of interest is dropped.
248	- **Full 12-sightline regen** ran end-to-end (exit 0, ~48 min) into
249	  `scratch/cluster-regen-out/` (not tracked `results/`). NED yield: 193 rows
250	  across 7 sightlines; DESI 29 rows. Budget md/csv/png regenerated (12 rows).
251	- **Cluster yield: 0 within 2·r200 on all 12 sightlines.** Raw in-cone
252	  candidates (Whitney 2, Phineas 7, Casey 1) were all correctly excluded.
253	  Oracle-verified on Phineas: 7 foreground clusters, impact 10.2–430 Mpc ≫
254	  2·r200 (2.3–2.9 Mpc). A legitimate null at Dec +70…+74 given catalog depth.
255	- **Figure reviewed:** budget PNG matches the md table; no cluster bars (zero

257	## Data-integrity follow-up (post-regen, 2026-06-23)
258	
259	The first regen exposed two catalog-data-loss bugs, which were root-caused, fixed
260	(commit `12a929e`), and re-run before promotion:
261	
262	1. **GLADE+ silently dropped (systematic).** Vizier renamed the table
263	   `VII/291/glade` → `VII/291/gladep`; the stale id returned 0 tables (no error),
264	   dropping every GLADE+ galaxy. The new table also changed schema: redshift as
265	   `zcmb`/`zhelio` (no literal `z`), stellar mass `M*` in 1e10 M☉ linear (the old
266	   `M_star` was log10). Fixed the id, map `zcmb`→`z`, convert `M*` → log10(M/M☉).
267	   Live-verified: 293 rows / 247 with z restored at zach; flows again (isha 2,
268	   phineas 1).
269	2. **Transient CDS Vizier timeouts** (observed: PS1 `Read timed out`) silently
270	   degraded a catalog to empty. Added `_retry` (exponential backoff) around the
271	   live `VizierEngine` and PS1 `query_region` calls.
272	3. **NED non-galaxy contamination (severe).** `NEDTAP.objdir` is a mixed catalog;
273	   once `NedTapEngine` actually returned data, its stars (`prefphytype='*'`, junk
274	   z~1e-4) and the FRB transient self-entry (untyped, z=z_FRB) passed the bare
275	   `z<z_FRB` foreground cut — designed for the galaxy-only GLADE+/DESI catalogs —
276	   and were counted as foreground galaxies, inflating the intervening DM. Casey:
277	   130 of 146 candidates were stars; intervening DM_raw ~5247 → 572 pc/cm³ after
278	   the fix. `_standardize_ned_tap` now keeps only extragalactic galaxy types
279	   (`_is_extragalactic_ned_type`: NED galaxy/group/cluster/pair/triple codes start
280	   with `G` minus `GammaS`; plus QSO/AGN). Live-verified per sightline: Casey
281	   148→18, Phineas 56→17 galaxies; Oran/Mahi → 0 (their only entries were stars /
282	   the FRB self-entry). Commit `8b864e3`.
283	
284	**Superseded galaxies (not recoverable, not a bug).** 7 old foreground galaxies
285	across 5 sightlines (zach 2, wilhelm 2, freya/hamilton/johndoeii 1 ea) were
286	present in older catalog versions (old `VII/291/glade`, old `VII/292/north`) but
287	are gone from the current versions and have **no counterpart with a redshift in
288	any current catalog** (gladep, current DESI North, NED-with-z, SDSS DR12, 2MASS,
289	LS-DR10). Several carry artifact signatures (repeated exact z=0.767/0.46, rough
290	15% photo-z errors). They are preserved in git history. (chromatica's 2 old GLADE
291	rows are background, z=0.0764 > z_frb=0.074 — correctly excluded.)
292	
293	- **Re-run + test suite:** `pytest galaxies/v2_0 -q` → **113 passed** (adds the NED
294	  star-filter test, two photo-z mask tests, and `test_plotting.py`). The 3
295	  data-coupled tests (`test_glade_unified_columns_and_mass`,
296	  `test_unified_mass_sources_ps1_and_assumed`, `test_glade_mass_source_is_catalog…`)
297	  were decoupled from the live `results/` snapshot into frozen inline fixtures
298	  (commit `1bf078a`) so they no longer break on regen.
299	- **Promoted to `results/`** (user-approved): current-catalog run replaces tracked
300	  data; 5 superseded sightline files removed (recoverable via git history). Net
301	  per-sightline foreground (≤100 kpc): 6 GAIN, 5 superseded-loss, 1 same. Commit
302	  `867ecd5`.
303	- **Re-promoted star-free** (user-approved, post-fix #3): full 12-sightline regen
304	  with the NED type filter. Foreground galaxies now Casey 18, Phineas 17, Whitney
305	  11, Isha 2; the other 8 sightlines have zero (mahi/oran/zach `_galaxies.csv`
306	  removed). Budget + prior-predictive sensitivity regenerated (Casey now robust
307	  `likely_negative_host`; Zach `likely_positive_host`). Commits `0cc8a90`,
308	  sensitivity regen.
309	
310	4. **DESI photo-z contamination (fix #4).** The star-free per-sightline figures
311	   exposed a second contamination class in the foreground sets, both from DESI
312	   `VII/292/north` photo-z: (a) **floor noise** — sources pinned at z=0.001-0.008
313	   (unreliable Legacy photo-z near z~0); (b) **background leakage** — z>z_FRB
314	   galaxies (e.g. z=0.965 behind a z=0.27 FRB) passing the 2σ foreground cut
315	   because their `e_zphot` is absurd (σ_z = 0.4-1.7). `_foreground_mask` now
316	   splits spec-z vs photo-z: spec-z (NED, GLADE+) keep `z<z_limit` with no floor
317	   (UGC 06371 z=0.009 survives); photo-z rows must clear `FOREGROUND_PHOTOZ_FLOOR`
318	   (0.01) and pass 2σ with `e_zphot` capped at `MAX_PHOTOZ_Z_ERR` (0.05). The new
319	   mask is a strict subset of the old, so the promoted snapshot was re-filtered
320	   (equivalent to a requery on the same catalog snapshot) rather than re-queried.
321	   Foreground galaxies: Casey 18→6, Phineas 17→10, Whitney 11→5, Isha 2. Budget
322	   improves: Casey host residual −380→−44 pc/cm³, Phineas −246→−174, Whitney
323	   −310→−251. Commits `e753bb6` (code), `4238f22` (data).
324	
325	- **Per-sightline galaxy+cluster figures (new standard).** `plot_sightline`
326	  (`galaxies/v2_0/plotting.py`) now renders foreground galaxies (z-coloured
327	  circles) AND galaxy clusters (crimson diamonds; dashed R200 ring when a catalog
328	  M500 exists, else unsized — NED `GClstr` carry no mass) on one on-sky angular
329	  map. `python -m galaxies.v2_0.plotting` writes `results/{name}_sky.png` for all
330	  12 (4 populated: casey/phineas/whitney/isha; clusters are NED NSC/WHL/ABELL at
331	  2-5 Mpc impact; 0 massed PSZ2/MCXC survive the cone). Commit `2ad704b`.

A produced plot is never \"validated\" until it has been looked at.\n\n## Deferred tasks gate completion (will block you)\n\nA session shall not be completed while deferred tasks remain that the agent can execute or implement itself. Loose ends are tracked in `.agents/deferred-tasks.md` — a markdown checklist where every open `- [ ]` item carries exactly one tag:\n\n- `@agent` — the agent can do it now → **blocks** end-of-turn until it is finished (`- [x]`).\n- `@human` — needs a person or a one-way door (push / PR / publish) → does not block.\n- `@decision` — a pending product/science choice → does not block.\n- `@separate-lane` — belongs to another task's git lane → does not block.\n\n`.claude/settings.json` registers a `Stop` hook (`.claude/hooks/deferred-task-gate.sh`) that blocks while any unchecked `@agent` item exists. To clear: **finish the work** and check it off, or — only if it genuinely cannot be done by the agent now — retag it `@human` / `@decision` / `@separate-lane`. Do not retag agent-doable work just to pass the gate; that defeats the policy. Add new follow-ups to the ledger as they arise, tagged honestly.\n\n## Protected-branch commit guard (will block the commit)\n\n`.claude/settings.json` registers a `PreToolUse` Bash hook (`.claude/hooks/no-commit-to-protected-branch.sh`) that **refuses `git commit` while `HEAD` is `main`/`master`**. Branch hygiene was otherwise prose-only, and `origin/main` already carries direct non-PR commits. To proceed: branch first (`git switch -c <feature-branch>`), then commit. The guard fails open when it cannot prove the branch is protected (not a repo, detached HEAD) and only sees the agent's own commits — an external auto-committer is a separate path.\n\n## Agent skills"
}

# CHIME+DSA joint scattering-fit summary

Per-sightline shared (τ₁GHz, α) from the joint CHIME+DSA fit (`scattering/scat_analysis/burstfit_joint.py`). Source results: `analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_json/` (committed).

## ⚠️ Trust: only 3 of 11 fits are trustworthy

**Trusted (use): johndoeII, phineas, wilhelm** — verified via a 4-lens adversarial workflow (wf_417320dd, 2026-06-19). Trusted α span **1.37→3.58** (johndoeII is genuinely sub-Kolmogorov).

**Do NOT cite the other 8.** Trust is a human adversarial verdict, *not* derived from log-evidence. Most other sources rail α at the upper bound (6.0), are unconstrained, or are unadjudicated pending the multicomponent hidden-pulse refit. `oran` is explicitly refuted (CHIME nuisance railed). A tight error bar alone (e.g. whitney, zach) does NOT imply trust.

## Verdict: APPROVE (with two important false-positive findings worth a follow-up; neither defeats the gate's security purpose)

The two gates are functionally correct on their core contract: the deferred-task hook blocks iff an unchecked `@agent` item exists and never blocks on `- [x]`/non-`@agent`/prose-without-checkbox; the commit guard refuses real `git commit` on main/master and fails open on detached-HEAD / non-repo / missing-python3 / malformed-JSON exactly as documented. settings.json is valid JSON, existing hooks preserved, exec bits set.

The bugs I found are all in the commit guard's substring matcher. Critically, they are **fail-safe in the security direction** — the false positives only fire *when you are genuinely on a protected branch* (line 24 still proves the branch), so the worst case is "a harmless non-commit command gets blocked while you're on main," which is annoying but not a security hole. The false negatives let a commit through, but that is the same outcome as the documented fail-open and the hook is explicitly scoped as a nudge, not a hard security boundary ("a guard must never wedge unrelated Bash calls").

### Findings

**[important] `.claude/hooks/no-commit-to-protected-branch.sh:20` — false negatives: real commits slip past the matcher.**
The pattern `*"git commit"*` requires the literal adjacent substring `git` SPACE `commit`. These real commits on `main` were **allowed (exit 0)** in my tests:
- `git -C /some/path commit -m x` — no adjacent `git commit` substring. (Reproduced: exit 0 on a main-branch repo.)
- `git\tcommit -m x` (tab), `git  commit` (two spaces), `git\ncommit` (newline) — all exit 0.
- Aliases (`gc -m x`) — exit 0 (genuinely unseeable; acceptable).

The `git -C … commit` miss is the notable one: it's a common, legitimate invocation form an agent would emit. Fix is one line — match the token sequence instead of the literal substring, e.g. `case "$cmd" in *"git "*"commit"*)` is still loose; cleaner is a regex anchoring `git` … `commit` as words: `[[ "$cmd" =~ (^|[^[:alnum:]])git([[:space:]]|[[:space:]]-[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]])+commit($|[^[:alnum:]-]) ]]`. Given the hook is a nudge and fails open by design, leaving it is defensible, but `git -C` is worth catching.

**[important] `.claude/hooks/no-commit-to-protected-branch.sh:20` — false positives on non-commit commands.**
Because the gate is pure substring, these were **blocked (exit 2) while on main**:
- `git commit-graph write` (a real, distinct subcommand)
- `git log --grep="git commit"`, `echo git commit`, `ls # git commit later`, and any heredoc containing `git commit` on its own line.

`git commit-graph` is the one that can actually bite a user on main. The comment at lines 16–18 acknowledges the substring choice as intentional ("ponytail"), and the blast radius is bounded to protected branches, so this is a usability nit elevated to important only because `commit-graph` is a legitimate command. Word-boundary matching (above) fixes both findings at once.

**[nit] `.claude/hooks/deferred-task-gate.sh:18` — `.*@agent` over-matches `@agentic` (and any `@agent…` superstring).**
An unchecked line tagged `@human` but whose text contains `@agentic` (or `@agentlike`, etc.) will block. Reproduced: `- [ ] use the @agentic framework @human` → blocked. Low-probability in practice; tighten with a trailing boundary if desired: `@agent([^[:alnum:]-]|$)`.

**[nit] `.claude/hooks/deferred-task-gate.sh:18` — section-agnostic; an unchecked `- [ ] … @agent` placed under `## Done` still blocks.**
By design unchecked-anywhere blocks (correct — a forgotten checkbox *should* block). Just noting it's not scoped to `## Open`; the contract doesn't require scoping, so this is informational, not a defect.

### Confirmed correct (no action)
- Fail-open: detached HEAD (exit 0), non-repo (exit 0), missing python3 (exit 0), empty/non-JSON/`{"foo":1}`/`command:null` stdin (exit 0). All verified.
- Deferred gate: `- [x]` and `- [X]` never block; `@human` never blocks; `@agent` in prose without a checkbox never blocks; multiple open items all listed; python3-missing emits the static fallback block JSON (valid). All verified.
- settings.json is valid JSON; Stop array order is figure-review → deferred-task → entire (existing two preserved, deferred inserted between); PreToolUse merged as a separate `Bash` matcher block alongside the existing `Task` block (correct — Claude Code runs all matching matcher blocks, so this is the right merge, not an overwrite).
- No shell-injection in the registered commands: both use `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/..."` with the path quoted; the `$REASON` heredoc is passed to python as `sys.argv[1]` (not interpolated into shell), and JSON-escaped by `json.dumps`, so a malicious ledger line cannot break out of the JSON or inject shell.

## Code Review: `joint-fit-provenance` PR

### Summary
A clean, well-scoped provenance fix: it relocates the joint-fit summary's source-of-truth from an uncommitted scratch path (`~/Developer/scratch/2026-06/flits-refit/`) to committed in-repo paths, adds a deterministic in-repo generator, and adds a drift-guard test. Every load-bearing claim in the PR holds up under independent adversarial testing.

### Strengths
- **The reproducibility claim is true.** I independently ran the generator from a clean checkout; `git diff --exit-code results/joint_fit_summary.md` returned 0 (byte-identical). The committed summary table is exactly what `render()` produces.
- **The drift test is real, not a tautology.** `tests/test_joint_summary_reproducible.py:21` reads the committed `.md` from disk (`SUMMARY.read_text()`) and compares to a *fresh* `gen.render()`. I proved it bites by mutating a sandbox copy of `wilhelm_joint_fit.json` (`alpha.median → 9.99`) — the test FAILED, as it should. It would catch any JSON value change or generator change that wasn't re-rendered.
- **No hidden path coupling.** The test computes `SUMMARY` from its own `parents[1]` and `render()` computes nothing about the output path — `render()` is pure and never touches `OUT`/`main()`. The test does not depend on the generator's write path being correct (only `render()` is exercised). I confirmed test-`SUMMARY` and generator-`OUT` independently resolve to the same file.
- **The c0 claim is exact.** All 11 `joint_json/*.percentiles.c0_C.median` (rounded to 3 dp) and `c0_D` match the `CALIBRATION_REVIEW.md:48-53` table with zero mismatches. 11 JSONs, 11 table rows, no missing/extra bursts.
- **Deterministic output.** `render()==render()` across calls; float formatting (`:.2f/:.4f/:.0f`) is locale-independent in Python f-strings (verified under `de_DE.UTF-8`); ordering is a stable Timsort (trust-rank primary, alphabetical-filename secondary) — reproducible across machines.
- **All 11 bursts covered**; every `TRUST`/`REASON` key maps to a real JSON burst (no orphan keys); every JSON burst has a `REASON`. The `railed`/`unconstrained` derivations match the rendered table and are sensible (e.g. chromatica/freya/hamilton α≈6.0 → railed; isha/oran wide → unconstrained).

### Issues

- **[NIT]** `gen_joint_summary.py:79` — the header count `"## ⚠️ Trust: only 3 of 11 fits are trustworthy"` is a hardcoded literal, while the trusted list two lines below (`:82`) and the "Do NOT cite the other 8" prose (`:88`) are partly computed/manual. If `TRUST` is ever edited, the computed trusted list updates but `"3 of 11"` and `"other 8"` silently drift. The drift *test* would still pass (it only compares committed-md to render output, and render emits the same stale string), so this inconsistency would not be caught. Low risk since trust verdicts change rarely and a human edits this block, but deriving the count (`len(trusted)`/`len(rs)`) would close the gap.

- **[NIT]** `gen_joint_summary.py:46` — `json.load(open(f))` leaks the file handle (no context manager / unclosed `open`). Harmless at 11 small files; trips `ResourceWarning` under `-W error`. Same pattern would be flagged by ruff `SIM115` if enabled.

- **[NIT]** `gen_joint_summary.py:50,68` — `railed`/`unconstrained` thresholds (`0.05`, `0.5`) and the trust-rank map are inline magic numbers. Fine for a one-off provenance script; noting only because the railed flag feeds a "not a measurement" scientific verdict.

Nothing here rises to blocking. Missing required keys hard-fail with `KeyError` (loud, not silent) — appropriate for a generator over committed inputs.

### Questions
None blocking. (Optional: the hardcoded `t/zach` lnZ `~−1.7e5` etc. in `REASON` strings are human prose, not asserted against JSON — by design, since trust is a stated human verdict.)

### Separate lane (not part of this PR, preserved untouched)
The worktree carries a pre-existing modification `M docs/entire-tracing-checkpoints.md` unrelated to these 4 files. I did not touch it. The 4 reviewed files are clean vs index after my verification runs (the generator reproduced the summary byte-identically, so no restore was needed). Worktree is merge-clean for this PR's scope.

### VERDICT: APPROVE
All four falsifiable claims (byte-identical reproduction, real drift test, exact c0 match, deterministic/complete generator) were independently verified and held. Findings are nits only.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# PreToolUse(Bash) guard: refuse `git commit` while HEAD is a protected branch
3	# (main/master). Branch hygiene is otherwise prose-only here, and origin/main
4	# already carries direct non-PR commits (a2333b5, eed6f04, ...). The agent should
5	# branch first, then commit.
6	#
7	# Fails OPEN whenever it cannot prove the branch is protected (not a git repo,
8	# detached HEAD, git missing) -- a guard must never wedge unrelated Bash calls.
9	# Scope: only the agent's own `git commit` calls in a Claude session; an external
10	# auto-committer is a separate path this hook cannot see.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	payload="$(cat)"
14	cmd="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("tool_input",{}).get("command",""))' 2>/dev/null || true)"
15	
16	# Only real commits matter. Substring match is intentional (ponytail): the branch
17	# check below is the actual gate, so a stray "git commit" in some other command is
18	# harmless unless we are genuinely on a protected branch.
19	case "$cmd" in
20	  *"git commit"*) ;;
21	  *) exit 0 ;;
22	esac
23	
24	branch="$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
25	[ -z "$branch" ] && exit 0  # detached HEAD / not a repo -> fail open
26	
27	case "$branch" in
28	  main | master)
29	    printf 'refuse: commit on protected branch "%s". Branch first (git switch -c <feature-branch>), then commit.\n' "$branch" >&2
30	    exit 2
31	    ;;
32	esac
33	exit 0
34

==== how does main produce/consume _joint_gate.json? (gate_joint_committed.py purpose) ====
"""Gate the committed joint CHIME-DSA scattering fits against the runtime 3-level
FLITS fit-quality contract, reusing the authoritative classify_fit_quality.

Reads joint_json/{burst}_joint_fit.json + the paired {burst}_joint_ppc.json,
applies Level-1 physical bounds + prior-rail detection, Level-2 reduced-chi2
(classify_fit_quality, worst of the two bands), and Level-3 alpha-physics, then
writes joint_gate_verdicts.{csv,md} and a per-burst {burst}_joint_gate.json
(mirroring the *_fit_results.json field shape). These are standalone verdict
artifacts -- the fit-verify workflow globs *_fit_results.json, so it does NOT
auto-discover these *_joint_gate.json files. tau x dnu (Level-3) is not evaluable
here -- no per-sightline scintillation bandwidth -- so it is reported N/A.

Level-1 here is the physical-bounds + prior-rail subset of the contract; the
optimizer-convergence / Jacobian-conditioning Level-1 gates do not map to these
nested-sampling fits (no Jacobian; convergence is proxied by log_evidence_err).
"""

import csv
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))  # repo root
from scattering.scat_analysis.burstfit import classify_fit_quality  # noqa: E402

ALPHA_MIN, ALPHA_MAX = 1.5, 6.0  # Level-1 physical gate (strict)
TAU_MIN, TAU_MAX = 1e-4, 100.0  # ms
RAIL_EDGE = 0.1  # alpha within this of a prior bound => prior-railed (unconstrained)
KOLM_LO, KOLM_HI = 3.5, 4.5  # Level-3 PASS-consistent alpha window (Kolmogorov ref 4.0)
_RANK = {"FAIL": 2, "MARGINAL": 1, "PASS": 0}


def _worst(*flags):
    return max(flags, key=lambda f: _RANK[f])


def gate_one(burst, fit, ppc):
    """Classify one joint fit. ppc may be None (chi2 unknown -> Level-2 MARGINAL)."""
    alpha = fit["alpha"]["median"]
    tau = fit["tau_1ghz"]["median"]

+# Eckert+2019 A&A 621,A40 (X-COP) / Vikhlinin+2006: the hot-gas mass fraction
+# within R500 spans ~0.10-0.13 and is lower at the smaller radii where most of the

-CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500 = 1.54

+# config.CLUSTER_M500_TO_M200 = 1.3 (typical c500 ~ 1.5). The earlier 1.54 assumed a
+# different concentration and was inconsistent with the 1.3 mass ratio used for R200.
+CLUSTER_R200_OVER_R500 = 1.48

# Velocity-offset window (km/s) below which a spec-z neighbour is host/local
# ambiguous, not a clean foreground. dv = c*(z_frb - z_gal)/(1 + z_frb); a galaxy
# inside this window sits at the host's recession velocity (group member / host
# peculiar velocity ~200-500 km/s) and cannot be cleanly attributed as an
# intervening system. Set at the upper edge of typical group dispersions.
FOREGROUND_AMBIGUITY_KMS = 500.0
SPEED_OF_LIGHT_KMS = 299792.458
# Spec-z catalogs: redshift is spectroscopic / distance-derived, so any z_err they
# carry (e.g. GLADE+'s generic 0.015 floor) is NOT a per-object photo-z and must

def main():
    base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
    results_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "results")
    configs_dir = os.path.join(base_dir, "scattering", "configs", "bursts", "chime")
    bursts_dir = os.path.join(results_dir, "bursts")

    df = build_all_budgets(
        results_dir=results_dir, configs_dir=configs_dir, bursts_dir=bursts_dir, enrich=False
    )

    # Emit TNS designations (not internal nicknames) in the CSV, table, and figure (#26).
    from scattering.scat_analysis.burst_metadata import load_tns_name

    df["name"] = [load_tns_name(n) for n in df["name"]]

    csv_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.csv")
    df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
    print(f"Wrote {csv_path}")

    md_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.md")
    with open(md_path, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("# FRB sightline DM & scattering budgets\n\n")
        fh.write(format_budget_table(df))
        fh.write("\n")
    print(f"Wrote {md_path}")

    fig = make_budget_figure(df)
    png_path = os.path.join(results_dir, "sightline_dm_scattering_budget.png")
    fig.savefig(png_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"Wrote {png_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
